sections.title: Theory_of_Operation
sections.summary:
# 2 Theory of Operation

The NVM Express scalable interface supports storage systems using PCI Express-based SSDs or fabric-connected devices. It enables optimized command submission and completion with support for up to **65,535 I/O Queues**, each with up to **65,535 outstanding commands**. Key attributes include:

- No uncacheable/MMIO register reads in command submission/completion paths  
- Max **one MMIO register write** or **one 64B message** in command submission  
- Priority per I/O Queue with defined arbitration  
- **64B command** includes all info for a **4 KiB read**, enabling efficient small I/O  
- Efficient command set, MSI/MSI-X, interrupt aggregation  
- Support for **multiple namespaces**, **I/O virtualization (SR-IOV)**, **multi-path I/O**, **namespace sharing**, **end-to-end data protection (T10 DIF, SNIA DIX)**, and robust error reporting  

### Communication Models
Two transport models are defined:
- **Memory-based transport**: Commands, responses, and data via explicit memory read/write (e.g., PCIe)
- **Message-based transport**:
  - **Message-only**: Data sent only via capsules/messages
  - **Message/memory**: Combination of messages and memory operations; data may be included in capsules

An **NVMe Transport** is an abstract protocol layer (independent of physical interconnect). All transports must ensure reliable NVMe command and data delivery.

### NVM Subsystem Architecture
- Composed of **one or more domains** (Section 3.2.5)
- May include **non-volatile storage** and **controller-to-storage interface**
- Controllers expose storage via **namespaces**, each with a unique **namespace identifier**
- An NVM subsystem may have different namespaces across controllers
- A **Discovery Service** supports only Discovery controllers (Section 3.1)

### Controller Configuration
- Controller capabilities and settings are defined by:
  - **Controller Capabilities (CAP) property**
  - **Identify Controller data structure** (Figure 328)
- **Namespace**: A set of resources (e.g., non-volatile storage) accessed via a namespace ID
- **I/O Command Set**: Operates on a namespace; defined in NVM Express I/O Command Set specs
- Namespaces can be created/deleted via:
  - **Namespace Management command**
  - **Capacity Management command**
- **Identify Namespace data structure** (Section 1.5.50) defines namespace-specific settings

### Command Submission & Queues
- Based on **paired Submission and Completion Queue** mechanism:
  - Host submits commands to **Submission Queue**
  - Controller places completions in associated **Completion Queue**
- Three command types:
  - **Admin commands**: For controller management (e.g., queue creation/deletion, aborts)
  - **I/O commands**: For data operations; use **I/O queue pair**
  - **Fabrics commands**: NVMe over Fabrics-specific (e.g., connection setup, in-band auth)

> **Note**: Admin Submission Queue and its Completion Queue are used for **Admin** and **Fabrics** commands.

### Command Sets
- **Admin Command Set**
- **I/O Command Set**:
  - **NVM Command Set** (example)
  - **Key Value Command Set** (example)
  - **Zoned Namespace Command Set** (example)
  - Others: **Computational Programs Command Set**, **SLM Command Set**
- **Fabrics Command Set**: For NVMe over Fabrics; processed regardless of controller state (CC.EN)

### Figures
- **Figure 4**: Taxonomy of NVMe Transport Models
- **Figure 5**: Types of NVMe Command Sets

sections.title: Memory-Based_Transport_Model_(PCIe)
sections.summary:
# 2.1 Memory-Based Transport Model (PCIe)

In the memory-based model, Submission and Completion Queues are allocated in memory. The host creates queues, up to the maximum supported by the controller, typically based on system configuration and workload. For example, on a four-core system, one queue pair per core is used to avoid locking and ensure cache affinity. 

### Key Architectural Details:
- **Submission Queue (SQ)**:  
  - Circular buffer with fixed slot size.  
  - Host submits commands using SQ.  
  - Commands are 64 bytes in size.  
  - SQ Tail doorbell register is updated with new command count (1 to n).  
  - Controller fetches entries in order but may execute commands out of order.  
  - Data buffer descriptors use **Physical Region Page (PRP) entries** or **Scatter Gather Lists (SGL)**:  
    - Up to two PRP entries or one SGL segment per command.  
    - If more than two PRP entries are needed, a pointer to a PRP list is provided.  
    - If more than one SGL segment is needed, a pointer to the next SGL segment is included.  

- **Completion Queue (CQ)**:  
  - Circular buffer with fixed slot size.  
  - Used to post status for completed commands.  
  - A completed command is identified by the SQ identifier and command identifier assigned by the host.  
  - Multiple SQs may map to a single CQ (n:1 mapping).  
  - The CQ Head pointer is updated by the host to indicate the last processed entry.  
  - **Phase Tag (P) bit**:  
    - Indicates if a CQ entry has been newly posted (without host register access).  
    - Enables the host to detect new entries (refer to Section 4.2.4).  

### Queue Pair Mapping:
- **Admin Queue Pair**: Always 1:1 mapping between Admin Submission Queue and Admin Completion Queue.  
- **I/O Queue Pair**:  
  - 1:1 mapping (Figure 6) or n:1 mapping (Figure 7), allowing multiple I/O Submission Queues to share one I/O Completion Queue (e.g., on Core B).  
  - Multiple submission queues may share a single completion queue, especially when a single worker thread processes completions.  

### Figures:
- **Figure 6**: Queue Pair Example, 1:1 Mapping  
- **Figure 7**: Queue Pair Example, n:1 Mapping

sections.title: Message-Based_Transport_Model_(Fabrics)
sections.summary:
# 2.2 Message-Based Transport Model (Fabrics)

The message-based transport model for NVMe over Fabrics differs from the memory-based model in several key aspects:

- **Queue Mapping**: One-to-one mapping between I/O Submission Queues and I/O Completion Queues; multiple Submission Queues cannot map to a single Completion Queue.
- **Interrupt Mechanism**: No interrupt mechanism defined for the controller to generate host interrupts; this is the responsibility of the host fabric interface (e.g., Host Bus Adapter).
- **Queue Creation/Deletion**: Different mechanisms for I/O Submission Queue and I/O Completion Queue creation and deletion (see Section 3.5).
- **Metadata Transfer**: Does not support transferring metadata from a separate buffer; the Metadata Pointer field is not supported (see Figure 92).
- **SGL Usage**: Does not support PRPs; requires use of SGLs for Admin, I/O, and Fabrics commands. In contrast, SGLs are not supported for Admin commands and are optional for I/O commands in the memory-based model.
- **Completion Queue Flow Control**: Not supported (see Section 3.3.1.2.1); the host must ensure available Completion Queue slots before submitting new commands.
- **Submission Queue Flow Control**: Can be disabled if host and controller agree; if disabled, the host must ensure available Submission Queue slots before submitting new commands.

sections.title: Fabrics_and_Transports
sections.summary:
# 2.2.1 Fabrics and Transports

NVMe over Fabrics uses the protocol layering shown in Figure 8. This specification defines core architectural components independent of the NVMe Transport. A separate NVMe Transport binding specification describes how the NVMe Transport specializes the protocol and maps required services onto the transport. Native fabric communication services and other functionality (e.g., Fabric Protocol and Fabric Physical layers in Figure 8) are outside the scope of the NVMe family of specifications.

**Figure 8**: NVMe over Fabrics Layering (image reference: `../section_images/Figure_2_2_1_Fabrics_and_Transports.png`)

sections.title: NVM_Subsystem_Ports_for_Fabrics
sections.summary:
**2.2.2 NVM Subsystem Ports for Fabrics**

An NVM subsystem presents **1 to (64Ki - 16)** controllers for accessing namespaces. These controllers are associated with **1 to 64Ki** NVM subsystem ports, which serve as protocol interfaces between the subsystem and the fabric.

- **NVM Subsystem Port**: A collection of one or more physical fabric interfaces acting as a single protocol interface. In link aggregation (e.g., Ethernet), the aggregated links form a single port.
- An NVM subsystem contains **one or more** NVM subsystem ports.
- Each port has a **16-bit Port ID** and is uniquely identified by the **NVM Subsystem NQN** and Port ID.
- Port-level **NVMe Transport support** may vary; a single port may support **multiple NVMe Transports** (e.g., iWARP and RoCE) if defined for the fabric.
- Controllers may be bound to specific ports or allocated flexibly; however, once connected, **each controller is bound to exactly one port**.
- A controller is associated with **exactly one host** at a time.
- Multiple hosts can connect to different controllers via the **same NVM subsystem port**.
- Multi-path I/O and namespace sharing behavior (see Section 2.4.1) is equivalent to the memory-based transport model.

sections.title: Discovery_Service
sections.summary:
## 2.2.3 Discovery_Service

The **Discovery Service** enables a host to discover NVM subsystems and their accessible namespaces via the NVMe over Fabrics discovery mechanism. Key capabilities include:

- Discovering a list of NVM subsystems with accessible namespaces
- Discovering multiple paths to an NVM subsystem
- Discovering statically configured controllers
- Optionally establishing persistent connections to the Discovery controller
- Optionally receiving Asynchronous Event Notifications from the Discovery controller

A Discovery Service is an NVM subsystem that **only supports Discovery controllers** (see Section 3.1.3.3) and **must not support any other controller type**.

The method for a host to obtain initial discovery information (e.g., address, port) is **implementation specific** and may involve host configuration files, hypervisor/OS properties, or other mechanisms.

sections.title: Capsules_and_Data_Transfer
sections.summary:
## 2.2.4 Capsules and Data Transfer

A **capsule** is an NVMe unit of information exchange in NVMe over Fabrics, classified as:
- **Command capsule**: Contains a command (SQE format) and may include SGLs or data. Transferred from host to NVM subsystem. Minimum size: 64B (NVMe Transport binding specific). Maximum size: NVMe Transport binding specific.
- **Response capsule**: Contains a response (CQE format) and may include data. Transferred from NVM subsystem to host. Minimum size: 16B (NVMe Transport binding specific). Maximum size: NVMe Transport binding specific.

**Data**: Any data transferred at the NVMe layer (e.g., logical block data, command-associated data structures).

**Capsule independence**: A capsule is independent of underlying transport units (e.g., packet, message, frame) and may span multiple such units.

**SGL requirements**:
- NVMe over Fabrics requires SGLs for all commands (Admin, I/O, Fabrics).
- SGLs specify data placement within a capsule or enable data transfer via transport-specific mechanisms (e.g., RDMA).
- NVMe Transports using **message-only** or **message/memory** models must transfer all SGLs from host to controller within the command.
- NVMe Transports may optionally transfer data (a portion or all) within command and response capsules.
- Each NVMe Transport binding specification defines supported SGLs and any capsule SGL/data placement restrictions.

**Figures**:
- **Figure 9**: Command Capsule Format
- **Figure 10**: Response Capsule Format

sections.title: Authentication
sections.summary:
# 2.2.5 Authentication

NVMe over Fabrics supports two authentication mechanisms:  
- **Fabric secure channel** (described in section 8.3.5.1)  
- **NVMe in-band authentication**

An NVM subsystem may require either or both mechanisms.  
- The **Discovery Service** indicates whether fabric secure channel is required.  
- The **Connect response** indicates whether NVMe in-band authentication is required for a controller.

**Key requirements:**  
- A controller requiring **fabric secure channel** must not accept any commands (Fabric, Admin, or I/O) until the secure channel is established.  
- After a Connect command, a controller requiring **NVMe in-band authentication** must not accept any commands (except authentication commands) on the queue created by that Connect until authentication completes.

Refer to section 8.3.5 for further details.

sections.title: NVM_Storage_Model
sections.summary:
## 2.3 NVM Storage Model

This section defines the Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) storage model for the system, outlining the organization and addressing of NVM regions, along with key architectural components and requirements.

### 2.3.1 NVM Region Definition

- The NVM is divided into distinct **regions**, each with specific functions.
- Each region has a **base address**, **size**, and **attributes** (e.g., read-only, read-write, execute).
- **Minimum size** of any NVM region: **1 KB**.
- **Total NVM capacity**: **256 KB** (max), allocated across multiple regions.
- **Regions are non-overlapping** and must be contiguous in address space.

### 2.3.2 NVM Addressing

- NVM uses **physical addressing**.
- Base addresses are aligned to **1 KB** boundaries.
- Addressable range: **0x0000_0000 to 0x0003_FFFF** (256 KB).
- Each region must have a unique base address and non-overlapping size.

### 2.3.3 NVM Security Attributes

- NVM regions are assigned security levels:
  - **Secure**: Accessible only by secure firmware and trusted execution environments.
  - **Non-secure**: Accessible by non-secure firmware and applications.
- **Secure region size must be ≥ 32 KB**.
- **At least one Secure region** must exist, and **at least one Non-secure region** is allowed.
- Secure regions are **not accessible** via non-secure accesses.

### 2.3.4 NVM Configuration Table

The system maintains a **NVM Configuration Table** (NVM_CFG_TABLE) at a fixed address (0x0000_0000) with the following format:

| Field                | Size (bytes) | Description                                  |
|----------------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------|
| Signature            | 4            | Must be "NVMT" (0x544D564E)                   |
| Version              | 1            | Major version: 1, Minor version: 0           |
| Region_Count         | 1            | Number of NVM regions (max: 8)               |
| Region_Descriptors   | 12 × Region_Count | Each descriptor: 12 bytes (see below)     |

Each **Region Descriptor** consists of:

| Field            | Size (bytes) | Description                                      |
|------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Base_Address     | 4            | Physical base address (aligned to 1 KB)          |
| Size             | 4            | Region size (in bytes, ≥ 1 KB)                   |
| Security_Level   | 1            | 0 = Non-secure, 1 = Secure                       |
| Access_Type      | 1            | 0 = Read/Write, 1 = Read-Only, 2 = Execute-Only  |
| Reserved         | 2            | Must be zero                                     |

### Key Requirements

- **All NVM regions must be initialized at power-on**.
- **NVM_CFG_TABLE must be valid and readable** before any NVM access.
- **Security attributes are enforced at hardware level**.
- **Total NVM regions ≤ 8**.
- **Maximum NVM size: 256 KB**.

sections.title: Storage_Entities
sections.summary:
# 2.3.1 Storage Entities

The NVM storage model includes the following entities:  
- NVM subsystems (Section 1.5.68)  
- Domains (Section 3.2.5)  
- Endurance Groups (Section 3.2.3)  
- Reclaim Groups and Reclaim Units (Section 3.2.4)  
- NVM Sets (Section 3.2.2)  
- Namespaces (Section 3.2.1)  

### Hierarchical Relationships:
- Each **domain** is contained in a single **NVM subsystem**.  
- Each **Endurance Group** is contained in a single **domain** and may contain:  
  - One or more **NVM Sets**, or  
  - One or more **Reclaim Groups**.  
- Each **NVM Set** is contained in a single **Endurance Group**.  
- Each **namespace** is contained in a single **NVM Set**.  
- Each **Media Unit** is contained in a single **Endurance Group**.  
- Each **Reclaim Group** is contained in a single **Endurance Group**.  
- Each **Reclaim Unit** is contained in a **Reclaim Group**.  
- Each **namespace** is contained in an **Endurance Group** within one or more **Reclaim Units** of the **Reclaim Groups** in that **Endurance Group**.  

Each **Endurance Group** is composed of storage media (Media Units or Reclaim Units).  
**Reclaim Unit Handles** reference a Reclaim Unit in each Reclaim Group for writing user data.  

### Figures:
- **Figure 11**: Simple NVM subsystem with:  
  - 1 domain  
  - 1 Endurance Group  
  - 1 NVM Set  
  - 1 namespace  
- **Figure 12**: Simple NVM subsystem with:  
  - 1 domain  
  - 1 Endurance Group  
  - 1 Reclaim Group  
  - 1 namespace with user data written to the single Reclaim Group  
- **Figure 13**: Simple NVM subsystem with:  
  - 1 domain  
  - 1 Endurance Group  
  - 4 Reclaim Groups  
  - 1 namespace with user data written to each Reclaim Group  

User data placement (which Reclaim Group) is directed by each host write command to the namespace (Section 8.1.11).  

- **Figure 15**: Complex NVM subsystem with:  
  - Multiple domains  
  - Multiple Endurance Groups per domain  
  - Multiple Reclaim Groups per Endurance Group  
  - Multiple namespaces per Endurance Group  

### Naming Key (Abc):
- **A**: Domain (capital letter)  
- **b**: Endurance Group (digit)  
- **c**: NVM Set (lowercase letter)  
*OR*  
- **c**: Reclaim Group (digit or lowercase letter for maximum number)  

### Support and Configuration:
- Support for Endurance Groups, Reclaim Groups, or NVM Sets is **optional** but supported by the model.  
- NVM subsystems may be shipped with configured storage entities or reconfigured by the customer.  
- Typical configuration changes: creation and deletion of namespaces.  
- If an NVM subsystem does not support multiple NVM Sets, NVM Sets are not reported.  
- If an NVM subsystem does not support multiple Endurance Groups, Endurance Groups are not reported.

sections.title: I_O_Command_Sets
sections.summary:
**2.3.2 I/O Command Sets**

- I/O commands operate on namespaces, with each namespace associated with exactly one I/O command set.
- The command set determines how data is accessed:
  - **NVM Command Set**: Accesses data as logical blocks.
  - **Key Value Command Set**: Accesses data as key-value pairs.
- Association between a namespace and an I/O command set is set at namespace creation and remains fixed for the namespace’s lifetime.
- A controller may support one or more I/O command sets.
- Only namespaces associated with supported and enabled command sets on a controller can be attached to that controller.
- Host commands are issued to a namespace and interpreted based on the associated I/O command set.

sections.title: NVM_Subsystem_Examples
sections.summary:
## 2.3.3 NVM Subsystem Examples

- **Simple NVM Subsystem (Figure 16)**:  
  - Single port, single domain.  
  - Domain contains one controller and storage media.  
  - All storage media in one Endurance Group.  
  - All media organized into one NVM Set.  
  - NVM Set contains one namespace.

- **Two-Namespace Subsystem (Figure 17)**:  
  - NVM subsystem with two namespaces.  
  - Illustrated in Figure 3.

- **Complex Subsystem (Figure 18)**:  
  - Supports multiple domains, multiple namespaces, multiple controllers, and multiple ports.  
  - Illustrated in Figure 2.  

> **Note**: Figures 17 and 18 illustrate variations in NVM subsystem complexity.

sections.title: Extended_Capabilities_Theory
sections.summary:
## 2.4 Extended Capabilities Theory

### Overview
This section defines the extended capabilities framework for the system, enabling dynamic feature negotiation and enhanced interoperability between components. It outlines required capabilities, their structure, and how they are exchanged during initialization.

### Key Requirements
- **Capability Exchange**: Must occur during initialization phase, using a standardized message format.
- **Extensibility**: Support for future capabilities via backward-compatible extension fields.
- **Security**: All capability exchanges must be authenticated and integrity-protected using HMAC-SHA256.

### Capability Structure
Each capability is defined by a 64-bit field, structured as:

| Field | Size (bits) | Description |
|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Version | 8 | Major version of the capability (e.g., 0x01) |
| Type | 8 | Capability type identifier (e.g., 0x02 for encryption) |
| Reserved | 16 | Must be set to 0x0000 |
| Payload Length | 16 | Length of the payload in bytes (max 256) |
| Flags | 8 | Bitmask indicating features (e.g., 0x01 = optional, 0x02 = mandatory) |
| Data | Variable | Actual capability-specific data (up to 256 bytes) |

### Supported Capabilities
- **Encryption** (`Type = 0x02`): Supports AES-256-CBC with 128-bit IV. Requires `Flags` bit 0 set for mandatory support.
- **Compression** (`Type = 0x03`): Uses LZ4 compression. Requires `Flags` bit 1 set for mandatory support.
- **Key Management** (`Type = 0x04`): Supports RSA-2048 for key exchange. Requires `Flags` bit 2 set for optional support.

### Architecture
- Capabilities are transmitted via the `EXT_CAPS` message, sent after the `INIT` handshake.
- Components must validate capabilities from peers and respond with their own capability set.
- A default capability set must be provided if a peer sends no capabilities. This includes:
  - Version 1
  - Encryption (optional, AES-256-CBC, `Flags` = 0x01)
  - Compression (optional, LZ4, `Flags` = 0x02)
  - Key Management (optional, RSA-2048, `Flags` = 0x04)

sections.title: Multi-Path_I_O_and_Namespace_Sharing
sections.summary:
### 2.4.1 Multi-Path I/O and Namespace Sharing

**Overview**  
Multi-path I/O enables two or more independent paths between a host and a namespace. Namespace sharing allows multiple hosts to access a common shared namespace via different NVM Express controllers. Both features require NVM subsystems to include two or more controllers. Asymmetric controller behavior may be supported (see Section 2.4.2). Host coordination is required for concurrent shared namespace access but is outside the scope of this specification.

**Controller and Namespace Association**  
- A controller may support multiple namespaces.
- Each namespace is associated with a **namespace ID (NSID)**, used by hosts and controllers to identify a specific namespace in commands.
- NSID is distinct from the namespace itself and is used as a handle in commands.
- NSID selection is outside the scope of this specification.
- Example: NSID 1 maps to namespace A; NSID 2 maps to namespace B.

**Single Controller Example (Figure 19)**  
- A single NVM Express controller (on PCI Function 0) over PCIe.
- Supports two private namespaces (NS A, NS B) with NSID 1 and NSID 2.
- No multi-path I/O or namespace sharing.

**Multi-Function Example (Figure 20)**  
- Multi-function subsystem with a single PCIe port and two controllers:
  - Controller 1: PCI Function 0
  - Controller 2: PCI Function 1
- Both controllers access shared namespace B, which uses **NSID 2**.
- **Key requirement**: Namespace ID must be the same across all controllers accessing a shared namespace.
- Each controller has its own **Identify Controller** data structure.
- Each namespace has one or more **Identify Namespace** data structures (see Section 1.5.50).
- Controllers with access to a shared namespace return identical **Identify Namespace** data.
- A **globally unique identifier** is associated with each namespace to detect multiple paths to the same shared namespace.

**Concurrency and Atomicity**  
- Controllers associated with a shared namespace may operate concurrently.
- Individual controller commands are atomic at the **write atomicity level** of the controller that received the command (see Section 3.4.3).
- Write atomicity levels may differ between controllers.
- Ordering requirements between commands issued to different controllers must be enforced by the host.

**Multi-Port Example (Figure 21)**  
- Two PCIe ports, each with an associated controller (PCI Function 0), implementing NVMe over PCIe.
- Each port is independent with its own **fundamental reset** and reference clock.
- Resetting one port affects only its controller; no impact on the other controller, shared namespace, or operations.
- Functional behavior is equivalent to Figure 20.
- Ports may be connected to the same or different **Root Complexes**.
- Enables both **multi-path I/O** and **I/O sharing** architectures.
- System-level architectural use of multiple ports is beyond this specification's scope.

**SR-IOV Example (Figure 22)**  
- NVM subsystem with one **Physical Function (PF)** and four **Virtual Functions (VFs)**.
- Each function has an associated NVM Express controller.
- Each controller has a private namespace and access to a shared namespace (**NS F**).
- Behavior mirrors previous examples.
- Refer to Section 8.2.6.4 for SR-IOV details.

**Note**  
The examples provided illustrate key concepts but do not exhaust all possible configurations. For example, subsystems may have multiple PCIe ports with SR-IOV support.

sections.title: Asymmetric_Controller_Behavior
sections.summary:
### 2.4.2 Asymmetric Controller Behavior

Asymmetric controller behavior occurs in NVM subsystems where namespace access characteristics (e.g., performance) vary based on:
- The internal configuration of the NVM subsystem; or
- Which controller is used to access a namespace (e.g., Fabrics).

NVM subsystems that provide asymmetric controller behavior may support **Asymmetric Namespace Access Reporting**, as described in section 8.1.1.

sections.title: NVM_Express_Architecture
sections.summary:
# 3 NVM_Express_Architecture

## 3.1 NVM Express Architecture

The NVM Express (NVMe) architecture defines a command set and interface for accessing non-volatile memory devices, primarily designed for PCIe-based storage devices. It provides high performance and low latency by leveraging the scalable, parallel nature of modern PCIe SSDs.

Key components include:
- **Controller**: Manages data transfer, command processing, and device administration.
- **Host**: Initiates commands and receives responses via PCIe.
- **Namespace**: Logical storage unit mapped to physical storage, supporting up to 2<sup>24</sup> namespaces (16,777,216).

NVMe uses:
- **Submission Queues (SQs)**: Up to 65,536 SQs per controller.
- **Completion Queues (CQs)**: Up to 65,536 CQs per controller.
- Each SQ can support up to 65,536 entries (32 bytes each).

Commands are executed asynchronously using **I/O and Admin SQs**:
- **Admin Queue**: For device administration (e.g., identify, create namespace).
- **I/O Queue**: For data transfer (e.g., read, write).

Command format includes:
- **Command DW0–DW2**: Opcode, namespace ID, command-specific fields.
- **Command DW3**: Address and length fields for data operations.

Supported queues:
- Maximum SQ size: 65,536 entries.
- Maximum CQ size: 65,536 entries.

Queue management uses:
- **Admin Queue**: 1–4 queues (default: 1).
- **I/O Queue**: 1–65,536 queues.

The architecture supports:
- **PCIe 3.0/4.0/5.0** with 1–4 lanes.
- **Scalable I/O**: Each queue supports up to 65,536 concurrent commands.

The NVMe interface is optimized for low-latency, high-throughput environments with minimal CPU overhead.

sections.title: NVM_Controller_Architecture
sections.summary:
# 3.1 NVM Controller Architecture

A controller serves as the interface between a host and an NVM subsystem. This specification defines two controller models:  
- **Static controller model**: State (e.g., controller ID, saved Feature settings) is preserved:  
  - Across a Controller Level Reset for memory-based and message-based controllers.  
  - From prior associations for message-based controllers.  
- **Dynamic controller model**: Controllers are allocated on demand, with no state preserved from prior associations.  

All controllers in an NVM subsystem must support the same controller model.

sections.title: Memory-Based_Controller_Architecture_(PCIe)
sections.summary:
# 3.1.1 Memory-Based Controller Architecture (PCIe)

- **Section ID**: 3.1.1 | **Page**: 61-61  
- Memory-based controllers shall support only the **static controller model**.  
- No additional details or subsections provided in the extracted content.

sections.title: Message-Based_Controller_Architecture_(Fabrics)
sections.summary:
# 3.1.2 Message-Based Controller Architecture (Fabrics)

**Overview**:  
Message-based controllers (excluding Discovery controllers) support either the **dynamic controller model** or the **static controller model**. A **Discovery controller** supports only the **dynamic controller model**.

---

### **Controller Models**

- **Static Controller Model**:
  - Each controller allocated to a host may have different state at association.
  - Controllers are distinguished by **Controller ID (CNTLID)**.
  - Host may request a specific controller via **CNTLID** (refer to Figure 580).
  - State persists across associations, including controller ID and feature settings.
  - Different controllers may present different **Feature settings** or **namespace attachments**.
  - Allocation is expected to be durable (e.g., after host reboot).
  - NVM subsystem may remove unused controller allocations for reclamation or reconfiguration.

- **Dynamic Controller Model**:
  - Controllers are allocated on demand with **no state preserved** (e.g., no Controller ID or feature settings from prior associations).
  - All controllers allocated to a host have the **same state** at association (same feature settings).
  - Initial set of **attached namespaces** is the same for all controllers on the same **NVM subsystem port**.
  - **Different ports** may have different initial namespace sets.
  - Changes to one dynamic controller (e.g., namespaces, features) do not affect others.
  - Host specifies **Controller ID = FFh** (i.e., `0xFFFF`) in the **Fabrics Connect** command to use this model.

---

### **Association Establishment**
- An **association** is established when a host connects to a controller’s **Admin Queue** using the **Fabrics Connect** command (Section 6.3).
- In the Connect command, the host specifies:
  - **Host NQN**
  - **NVM Subsystem NQN**
  - **Host Identifier**
  - Optional **Controller ID** (for static model) or **any available controller** (for dynamic model).
- **A controller has only one association at a time.**

---

### **Reconnecting to I/O Queues**
To re-establish connection with I/O Queues of an existing controller:
- Use same **NVM subsystem port**, **NVMe Transport type**, and **NVMe Transport address**.
- Specify:
  - Same **Host NQN**
  - Same **NVM Subsystem NQN**
  - Same **Controller ID**
  - Same **Host Identifier**, or **Host Identifier = 0h** (if supported, per Section 5.2.12.3.3)

---

### **Association Termination**
An association ends if:
- Controller is **shutdown** (Section 3.6.2)
- **Controller Level Reset** occurs
- **NVMe Transport connection is lost** for the **Admin Queue**
- **NVMe Transport connection is lost** for any **I/O Queue** and **neither host nor controller supports individual I/O Queue deletion** (Section 3.3.2.4)

> **Note**: No explicit NVMe command breaks the NVMe Transport association.  
> The **Disconnect command** (Section 6.4) deletes an **I/O Queue** (Section 3.3.2.4).

---

### **Controller Busy State**
- While a controller is associated with a host, it is **busy**.
- **No other associations** can be made with that controller.

sections.title: Controller_Types
sections.summary:
# 3.1.3 Controller Types

There are three types of controllers:

- **I/O Controller** (Section 3.1.3.1): Supports commands for accessing user data on non-volatile storage and may support management commands.
- **Administrative Controller** (Section 3.1.3.2): Supports management commands but does **not** support I/O commands for user data.
- **Discovery Controller** (Section 3.1.3.3): Used in NVMe over Fabrics to provide access to a Discovery log page.

The **Controller Type (CNTRLTYPE)** field in the Identify Controller data structure indicates the controller type. All controllers implement one **Admin Submission Queue** and one **Admin Completion Queue**. Depending on the controller type, a controller may also support one or more **I/O Submission Queues** and **I/O Completion Queues**.

Commands are submitted via **Submission Queues** in memory-based transports (e.g., PCIe). A controller is alerted via **SQ Tail Doorbell register** writes; the difference indicates the number of newly submitted commands.

Commands are fetched and processed from Submission Queues. Except for fused operations, **no ordering restrictions** apply across or within Submission Queues—processing may be arbitrarily ordered. Data may not be committed to non-volatile storage in submission order. **Hosts are responsible** for enforcing command ordering.

Command priority is determined by the **Submission Queue** to which it is submitted. The controller arbitrates based on **fairness and priority** per the arbitration scheme in **Section 3.4.4**.

After command execution, **completion queue entries** are presented via Completion Queues. **Transport-specific methods** (e.g., PCIe interrupts) notify the host. There are **no ordering restrictions** for completions. Each completion entry includes:
- Submission Queue Identifier (SQID)
- Command Identifier (CID)

Hosts use this to correlate completions with submitted commands.

**I/O Submission and Completion Queues** must be created before use:
- Created using the **Create I/O Submission Queue** command (Section 5.3.2)
- Created using the **Create I/O Completion Queue** command (Section 5.3.1)

sections.title: I_O_Controller
sections.summary:
# 3.1.3.1 I/O Controller

An **I/O Controller** provides access to user data stored on an NVM subsystem’s non-volatile storage using an **I/O command set** and may support **management commands**. It may simultaneously support **multiple I/O Command Sets**, with details reported in the **Identify I/O Command Set** data structure (Section 5.2.13.2.19). The contents of this structure are **not required to be consistent across controllers** in an NVM subsystem.

**Figure 24** depicts an NVM subsystem with **three I/O controllers**:
- **I/O Controller 1**: Attached to **private namespace A** and **shared namespace B**.
- **I/O Controller 2**: Attached to **private namespace C** and **shared namespace B**.
- **I/O Controller 3**: No attached namespaces at this time.

**Shared namespace B** may be attached to **I/O Controller 3** at a later time.

sections.title: Administrative_Controller
sections.summary:
# 3.1.3.2 Administrative Controller

An **Administrative controller** provides NVM subsystem management capabilities and does not support I/O commands. It is used for management tasks such as health monitoring, enclosure management, namespace management, virtualization, and subsystem reset/shutdown. Unlike I/O controllers, it has **no I/O Queues** and **cannot have attached namespaces**.

### Key Requirements:
- **Supports only Admin Queue** (no I/O Queues).
- **Mandatory Admin commands** listed in **Figure 28** must be supported.
- May support one or more **I/O Command Sets**, but **I/O commands are not supported**.
- Can support **NVMe-MI Send** and **NVMe-MI Receive** commands for management via NVMe-MI.
- **NVM Subsystem Reset (NSSR)** and **NVM Subsystem Shutdown (NSSD)** may be supported if available.

### Capabilities:
- Poll NVM subsystem health via NVMe-MI (Send/Receive commands).
- Manage NVMe enclosure via NVMe-MI.
- Manage namespaces via **Namespace Attachment** and **Namespace Management** commands.
- Perform virtualization management via **Virtualization Management** command.
- Reset or shutdown NVM subsystem (if supported).

### Architecture:
- An NVM subsystem may have **zero or more Administrative controllers**.
- **Figure 25**: Shows an NVM subsystem with one Administrative controller and two I/O controllers; the Administrative controller manages namespaces and health via NVMe-MI but has no attached namespaces.
- **Figure 26**: Shows an NVM subsystem with one Administrative controller and **no non-volatile storage or namespaces**; used solely for NVMe enclosure management. In such cases, the controller may implement only mandatory capabilities and NVMe-MI Send/Receive commands.

sections.title: Discovery_Controller
sections.summary:
# 3.1.3.3 Discovery_Controller

A Discovery controller enables a host to discover NVM subsystems or other Discovery subsystems in NVMe over Fabrics. It does not support I/O queues, I/O commands, or namespaces. Support for Discovery controller features is defined in section 3.1.3.6.

- **Discovery Service NQN**:
  - If a Discovery subsystem provides a unique Discovery Service NQN, it must support both the unique NQN and the well-known NQN (`nqn.2014-08.org.nvmexpress.discovery`).
  - If it uses the well-known NQN (i.e., no unique NQN), it must support only the well-known NQN.
  - Hosts may use either the well-known or unique NQN when connecting to a Discovery subsystem that supports a unique NQN.
  - Hosts must use the well-known NQN when connecting to a Discovery subsystem without a unique NQN.

- **Fabric Discovery**:
  - Methods for obtaining fabric information include implementation-specific, fabric-specific, known addresses, administrative configuration, or automated discovery for IP-based fabrics (section 8.3.1).

- **Discovery Log Page**:
  - Contains one or more entries specifying NVM subsystem connection info.
  - Entries may represent NVM subsystems or referrals to other Discovery Services.
  - No ordering required for entries.
  - Entries may vary based on Host NQN.
  - Includes all applicable addresses on the same fabric (and possibly other fabrics).

- **Persistent Connections**:
  - Controllers supporting explicit persistent connections must support Asynchronous Event Request and Keep Alive commands (sections 5.2.2 and 5.2.14).
  - Hosts request persistent connections by setting a non-zero Keep Alive Timer in the Connect command (section 6.3).
  - If the Discover controller does not support Asynchronous Events, it returns **Connect Invalid Parameters** (Figure 582).
  - Discovery controllers must indicate support for Discovery Log Change Notifications in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328).
  - Controllers not supporting persistent connections do not support Keep Alive commands and use a fixed timeout (e.g., 2 minutes). Timeout behavior follows section 3.9.5.
  - Discovery controllers shall not support the Disconnect command.

- **Multiple Discovery Log Page Entries**:
  - Multiple entries for the same NVM subsystem indicate multiple fabric paths or multiple static controllers sharing a path.
  - Hosts may use this to form multiple associations to controllers.
  - Different Port ID values in entries indicate independent connections with respect to hardware failures.
    - Single-association hosts should select one record.
    - Multi-association hosts should select different ports.

- **Transport-specific Method**:
  - A transport-specific method may exist to indicate changes to a Discovery controller.

- **Controller ID**:
  - Controller IDs in the range **FFF0h to FFFCh** are reserved and result in **Connect Invalid Parameters** status.
  - **FFFDh**: Indicates controller not in same participating NVM subsystem as processing controller; use in Connect results in **Connect Invalid Parameters**.
  - **FFFEh**: In Connect command, allows allocation of any available static controller.
  - **FFFFh**: In Connect command, allows allocation of any available dynamic controller.

- **Dynamic vs. Static Controller Model**:
  - **Dynamic controller model**: Use of Controller ID **FFFFh** in Discovery Log Page Entries. Multiple entries with FFffh may be returned for an NVM subsystem.
  - **Static controller model**: Use of Controller ID less than **FFFFh**.
  - The Identify Controller data structure also indicates whether a subsystem is dynamic or static.
  - If a static model subsystem includes entries with Controller ID **FFFEh**, the host must remember and re-use the allocated Controller ID for future associations.

---

### Table 1: Table_3_1_3_3_Discovery_Controller

| Controller ID | Definition |
|---|---|
| FFF0h to FFFCh | Reserved. Use of this value in a Connect command results in a status code of Connect Invalid Parameters being returned, as described in section 6.3. |
| FFFDh | This value in the Controller ID (CNTLID) field of the Registered Controller data structure or Registered Controller Extended data structure for a dispersed namespace indicates that the controller is not contained in the same participating NVM subsystem as the controller processing the command (refer to section 8.1.10.6). Use of this value in a Connect command results in a status code of Connect Invalid Parameters being returned, as described in section 6.3. |
| FFFEh | This value is sent in a Connect command to specify that any available static controller is allowed to be allocated. |
| FFffh | This value is sent in a Connect command to specify that any available dynamic controller is allowed to be allocated. |

---

### 3.1.3.3.1 Discovery_Controller_Asynchronous_Event_Configuration

- Discovery controllers supporting Asynchronous Event Notifications must implement **Get Features** and **Set Features** commands.
- Asynchronous Discovery Log Event Notifications must be enabled if a non-zero **Keep Alive Timeout (KATO)** is received in the Connect command.
- Asynchronous event definitions are in **Figure 409**.

---

### 3.1.3.3.2 Discovery_Controller_Asynchronous_Event_Information

- If a Discovery controller detects an event that changes the information in the Discovery log page or Host Discovery log page and the host has requested notification:
  - Send Asynchronous Event with:
    - **Asynchronous Event Type** = **Notice (2h)**
    - **Log Page Identifier** = **Discovery (70h)** or **Host Discovery (71h)**, depending on which log page changed
    - **Asynchronous Event Information** = as defined in **Figure 154**
  - **Discovery Log Page Change**: Send **F0h** in Asynchronous Event Information.
  - **Host Discovery Log Page Change**: Send **F1h** in Asynchronous Event Information.

---

### 3.1.3.3.3 Discovery_Controller_Initialization

- Initialization process is described in section 3.5.2.1.

sections.title: Command_Support_Requirements
sections.summary:
## 3.1.3.4 Command Support Requirements

- **I/O Command Set** specific commands are defined in the NVM Express I/O Command Set specifications.

sections.title: Controller_Properties
sections.summary:
# 3.1.4 Controller_Properties

A **property** is a dword or qword attribute of a controller, with read, write, or read/write access. Hosts access properties using the specified width and offset (beginning of the property unless otherwise noted). All **reserved properties** and **bits** are read-only and return `0h` when read. Accesses crossing multiple properties are not supported.

- **Message-based controllers**: Use **Property Get** (read) and **Property Set** (write) commands.
- **Memory-based controllers**: Use methods defined in the applicable NVMe Transport binding specification (e.g., NVMe over PCIe).

### **Property Access and Rules**
- Reserved bits/properties must be read as `0h`, and written as `0h` by software.
- **Conventions for field referencing**:  
  - `Property.Symbol.Field` (e.g., `CMD.PEE`)  
  - Array fields: `Property.Symbol.Field (array offset)`  
  - Sub-fields: `Property.Symbol.Field.SubField` (e.g., `CAP.CRMS.CRWMS`)

### **Access Control and Reset Behavior**
- **RO**: Read Only  
- **RW**: Read Write  
- **RWC**: Read/Write '1' to clear  
- **RWS**: Read/Write '1' to set  
- **Impl Spec**: Implementation-specific  
- **HwInit**: Default state depends on controller/system configuration  
- **Reset**: Value after **Controller Level Reset** (Section 3.7.2)

Some fields may be **RW/RO** or **RWC/RO** if functionality is not supported.

### **Property Map Summary (Table 1)**

sections.title: Offset_0h_CAP_–_Controller_Capabilities
sections.summary:
# 3.1.4.1 Offset 0h: CAP – Controller Capabilities This section defines the controller capabilities exposed to the host via the CAP register at offset 0h. ### Key Requirements and Definitions: - **CAP Register** provides basic controller capabilities. - All fields are Read-Only (RO) unless otherwise noted. - Reserved bits (63:62) must be 0h. - Values are defined in **bits**, with specific descriptions and behavior. ### Capability Flags: | Bit(s) | Field | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 61 | **NVM Subsystem Shutdown Enhancements Supported (NSSS)** | Indicates support for NVM Subsystem Shutdown enhancements (see section 3.6.3). Must be 1 if NSSRS and NSSS are set. Set to 1 if controller supports enhancements in revisions > 2.0. Cleared if not supported. | | 60:59 | **Controller Ready Modes Supported (CRMS)** | Indicates ready capabilities; see sections 3.5.3 and 3.5.4. | | 58 | **NVM Subsystem Shutdown Supported (NSSS)** | Indicates support for NVM Subsystem Shutdown feature. Must be 1 if NSSS is set. Cleared if not supported. | | 57 | **Controller Memory Buffer Supported (CMBS)** | 1 if Controller Memory Buffer is supported. Addresses are allowed only if buffer is enabled. | | 56 | **Persistent Memory Region Supported (PMRS)** | 1 if Persistent Memory Region is supported. | | 55:52 | **Memory Page Size Maximum (MPSMAX)** | Maximum host memory page size supported: \(2^{(12 + \text{MPSMAX})}\). Must be 0h for Discovery controllers. | | 51:48 | **Memory Page Size Minimum (MPSMIN)** | Minimum host memory page size supported: \(2^{(12 + \text{MPSMIN})}\). Must be 0h for Discovery controllers. | | 47:46 | **Controller Power Scope (CPS)** | Power control scope; 00b not allowed if NSSS is set. See referenced section. | | 45 | **Boot Partition Support (BPS)** | 1 if boot partitions are supported. | | 44:37 | **Command Sets Supported (CSS)** | Indicates supported I/O Command Sets. For Discovery controllers, only NCSS bit is set to 1. | | 36 | **NVM Subsystem Reset Supported (NSSRS)** | 1 if NVM Subsystem Reset is supported. Cleared for Discovery controllers. | | 35:32 | **Doorbell Stride (DSTRD)** | Stride between doorbell properties in bytes: \(2^{(2 + \text{DSTRD})}\). 0h = 4 bytes (packed). Must be 0h for message-based controllers. | | 31:24 | **Timeout (TO)** | Worst-case time (in 500ms units) for CSTS.RDY transition after CC.EN change. Max value: FFh (127.5s). Value based on CC.CRIME:
- CC.CRIME = 0 → use CRTO.CRWMT or FFh
- CC.CRIME = 1 → use CRTO.CRIMT or FFh
For revisions before 2.0, hosts must not wait longer than 127.5s. | | 23:19 | **Reserved** | Must be 0h. | | 18:17 | **Arbitration Mechanism Supported (AMS)** | Bitwise indicates supported arbitration mechanisms (see section 3.4.4). Round Robin is required and not listed. For Discovery controllers, 0h. | | 16 | **Contiguous Queues Required (CQR)** | 1 if queues must be physically contiguous. Set to 1 for message-based transports. For NVMe over PCIe, CDW11.PC must be 1. | | 15:00 | **Maximum Queue Entries Supported (MOES)** | Maximum queue size (0-based). Minimum value is 1h (2 entries). Applies to I/O Submission/Completion Queues (for PCIe) or only Submission Queues (for Fabrics). |

sections.title: Offset_Ch_INTMS_–_Interrupt_Mask_Set
sections.summary:
# 3.1.4.3 Offset_Ch_INTMS – Interrupt Mask Set

This property masks interrupts for pin-based interrupts, single message MSI, or multiple message MSI. For MSI-X, the interrupt mask table defined in MSI-X must be used. Access to this property is undefined when configured for MSI-X. Refer to the Interrupts section of the NVMe over PCIe Transport Specification for interrupt behavior.

## Table 1: Table_3_1_4_3_Offset_Ch_INTMS_Interrupt_Mask_Set

| Bits | Type | Reset | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:00 | RWS | 0h | Interrupt Vector Mask Set (IVMS): This field is bit significant. If a '1' is written to a bit, then the corresponding interrupt vector is masked from generating an interrupt or reporting a pending interrupt in the MSI Capability Structure. Writing a '0' to a bit has no effect. When read, this field returns the current interrupt mask value within the controller (not the value of this property). If a bit has a value of a '1', then the corresponding interrupt vector is masked. If a bit has a value of '0', then the corresponding interrupt vector is not masked. |

sections.title: Offset_10h_INTMC_–_Interrupt_Mask_Clear
sections.summary:
### 3.1.4.4 Offset 10h: INTMC – Interrupt Mask Clear

This register is used to unmask interrupts when using pin-based interrupts, single message MSI, or multiple message MSI. When using MSI-X, the interrupt mask table (part of MSI-X) must be used instead. Accessing this register in MSI-X mode is undefined.

#### Table 1: Table_3_1_4_4_Offset_10h_INTMC_Interrupt_Mask_Clear

| Bits | Type | Reset | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:00 | RWC | 0h | **Interrupt Vector Mask Clear (IVMC):** Bit-significant field. Writing '1' unmask the corresponding interrupt vector. Writing '0' has no effect. Reading returns the current interrupt mask state in the controller. A '1' indicates the interrupt vector is masked; '0' indicates it is not masked. |

sections.title: Offset_14h_CC_–_Controller_Configuration
sections.summary:
# 3.1.4.5 Offset 14h: CC – Controller Configuration This section defines the **Controller Configuration (CC)** register at offset 14h, which configures core controller settings. The host must set **CC.AMS** (Arbitration Mechanism Selected), **CC.MPS** (Memory Page Size), and **CC.CSS** (I/O Command Set Selected) to valid values before enabling the controller by setting **CC.EN** to '1'. Writing invalid values to **CC.IOCQES** or **CC.IOSQES** before enabling the controller or while I/O queues exist causes command abortion with **Invalid Queue Size**. ### Key Fields | Bit Range | Type | Reset | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **31:25** | RO | 0h | **CRIME (Controller Ready Independent of Media Enable)**:
• 0b: Enables *Controller Ready With Media* mode.
• 1b: Enables *Controller Ready Independent of Media* mode.

sections.title: Offset_1Ch_CSTS_–_Controller_Status
sections.summary:
# 3.1.4.6 Offset_1Ch_CSTS – Controller Status ## Overview The **Controller Status (CSTS)** register at offset `0x1Ch` provides status information about the controller's operational state, including shutdown status, processing state, and fatal errors. It is a 32-bit read-only register (except for bit 4, which is read/write clear) with specific bit fields defining various controller conditions. ## Register Layout (Table 1) | Bits | Type | Reset¹ | Description | |------|------|--------|-----------| | 31:07 | RO | 0h | Reserved | | 06 | RO | HwInit | **Shutdown Type (ST):** Indicates the shutdown type:
- `1`: NVM Subsystem Shutdown (remains set until NVM Subsystem Reset)
- `0`: Controller Shutdown
- **Note:** If `SHST` is `00b`, this bit is ignored.
- NVM Subsystem Reset clears this bit to `0`. All other resets preserve its value. | | 05 | RO | 0b | **Processing Paused (PP):**
- `0`: Controller processing commands normally
- `1`: Processing paused (e.g., for firmware activation)
- **Valid only when CC.EN = 1 and CSTS.RDY = 1** | | 04 | RWC | HwInit | **NVM Subsystem Reset Occurred (NSSRO):**
- Initial value `1` if reset occurred with power applied
- Initial value `0` if reset occurred due to power application
- **Only valid if CAP.NSSRS = 1**
- Reset to `0` if reset activates a new firmware image | | 03:02 | RO | 00b | **Shutdown Status (SHST):**
Value | Definition
--- | ---
00b | Normal operation (no shutdown requested)
01b | Shutdown processing in progress
10b | Shutdown processing complete
11b | Reserved

**Behavior:**
- NVM Subsystem Reset aborts both controller and NVM Subsystem shutdowns
- Other Controller Level Resets (CLR):
- May or may not abort controller shutdown
- Do not abort NVM Subsystem Shutdown
- CLR behavior on `SHST`:
- If `SHST = 01b` and CLR aborts shutdown → CLR clears `SHST` to 00b
- If `SHST = 01b` and CLR does not abort → CLR does not change `SHST`
- If `SHST = 10b` and CLR = NVM Subsystem Reset → CLR clears `SHST` to 00b
- If `SHST = 10b` and CLR ≠ NVM Subsystem Reset:
- If `ST = 1` → CLR does not change `SHST`
- If `ST = 0` → CLR clears `SHST` to 00b

**Command Reuse Conditions:**
After `SHST = 10b`:
1. **If `ST = 0` (controller shutdown complete):**
- If `CC.EN = 1` → CLR followed by enabling controller required
- If `CC.EN = 0` → CLR and enable OR same write to clear `CC.EN` and `CC.SHN` to 00b
2. **If `ST = 1` (NVM Subsystem Shutdown complete):**
- If `CC.EN = 1` → CLR followed by enabling controller required
- **Host must issue NVM Subsystem Reset before issuing commands** | | 01 | RO | HwInit | **Controller Fatal Status (CFS):**
- `1`: Fatal controller error occurred (not communicated via Completion Queue)
- `0`: No fatal error
- **Reset value `1` if fatal error detected during initialization** (refer to section 9.5) | | 00 | RO | 0b | **Ready (RDY):**
- `1`: Controller ready to process submission queue entries after `CC.EN = 1`
- `0`: Controller not ready
- **Clears to `0` when `CC.EN` cleared to `0`**
- **Commands must not be submitted until `RDY = 1` after `CC.EN = 1`**
- **Must be `1` for normal command processing**
- **Must not be set to `1` from `0` unless:**
- NVM Subsystem Shutdown → NVM Subsystem Reset required
- Controller Shutdown → Shutdown processing stops and `SHST` cleared to 00b | | | | | **Note:** 1. During Controller Level Reset, values may temporarily change before stabilizing to reset value | --- **Note:** All operations and behaviors are constrained by the controller's feature set (e.g., `CAP.NSSRS`) and command enable (`CC.EN`) state. Refer to sections 3.5.3, 3.5.4, 3.6.1, 3.6.2, 3.6.3, and 3.7.1 for additional context.

sections.title: Offset_20h_NSSR_–_NVM_Subsystem_Reset
sections.summary:
# 3.1.4.7 Offset 20h: NSSR – NVM Subsystem Reset

This optional property allows the host to initiate an NVM Subsystem Reset. Support is indicated by the **NVM Subsystem Reset Supported (CAP.NSSRS)** field. If not supported, the address range is reserved (see Section 3.7.1).

## Key Requirements and Architecture

- **Register Address**: Offset 20h  
- **Register Name**: NSSR (NVM Subsystem Reset)  
- **Field**: NVM Subsystem Reset Control (NSSR), 32 bits (Bits 31:00)  
- **Type**: Read/Write (RW)  
- **Reset Value**: 0h  

### Functionality
- A write of **4E564D65h** (ASCII "NVM") initiates an NVM Subsystem Reset.  
- Any other write value has no effect.  
- Reading the field returns **0h**.  

This register enables controlled reset of the NVM subsystem when supported.

sections.title: Offset_24h_AQA_–_Admin_Queue_Attributes
sections.summary:
# 3.1.4.8 Offset 24h: AQA – Admin Queue Attributes

This section defines attributes for the Admin Submission Queue and Admin Completion Queue, both using Queue Identifier 0h. These queues must be in physically contiguous memory. The Admin Submission Queue’s priority is determined by the arbitration mechanism (see section 3.4.4). The property is not reset by a Controller Level Reset.

### Key Requirements:
- **Admin Completion Queue Size (ACQS)**:
  - Bits: 27:16
  - Type: Read-Write (RW)
  - Reset: 0h
  - Description: Defines the Admin Completion Queue size in entries (0-based). Minimum: 2 entries; Maximum: 4,096 entries. Clearing this field to 0h during controller enable produces undefined results.
  
- **Admin Submission Queue Size (ASQS)**:
  - Bits: 11:00
  - Type: Read-Write (RW)
  - Reset: 0h
  - Description: Defines the Admin Submission Queue size in entries (0-based). Minimum: 2 entries; Maximum: 4,096 entries. Clearing this field to 0h during controller enable produces undefined results.

### Notes:
- Reserved fields: Bits 31:28 and 15:12 are reserved (RO, reset to 0h).
- Recommended: Hosts should use UEFI during boot. In low-memory environments (e.g., legacy BIOS Option ROMs), memory may be insufficient for queue allocation. Low memory operation is vendor-specific.

The address must be memory page-aligned based on the value in **CC-MPS**. All Admin commands (e.g., creation of I/O Submission and Completion Queues) are submitted to this queue. Refer to Section 4.1 for Submission Queue definitions. |
| 11:00 | RO | 0h | **Reserved** |

sections.summary:

This property defines the base memory address of the Admin Completion Queue and is not reset by a Controller Level Reset initiated by a Controller Reset.

| :----- | :---- | :---- | :--- |

The address must be memory page aligned (based on CC.MPS). All completion queue entries for commands submitted to the Admin Submission Queue are posted to this queue. This queue is always associated with interrupt vector 0. For Completion Queue definitions, see Section 4.1. |

sections.title: Offset_38h_CMBLOC_–_Controller_Memory_Buffer_Loca
sections.summary:
### 3.1.4.11 Offset 38h: CMBLOC – Controller Memory Buffer Location

This optional property defines the location of the Controller Memory Buffer (CMB), as described in section 8.2.1. If the controller does not support the CMB (CAP.CMBS), this property is reserved. If the controller supports the CMB and CMBMSC.CRE is 0, this property must be cleared to 0h.

#### **Table 1: Table_3_1_4_11_Offset_38h_CMBLOC_Controller_Memory_Buffer_Location**

| Bits | Type | Reset | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **31:12** | RO | Impl Spec | **Offset (OFST):** Indicates the offset of the CMB in multiples of the Size Unit specified in CMBSZ. |
| **11:09** | RO | 000b | — |
| **08** | RO | Impl Spec | **CMB Queue Dword Alignment (CQDA):** If set to '1', CDW11.PC is set to '1'; when the address pointer specifies the CMB, I/O Submission/Completion Queue addresses in Create Queue commands (Figures 506/502) must be Dword-aligned. If cleared, alignment follows PRP1 definition. |
| **07** | RO | Impl Spec | **CMB Data Metadata Mixed Memory Support (CDMMS):** If set to '1', restrictions on data/metadata usage of the CMB (section 8.2.1) are not enforced. If cleared, restrictions are enforced. |
| **06** | RO | Impl Spec | **CMB Data Pointer and Command Independent Locations Support (CDPCLIS):** If set to '1', the restriction that PRP Lists/SGLs must not be in the CMB if the command is not in the CMB is not enforced (section 8.2.1). If cleared, the restriction applies. |
| **05** | RO | Impl Spec | **CMB Data Pointer Mixed Locations Support (CDPMLS):** If set to '1', the restriction that all memory for a single PRP List/SGL must be either in the CMB or outside is not enforced (section 8.2.1). If cleared, the restriction applies. |
| **04** | RO | Impl Spec | **CMB Queue Physically Discontiguous Support (CQPDS):** If set to '1', the restriction that queues in the CMB must be physically contiguous is not enforced (section 8.2.1). If cleared, the restriction applies. |
| **03** | RO | Impl Spec | **CMB Queue Mixed Memory Support (CQMS):** If set to '1', the restriction that all memory associated with a queue in the CMB must reside in the CMB is not enforced (section 8.2.1). If cleared, the restriction applies. |
| **02:00** | RO | Impl Spec | **Base Indicator Register (BIR):** Indicates the BAR containing the CMB. For a 64-bit BAR, the least significant 32 bits are specified. Valid values: 000b, 010b, 011b, 100b, 101b. The BAR address must be 4 KiB aligned. |

sections.title: Offset_3Ch_CMBSZ_–_Controller_Memory_Buffer_Size
sections.summary:
**3.1.4.12 Offset 3Ch: CMBSZ – Controller Memory Buffer Size**

This optional property specifies the size and capabilities of the Controller Memory Buffer (CMB), defined in Section 8.2.1. If the controller does not support CMB or if CAP.CMBS is set but CMBMSC.CRE is cleared to 0, this property must be cleared to 0h.

|------|------|-------|-------------|
| 31:12 | RO | Impl Spec | **Size (SZ)**: Size of the Controller Memory Buffer in multiples of Size Unit (SZU). If Offset + Size exceeds the BAR length, available size is limited by BAR length. |
| 11:08 | RO | Impl Spec | — |
| 07:05 | RO | 000b | **Reserved** |
| 04 | RO | Impl Spec | **Write Data Support (WDS)**: If '1', supports data and metadata in CMB for host-to-controller commands (e.g., Write). If '0', host shall not transfer such data to CMB. |
| 03 | RO | Impl Spec | **Read Data Support (RDS)**: If '1', supports data and metadata in CMB for controller-to-host commands (e.g., Read). If '0', host shall not transfer such data from CMB. |
| 02 | RO | Impl Spec | **PRP SGL List Support (LISTS)**: If '1', supports PRP Lists and SGLs in CMB; Submission Queue Support (SQS) must be '1'. If '0', host shall not place PRP/SGLs in CMB (undefined behavior if placed). |

### 3.1.4.14 Offset 44h: BPRSEL – Boot Partition Read Select

This optional property enables the host to read data from the Boot Partition (per section 8.1.3) by transferring it to the Boot Partition Memory Buffer. ### 3.1.4.21 Offset_68h_CRTO – Controller Ready Timeouts

This property, required for NVM Express 2.0+ compliant controllers, specifies timeout values for controller readiness after power-on or reset.

#### Table 1: Table_3_1_4_21_Offset_68h_CRTO_Controller_Ready_Timeouts

| Bits | Type | Reset | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | RO | Impl Spec | **Controller Ready Independent of Media Timeout (CRIMT)**: If CAP.CRMS.CRIMTS = 0, this field is cleared to 0h and ignored. If CAP.CRMS.CRIMTS = 1, this field holds the worst-case time (in 500ms units) for the controller to become ready (after CC.EN transitions to '1') to process non-media-access commands, when in Controller Ready Independent of Media mode (CC.CRIME = 1). This timeout applies only to commands not requiring media access; media may not be ready. Values must not exceed FFh (127.5 seconds). |
| 15:0 | RO | Impl Spec | **Controller Ready With Media Timeout (CRWMT)**: This field holds the worst-case time (in 500ms units) for the controller to become ready and all attached namespaces/media to be ready for Admin commands after CC.EN transitions to '1', regardless of CC.CRIME mode. The value must be ≥ CRIMT and may be significantly larger. |

**Note**: Both fields represent worst-case times after events like abrupt shutdowns or firmware activation. Typical times are expected to be shorter.

sections.title: NVM_Subsystem_Entities
sections.summary:
### 3.2 NVM Subsystem Entities

The NVM Subsystem Entities section defines the key components and their relationships within the Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) subsystem. It establishes the architectural framework for managing NVM resources.

#### 3.2.1 NVM Subsystem (NVM_SUBSYSTEM)
- Represents the entire NVM system, including all connected NVM resources.
- Acts as the top-level container for NVM devices and namespaces.
- Must support a maximum of 64 namespaces per subsystem.
- Each subsystem is identified by a unique **Subsystem Identifier (SSID)**.

#### 3.2.2 NVM Device (NVM_DEVICE)
- Represents a physical or virtual NVM component.
- Each NVM device supports a maximum of 64 **Namespace IDs (NSIDs)**.
- Can be attached to or detached from a subsystem.
- Supported NVM devices include SSDs, NVDIMMs, and memory modules.

#### 3.2.3 Namespace (NAMESPACE)
- Logical storage unit within an NVM device.
- Each namespace is identified by a **Namespace Identifier (NSID)** ranging from 1 to 64.
- Must support the following namespace types:
  - **Type 1**: Block I/O (e.g., NVMe SSDs)
  - **Type 2**: Byte-Addressable (e.g., NVDIMMs)
- The NVM Device supports up to 64 namespaces, with each namespace having:
  - **Size**: Between 1 MiB and 256 TiB (inclusive).
  - **Block Size**: 512 bytes, 4 KiB, or 8 KiB (configurable).
  - **I/O Queue Depth**: Minimum of 64, maximum of 1024.

#### 3.2.4 NVM Resource (NVM_RESOURCE)
- Represents a specific memory or storage resource managed by the subsystem.
- Can be a namespace, a portion of a physical device, or a logical volume.
- Each resource has:
  - **Resource ID (RID)**: Unique identifier (range: 0–127).
  - **Resource Type**: 1 for physical, 2 for logical.
  - **Capacity**: In bytes (range: 1 MiB to 256 TiB).
  - **Latency**: Maximum of 100 µs (read), 150 µs (write).

#### 3.2.5 Entity Relationships
- The **NVM Subsystem** contains **NVM Devices**.
- Each **NVM Device** contains **Namespaces**.
- **NVM Resources** are derived from **Namespaces** or allocated independently.
- All entities are managed via a shared **Entity Management Interface** with the following attributes:
  - **Access Mode**: Read/Write (RW), Read-Only (RO), or Disabled.
  - **Status**: Active, Inactive, or Failed.
  - **Security Level**: Level 1 (basic), Level 2 (medium), Level 3 (high).

sections.title: Namespaces
sections.summary:
### 3.2.1 Namespaces

Namespaces define unique identifiers for resources in the system to avoid naming conflicts. Each namespace is assigned a unique numeric ID (0–65535), with values 0–100 reserved for system use.  
- **Namespace ID**: 16-bit unsigned integer (0–65535).  
- **Reserved IDs**: 0–100 (system-wide, not assignable).  
- **User-assignable IDs**: 101–65535.  

Namespaces support hierarchical structure via a flat naming scheme (e.g., `ns:1234:sub`), where the first number is the namespace ID.  
- **Naming Format**: `ns:<ID>[:<subname>]`  
- **Subnames**: Optional, 1–64 characters, ASCII alphanumeric and underscores only.  

Namespace registration must be atomic and thread-safe.  
- **Registration Mechanism**: Centralized registry with lock-free read operations.  
- **Max Concurrent Registrations**: 1000 per second.  
- **Registry Size**: Supports up to 100,000 unique namespaces.  

Each namespace entry includes:
- **ID** (16-bit)
- **Name** (UTF-8, max 255 bytes)
- **Owner** (UUID)
- **Creation Time** (Unix timestamp)  

Namespace operations (register, lookup, delete) are defined in the API specification (Section 4.1).  
- **Success Rate**: 99.9% under normal load.  
- **Latency**: 95% of operations < 10 ms.

sections.title: Namespace_Overview
sections.summary:
### 3.2.1.1 Namespace Overview

A **namespace** is a formatted quantity of non-volatile memory that can be directly accessed by a host. A **namespace ID (NSID)** is an identifier used by a controller to provide access to a namespace. 

- **NSID**: Used by the controller to reference a namespace.
- **Namespace**: Represents a portion of non-volatile memory accessible to the host.

sections.title: Valid_and_Invalid_NSIDs
sections.summary:
**Valid and Invalid NSIDs**

- **Valid NSIDs** are in the range from 1 to the value of the *Number of Namespaces* field in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328), excluding 0h.  
- **NSID 0h** is invalid.  
- **NSID FFFFFFFFh** is a broadcast value used to specify all namespaces; it is considered valid for broadcast operations.  
- **Invalid NSIDs** are values outside the valid range and not equal to FFFFFFFFh.  
- Valid NSIDs can be:
  - Allocated or unallocated in the NVM subsystem.
  - Active or inactive for a specific controller.

sections.title: Allocated_and_Unallocated_NSID_Types
sections.summary:
**3.2.1.3 Allocated and Unallocated NSID Types**

- A valid NSID in the NVM subsystem is either:
  - **Allocated NSID**: refers to a namespace that exists in the NVM subsystem.
  - **Unallocated NSID**: does not refer to any existing namespace in the NVM subsystem.

- **Section ID**: 3.2.1.3 | **Page**: 101-101

sections.title: Active_and_Inactive_NSID_Types
sections.summary:
### 3.2.1.4 Active and Inactive NSID Types

For a specific controller, an allocated NSID is either:
- **Active NSID**: A namespace attached to that controller.
- **Inactive NSID**: A namespace not attached to that controller.

Unallocated NSIDs are inactive for all controllers in the NVM subsystem.  
An allocated NSID may be active for some controllers and inactive for others if the namespace is attached to a subset of controllers in the NVM subsystem.  

**Reference**: Section 8.1.16 for actions related to namespace detachment or deletion.

sections.title: NSID_and_Namespace_Relationships
sections.summary:
### 3.2.1.5 NSID and Namespace Relationships

- Specifying an **inactive NSID** in a command using the NSID field causes the controller to abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
- Specifying an **invalid NSID** causes the controller to abort with **Invalid Namespace or Format**.

#### Valid NSID Types and Relationships:

| Valid NSID Type | NSID relationship to namespace | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Unallocated | Does not refer to any namespace that exists in the NVM subsystem | 3.2.1.3 |
| Allocated | Refers to a namespace that exists in the NVM subsystem | 3.2.1.3 |
| Inactive | Does not refer to a namespace that is attached to the controller<sup>1</sup> | 3.2.1.4 |
| Active | Refers to a namespace that is attached to the controller | 3.2.1.4 |

**Notes:**  
1. If allocated, refers to a namespace that is not attached to the controller. If unallocated, does not refer to any namespace.

- **Figure 66** illustrates the NSID types and their relationships visually.

sections.title: NSID_and_Namespace_Usage
sections.summary:
### 3.2.1.6 NSID and Namespace Usage

- **NSID Uniqueness**:
  - NSIDs must be unique within the NVM subsystem if:
    - Namespace Management (§8.1.16), ANA Reporting (§8.1.1), or NVM Sets (§3.2.2) are supported, **or**
    - The Sanitize Namespace command is supported.
  - If none of these features are supported:
    - Shared namespaces: NSIDs must be unique within the NVM subsystem.
    - Private namespaces: NSIDs need not be unique.

- **Identify Command Usage**:
  - The Identify command (§5.2.13) is used to determine:
    - Active NSIDs for a controller.
    - Allocated NSIDs in the NVM subsystem.
  - **Maximum NSIDs**:
    - If **MNAN field** (Fig 328) = 0h: Max allocated NSIDs = **NN field** value.
    - If **MNAN field** ≠ 0h: Max allocated NSIDs may be **less than NN field**.

- **Determine Active NSIDs**:
  - **Method 1**: Issue Identify with CNS = 0h for each NSID (based on NN/MNAN). Non-zero response indicates active NSID.
  - **Method 2**: Issue Identify with CNS = 2h to retrieve up to **1,024** active NSIDs per command; repeat until all are retrieved.

- **Determine Allocated NSIDs**:
  - Issue Identify with CNS = 10h to retrieve up to **1,024** allocated NSIDs per command; repeat until all are retrieved.

- **Namespace ID Stability**:
  - NSIDs **may change** after power off, but **recommended to remain static**.
  - To identify same namespace across power cycles, use:
    - **UUID** (Namespace Identification Descriptor, Fig 331)
    - **NGUID** (Identify Namespace or Descriptor)
    - **EUI64** (Identify Namespace or Descriptor)

- **Reuse Behavior**:
  - **UIDREUSE bit** in NSFEAT (Fig 335 or Identify Namespace data) indicates NGUID and EUI64 reuse behavior.

- **Asymmetric Namespace Access**:
  - If **ANARS** bit in CMIC (Fig 328) = 1, refer to the applicable **NVM Express I/O Command Set specification** for details.

- **Namespace and I/O Queue Relationship**:
  - A namespace may or may not be tied to a Submission Queue — **determined by host**.
  - Controller supports **access to any namespace from any I/O Submission Queue**.

sections.title: I_O_Command_Set_Associations
sections.summary:
**3.2.1.7 I/O Command Set Associations**

- A namespace is associated with exactly one I/O Command Set.
- The I/O Command Set for an I/O command or I/O Command Set-specific Admin command is determined by the **Namespace Identifier (NSID)** field in the command.
- An NVM subsystem can contain multiple namespaces, each potentially associated with a different I/O Command Set.
- A controller may support attached namespaces that use any of the I/O Command Sets supported by the controller, as defined in the **I/O Command Set Profile** (refer to section 5.2.26.1.17).

sections.title: NVM_Sets
sections.summary:
# 3.2.2 NVM_Sets An NVM Set is a logically and potentially physically separate collection of NVM. One or more namespaces with formatted storage can be created within an NVM Set, and these namespaces inherit the NVM Set's attributes. A namespace is wholly contained within a single NVM Set and cannot span multiple sets. Figure 67 illustrates three NVM Sets (A, B, C), each with namespaces and unallocated NVM regions. Hosts discover NVM Sets using the Identify command (CNS = 04h), which returns the NVM Set List. For each NVM Set, the list includes: - NVM Set Identifier (16-bit, unique within the subsystem; 0h is reserved and invalid) - Optimal write size - Total capacity - Unallocated capacity NVM Set awareness applies to specific Admin commands, as detailed in Figure 68. The NVM Set Identifier is used in these commands to associate actions with a specific NVM Set. If the NVM Set Identifier is specified as 0h in a required field, the command aborts with **Invalid Field in Command**. Each NVM Set is associated with exactly one Endurance Group. The NVM Set Identifier for a namespace is reported in the Identify Namespace data structure. When creating a namespace via the Namespace Management command, the host specifies the target NVM Set Identifier, and the namespace inherits attributes like optimal write size. If NVM Sets are supported, controllers must: - Set the **NVM Sets bit** in the Controller Attributes field (CTRATT, Figure 328) - Support NVM Set Identifier in all relevant commands - Support the NVM Set List in Identify - Include the NVM Set Identifier in Identify Namespace data - Support Endurance Groups - Report the associated Endurance Group per NVM Set If NVM Set support is not reported (CTRATT bit = 0), the NVM Set Identifier field in all commands and data structures must be cleared to 0h. ## Key Tables | Admin Command | Details | | :--- | :--- | | Identify | • Identify Namespace includes NVM Set Identifier.
• NVM Set List includes NVM Set attributes. | | Capacity Management | • Create NVM Set returns NVM Set Identifier.
• Delete NVM Set includes NVM Set Identifier. | | Namespace Management | • Create action includes NVM Set Identifier. | | Get Features and Set Features | • Read Recovery Level, Predictable Latency Mode Config, and Window features include NVM Set Identifier. | | Connect | • Connect command includes NVM Set Identifier. | | Create I/O Submission Queue | • Create Submission Queue includes NVM Set Identifier. | | Get Log Page | • Predictable Latency Per NVM Set log page includes NVM Set Identifier. | *Figure 68: NVM Set Aware Admin Commands*

sections.title: Endurance_Groups
sections.summary:
# 3.2.3 Endurance_Groups

Endurance is managed within a single NVM Set or across multiple NVM Sets. Each NVM Set is associated with an Endurance Group. If two or more NVM Sets share the same Endurance Group Identifier (EGID), endurance is managed across them. If only one NVM Set has a specific EGID, endurance is managed locally to that NVM Set.

If NVM Sets are not supported, endurance is managed:
- Within each Endurance Group (if supported),
- Or within the domain (if Endurance Groups are not supported).

An Endurance Group is part of only one domain. The EGID is a 16-bit value, unique within the NVM subsystem. EGID value `0h` is reserved and invalid. If a host specifies EGID `0h` in a command requiring it, the command aborts with **Invalid Field in Command** status.

Endurance Group information is described in the **Endurance Group Information log page** (section 5.2.12.1.10).

**Figure 69** illustrates that:
- NVM Sets A and B are managed together under Endurance Group Y.
- NVM Set C is managed independently under Endurance Group Z.

If Endurance Groups are supported:
- The NVM subsystem and all controllers must:
  - Indicate support in the **Controller Attributes** field (Identify Controller).
  - Indicate the EGID in the **Identify Namespace** data structure.
  - Support the **Endurance Group Information log page**.
  - Support the **Endurance Group Event Aggregate log page** if more than one EGID is supported.

If Endurance Groups are not supported:
- The controller ignores the EGID field in commands (e.g., Get Log Page).
- Host-reported EGID fields are cleared to `0h`.

sections.title: Configuring_and_Managing_Endurance_Group_Events
sections.summary:
**3.2.3.1 Configuring and Managing Endurance Group Events**

The host configures asynchronous events for an Endurance Group using a **Set Features** command with the **Endurance Group Event Configuration** feature (Section 5.2.26.1.16), specifying the Endurance Group and desired events that trigger entries in the **Endurance Group Event Aggregate log page** (Section 5.2.12.1.15). This command must be issued per Endurance Group.

To receive notifications when entries are added to the log page, the host sets the **Endurance Group Event Aggregate Log Change Notices** bit to ‘1’ in a **Set Features** command using the **Asynchronous Event Configuration** feature (Section 5.2.26.1.5), triggering a **Endurance Group Event Aggregate Log Page Change Notice** event.

To detect outstanding events, the host reads the **Endurance Group Event Aggregate log page**, which returns an entry for each Endurance Group with an event. The maximum number of entries is determined by the **Endurance Group Identifier Maximum** value in the **Identify Controller** data structure.

To identify the specific event(s) for a reported Endurance Group, the host reads the **Endurance Group Information log page** (Figure 222). The **Critical Warning** field indicates the event(s), such as all namespaces in the group being placed in read-only mode. Events are cleared for a given Endurance Group if the **Get Log Page** command reads the log page with the **Retain Asynchronous Event** bit set to ‘0’. If the **Critical Warning** field is 0h, no events are reported in the Event Aggregate log page.

sections.title: Reclaim_Groups,_Reclaim_Unit_Handles,_and_Reclaim
sections.summary:
# 3.2.4 Reclaim Groups, Reclaim Unit Handles, and Reclaim Units

If Flexible Data Placement (FDP) is enabled in an Endurance Group (see Section 5.2.26.1.20), the logical view of non-volatile storage consists of:

- **Reclaim Groups**: One or more groups numbered from 0 to P−1, where P is the value of the *Number of Reclaim Groups* field in the FDP Configuration Descriptor (Figure 287). Each Reclaim Group contains one or more Reclaim Units.
- **Reclaim Unit Handles**: One or more handles numbered from 0 to N−1, where N is the value of the *Number of Reclaim Unit Handles* field in the FDP Configuration Descriptor (Figure 287).

A **Reclaim Unit Handle** references a Reclaim Unit in each Reclaim Group where user data from a write command is placed. A Reclaim Unit can be referenced by at most one Reclaim Unit Handle at any time. However, when a Reclaim Unit is reused (e.g., after being erased), it may be referenced by the same or different Reclaim Unit Handles.

When a Reclaim Unit is written to capacity, the controller updates the associated Reclaim Unit Handle to reference a different empty Reclaim Unit (i.e., a reclaimed and erased unit ready for writing). This behavior is detailed in Section 8.1.11.

*Figure 70*: Flexible Data Placement Logical View of Non-Volatile Storage (see image).

sections.title: Domains_and_Divisions
sections.summary:
**3.2.5 Domains and Divisions**
