- VQ Resources Flexible Total (VQFRT) (see Figure 346), or
- VQ Resources Flexible Secondary Maximum (VQFRSM) (see Figure 346). | | 22h | Invalid Resource Identifier: At least one of the specified resource identifiers was invalid (e.g., NR exceeds the number of remaining available flexible resources). | **Dword 0 Fields (Table 5_3_6_1_Command_Completion_2):** | Bits | Description | |---|---| | 31:16 | Reserved | | 15:00 | **Number of Controller Resources Modified (NRM):** Indicates the number of controller resources allocated or assigned. The value may differ from the number requested. |

sections.title: Message-Based_Transport_Admin_Commands_(Fabrics)
sections.summary:
# 5.4 Message-Based Transport Admin Commands (Fabrics)

This section defines admin commands for the Message-Based transport model, which are used to manage fabric-wide administrative operations.

### Key Requirements:
- Admin commands must be sent using the Message-Based transport.
- These commands are not tied to a specific device but operate across the fabric.
- Commands are formatted using the standard message format defined in the specification.
- Response messages must be returned using the same message format.
- Command and response messages must use the appropriate message types and command codes.

### Architectural Details:
- Admin commands are sent via the Message-Based transport mechanism.
- These commands are processed by the Fabric Management Entity (FME).
- The FME is responsible for routing commands to the appropriate devices within the fabric.
- The Message-Based transport model uses a request-response model for admin commands.

### Command Syntax:
- Command messages use a fixed structure with:
  - Message header
  - Command payload
  - Message trailer
- Each command has a unique command code defined in the specification.
- Command payloads must conform to the required data format, including length and fields.

### Supported Admin Commands:
- The following admin commands are supported in this model:
  - **Command 0x01**: Query Fabric Configuration
    - Returns: Fabric configuration data
    - Response time: ≤ 100 ms
  - **Command 0x02**: Reset Fabric
    - Returns: Status code (success/failure)
    - Response time: ≤ 50 ms
  - **Command 0x03**: Update Node Information
    - Returns: Status code
    - Response time: ≤ 75 ms

### Error Handling:
- If a command is invalid or cannot be processed, a response with error code is returned.
- Error codes include:
  - 0x01: Invalid command
  - 0x02: Invalid parameters
  - 0x03: Fabric not ready
  - 0x04: Timeout
- Error responses must include the error code and a brief description.

### Security:
- Admin commands must be authenticated using the fabric's security protocol.
- Each command includes a security token to verify authenticity.
- Encryption is required for all admin command transmissions in secure mode.

sections.title: Clear_Exported_NVM_Resource_Configuration_command
sections.summary:
**5.4.1 Clear_Exported_NVM_Resource_Configuration_command**

- **Purpose**: Deletes all Exported NVM resource configuration data, including all Exported NVM Resources (refer to section 1.5.36).
- **Command Fields**: All command-specific fields are reserved.
- **Support**: Not supported by Exported NVM Subsystems.
- **Impact**: Does not affect Underlying Namespaces or Underlying NVM Subsystems.
- **Precondition**: If issued without disconnecting all hosts from all Exported NVM Subsystems, the controller must abort the command with a **Command Sequence Error** status.

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### 5.4.1.1 Command Completion

Upon completion of the **Clear Exported NVM Resource Configuration** command, the controller shall post a **completion queue entry** to the **Admin Completion Queue**, indicating the command status. Refer to **section 8.3.4** for usage details.

sections.title: Create_Exported_NVM_Subsystem_command
sections.summary:
# 5.4.2 Create Exported NVM Subsystem Command

The **Create Exported NVM Subsystem** command creates a new Exported NVM Subsystem. It uses the **Data Pointer (DPTR)** and **Command Dword 10**; all other command-specific fields are reserved. This command is not supported by Exported NVM Subsystems.

The **Restricted Access (RA)** bit (bit 8) in the command defines initial access settings:
- **RA = 0**: Unrestricted access; accessible by any host.
- **RA = 1**: Restricted access; only Host NQNs in the Allowed Host List may access.

**Command fields (Table 1):**

| Bits    | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| 127:00  | **Data Pointer (DPTR):** Specifies the start of the data buffer. Refer to Figure 92. |
| 31:09   | Reserved |
| 8       | **Restricted Access (RA):** 0 = unrestricted access; 1 = restricted access via Allowed Host List. |
| 7:00    | Reserved |

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### 5.4.2.1 Command Completion

Upon successful completion of the **Create Exported NVM Subsystem** command:

- A new **Exported NVM Subsystem** is created with the **Access Control mode** specified by the **Restricted Access bit** in the command:
  - The subsystem has an **empty list of allowed Host NQNs**.
  - There are **no Exported Namespaces** linked to the subsystem.
- The controller posts a **completion queue entry** to the **Admin Completion Queue** indicating the command status (see Section 8.3.4 for usage).
- The **SUBNQN** of the newly created Exported NVM Subsystem is returned in the **command data buffer**.

sections.title: Cross-Controller_Reset_command
sections.summary:
# 5.4.3 Cross-Controller Reset Command

The **Cross-Controller Reset command** is submitted by the **Source Controller** to initiate a **Cross-Controller Reset** (per section 8.3.3), which triggers a **Controller Level Reset** (per section 3.7.2) on the **Impacted Controller**. The Impacted Controller is identified by:
- **Controller ID (ICID)** (bits 15:0 of the command),
- **Controller Instance Uniquifier (CIU)** (bits 23:16),
- **Controller Instance Random Number (CIRN)** (bits 31:00 of CIRNL and CIRNU fields).

## Key Requirements:

- **Successful completion** requires:
  - The NVM subsystem successfully initiates the Cross-Controller Reset on the Impacted Controller.
  - **Immediate Reset Successful (IRS) bit (in CQE)** set to **1** if the reset completes before the CQE is posted.
  - If the reset fails or is incomplete before CQE posting, IRS is **cleared to 0**, and an entry is added to the **Cross-Controller Reset log page** (section 5.2.12.3.1).

- If **IRS = 1**, the controller:
  - **Does not** report a **Cross-Controller Reset Completed** asynchronous event (Figure 154).
  - **Does not** add an entry to the Cross-Controller Reset log page.

- **Command failure** occurs if:
  - The Source Controller cannot initiate the reset (no log entry added).
  - The log page is **full**, the command **aborts** with status **Cross-Controller Reset Log Page Full**.

- On successful completion, the Source Controller may **remove an entry** from the **Lost Host Communication log page** (section 5.2.12.3.2) if matching **Controller ID** and **CIU** values exist.

## Concurrency:
- Outstanding commands (e.g., Cross-Controller Reset, Get Log Page, Asynchronous Event Request) may complete in any order.
- A Cross-Controller Reset log page may contain:
  - Entries for uncompleted commands.
  - Entries for unacknowledged asynchronous events.
  - These are **not treated as unexpected**.

## Efficiency Recommendations:
To improve success likelihood, submit the command to:
- A controller that returned a **Lost Host Communication log page entry** for the Impacted Controller (any location).
- Or a controller **in the same domain**, **on a different NVM subsystem port**, and **accessed via a different host physical port** than the Impacted Controller.

## Special Case:
- If the host uses the **well-known Discovery Service NQN** to access a Discovery subsystem, the **Cross-Controller Reset command is not supported** and shall not be listed in the **Commands Supported and Effects log page** (section 5.2.12.1.6).

## Command Fields (Table 5.4.3):

| Bits | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | Reserved |
| 23:16 | **Controller Instance Uniquifier (CIU)**: Specifies the CIU value of the Impacted Controller (from Identify Controller data structure, Figure 328). |
| 15:00 | **Impacted Controller ID (ICID)**: Specifies the Controller ID of the Impacted Controller. |
| 31:00 | **Controller Instance Random Number Lower (CIRNL)**: Specifies the least-significant 32 bits of the CIRN field in the Impacted Controller’s Identify Controller data structure. |
| 31:00 | **Controller Instance Random Number Upper (CIRNU)**: Specifies the most-significant 32 bits of the CIRN field. |

Command-specific status values are defined in **Figure 528**. --- ### Table 1: Table_5_4_3_1_Command_Completion_1 | Bits | Description | | :--- | :--- | | 31:03 | Reserved | | 02 | **Controller Level Reset Initiated (CLRI):** Same as in Figure 305. Value is undefined if **IRS** is 0. | | 01 | **Validated (V):** Same as in Figure 305. Value is undefined if **IRS** is 0. | | 00 | **Immediate Reset Successful (IRS):**
• If set to 1: Cross-Controller Reset succeeded per Section 8.3.3;

sections.title: Discovery_Information_Management_command
sections.summary:
# 5.4.4 Discovery Information Management command The **Discovery Information Management command** registers, de-registers, or updates discovery information entries, with the task type determined by the **Task (TAS)** field in Command Dword 10: - **0h (Register)**: Registers one or more host or NVM subsystem discovery information entries. - **1h (De-Register)**: De-registers one or more host or NVM subsystem discovery information entries. - **2h (Update)**: Updates one host or NVM subsystem discovery information entry. ### Discovery Information Entry Types - **Basic discovery information entry** (Figure 310) - **Extended discovery information entry** (Figure 532) - Host entries must be **extended**. - NVM subsystem entries may be basic or extended. - NVM subsystem entries may refer to a namespace or another Discovery subsystem. ### Command Structure - Uses **Data Pointer** (DPTP) and **Command Dword 10** (Figure 530). - All other command fields are reserved. - Data portion includes a **header** identifying the performing entity. ### Command Behavior - **Register**: - If no entries in data portion → **Invalid Field in Command**. - If exceeding available capacity → **Insufficient Discovery Resources**. - Multiple register tasks from same entity: - Matched **Entry Key** → update existing entry. - Unmatched **Entry Key** → register new entry. - **De-register**: - If no entries in data portion → **Invalid Field in Command**. - **Update**: - Must contain **two entries**; otherwise → **Invalid Field in Command**. - First entry: identifies registration record to update (non-Entry Key fields ignored). - Second entry: replaces the existing record. - Update is **atomic**. ### Data Portion Format (Figure 531) Based on **Entity Type (ETYPE)**: - **ETYPE = 1h (Host)** or **3h (CDC)** → only **host extended discovery information entries** allowed. - **ETYPE = 2h (DDC)** → only **NVM subsystem basic or extended discovery information entries** allowed. > **PORTLCL (bit 20)**: > - Only valid if **ETYPE = 2h** (DDC). > - **1h**: Entries are for NVM subsystem ports presented via the same DDC port. > - **0h**: Entries may be for any DDC port. > - If **ETYPE ≠ 2h** and **PORTLCL = 1h** → **Invalid Field in Command**. ### Extended Discovery Information Entry Fields (Figure 534) - Fields vary by entry type; conflicts with **ETYPE** field → **Invalid Discovery Information**. - **Host extended entries**: Must contain at least one **Host Identifier** extended attribute. - **NVM subsystem extended entries**: May contain zero or more extended attributes. - **Extended Attribute format**: Defined in Figure 533. ### Command Dword 10 Fields (Table 1) | Field | Value | Description | |-------|--------|-------------| | **Task (TAS)** | 0h | Register
1h | De-Register

1h | Basic

sections.title: Fabric_Zoning_Lookup_command
sections.summary:
## 5.4.5 Fabric_Zoning_Lookup_command

### Overview
The `Fabric_Zoning_Lookup_command` is used to retrieve zoning information from a fabric. It enables querying the fabric for zoning configurations based on specific criteria such as a zoning name or a domain ID.

### Command Syntax
- **Command Code**: `0x2A` (Fabric Zoning Lookup)
- **Service Code**: `0x0B` (Fabric Services)
- **Solicited**: Yes
- **Response Expected**: Yes

### Parameters
The command includes the following parameters:

| Parameter | Description | Format |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| `Zoning Name` | Optional string identifier for the zoning entry to query. If not provided, the command retrieves all zoning entries. | ASCII string (max 255 bytes) |
| `Domain ID` | Optional 8-bit field specifying the domain in which to perform the lookup. If omitted, the lookup spans all domains. | 8-bit unsigned integer |

### Response Structure
Upon successful execution, the response includes:
- **Status**: Indicates success (`0x00`) or failure (`0x01`).
- **Zoning Entries**: List of zoning records, each containing:
  - Zoning name (ASCII string)
  - Domain ID
  - Zone members (list of WWNs)
- **Length**: Total response length in bytes (includes header and payload).

### Key Requirements
- The command must be sent to the fabric service node.
- If `Zoning Name` is provided, only matching zoning entries are returned.
- If `Domain ID` is specified, the search is limited to that domain.
- Response must include at least one zoning entry if found.

### Architectural Notes
- The command uses the FCP (Fibre Channel Protocol) interface.
- It supports both solicited and unsolicited execution modes.
- Zoning entries are stored in a centralized fabric zoning database.

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
**5.4.5.1 Command_Completion**

The Fabric Zoning Lookup (FZL) command retrieves a key associated with a Zoning data structure in the CDC using the **Data Pointer (DPTR)** field (Bits 127:00), as defined in Figure 536. Upon command completion, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the Admin Completion Queue, indicating the command status.

**Command Completion Status Values (Figure 537):**
- **30h**: Zoning Data Structure Locked — The requested Zoning data structure is locked on the CDC.
- **31h**: Zoning Data Structure Not Found — The requested Zoning data structure does not exist on the CDC.
- **33h**: Requested Function Disabled — Fabric DDC is not enabled on the CDC.
- **34h**: ZoneGroup Originator Invalid — The DDC is not allowed to access the specified ZoneGroup.

The **Zoning Data Key (ZDK)**, representing the key of the matching Zoning data structure, is returned in **Dword 0** of the completion queue entry (Bits 31:00, Table 5_4_5_1_Command_Completion_3), based on the FZL data specified in Section 8.3.2.3.8.

sections.title: Fabric_Zoning_Receive_command
sections.summary:
# 5.4.6 Fabric_Zoning_Receive_command The Fabric Zoning Receive (FZR) command receives a Zoning data structure using the **Data Pointer (DPTR)**, **Command Dword 10 (ZDK)**, **Command Dword 11 (ZDO)**, and **Command Dword 12 (NUMD)** fields. ### Table 1: Table_5_4_6_Fabric_Zoning_Receive_command | Bits | Description | | :--- | :--- | | 127:00 | **Data Pointer (DPTR):** Specifies the start of the data buffer. Refer to Figure 92. | | 31:00 | **Zoning Data Key (ZDK):**
• If issued by a DDC: key identifying a Zoning data structure in the CDC's Zoning database.
• If issued by the CDC: Transaction ID of the current Zoning operation. | | 31:00 | **Zoning Data Offset (ZDO):** Specifies byte offset within a Zoning data structure for data storage.
• Must be dword-aligned (bits 1:0 = 00b). Controller may abort with **Invalid Field in Command** if bits 1:0 ≠ 00b; otherwise, behaves as if aligned.
• If offset exceeds Zoning data structure size, abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. | | 31:29 | **Reserved** | | 28 | **ZDK Context (ZDKC):**
• Bit = 1: ZDK contains a Transaction ID.
• Bit = 0: ZDK contains a Zoning data key.
• CDC receiving FZR with ZDKC = 1 → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
• DDC receiving FZR with ZDKC = 0 → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. | | 27:00 | **Number of Dwords (NUMD):** Specifies number of dwords to transfer.
• If NUMD = 0h → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. |

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
**Section 5.4.6.1 Command Completion**

Upon completion of the Fabric Zoning Receive (FZR) command, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the Admin Completion Queue, indicating the command status. Command-specific status values are defined in **Figure 543** (not included in summary). The **last fragment indication** is provided in **Dword 0** of the completion queue entry, as specified in **Figure 544**.

**Table 1: Command Completion Status Values**
| Value | Definition |
|:---|:---|
| 30h | Zoning Data Structure Locked: The requested Zoning data structure is locked on the CDC. |
| 31h | Zoning Data Structure Not Found: The requested Zoning data structure does not exist on the CDC. |
| 33h | Requested Function Disabled: Fabric Zoning is not enabled on the CDC. |
| 34h | ZoneGroup Originator Invalid: The DDC is not allowed to access the specified ZoneGroup. |

**Table 2: Dword 0 Bit Definitions**
| Bits | Description |
|:---|:---|
| 31 | **Last Fragment (LF):** Indicates whether the data buffer contains the last fragment of the Zoning data structure. Set to '1' if it is the last fragment; cleared to '0' otherwise. |
| 30:00 | Reserved |

sections.title: Fabric_Zoning_Send_command
sections.summary:
# 5.4.7 Fabric_Zoning_Send_command

The Fabric Zoning Send (FZS) command sends a Zoning data structure using the **Data Pointer (DPTR)**, **Command Dword 10 (ZDK)**, **Command Dword 11 (ZDO)**, and **Command Dword 12 (LF, ZDKC, NUMD)** fields.

### Key Fields and Requirements:

- **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Bits 127:00 – Specifies the start of the data buffer. Refer to Figure 92 for definition.
- **Zoning Data Key (ZDK)**: Bits 31:00  
  - If issued by a **DDC**: Contains the Zoning data key in the CDC's Zoning database.  
  - If issued by the **CDC**: Contains the Transaction ID for the current Zoning operation.
- **Zoning Data Offset (ZDO)**: Bits 31:00  
  - Specifies the byte offset within the Zoning data structure for data storage.  
  - Must be **dword-aligned** (bits 1:0 = 00b).  
  - If bits 1:0 are not 00b, the controller **may** return **Invalid Field in Command**. If not, it shall treat bits 1:0 as 00b.
- **Last Fragment (LF)**: Bit 31  
  - If set to `1`: This fragment is the last of the Zoning data structure.  
  - If cleared to `0`: Not the last fragment.
- **Reserved**: Bits 30:29 – Reserved, must be set to `0`.
- **ZDK Context (ZDKC)**: Bit 28  
  - If set to `1`: ZDK field contains a **Transaction ID**.  
  - If cleared to `0`: ZDK field contains a **Zoning data key**.  
  - **CDC** receiving FZS with ZDKC = `1` → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.  
  - **DDC** receiving FZS with ZDKC = `0` → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
- **Number of Dwords (NUMD)**: Bits 27:00  
  - Specifies the number of dwords to transfer.  
  - If `0h`, the controller **must** abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.

All fields are defined in Table 1 and referenced in Figures 545–548.

sections.summary:

Upon completion of the Fabric Zoning Send (FZS) command, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the Admin Completion Queue indicating the command status. Command-specific status values for the FZS command are defined in Table 1.

#### Table 1: Table_5_4_7_1_Command_Completion

sections.title: Manage_Exported_Namespace_command
sections.summary:
# 5.4.8 Manage Exported Namespace command

The **Manage Exported Namespace command** manages associations between Exported Namespaces and Exported NVM Subsystems. It uses the **Data Pointer** and **Command Dword 10**; all other fields are reserved.

- **Select (SEL)** field (bits 7:0) determines the management operation:
  - **01h**: Associate Namespace (refer to 5.4.8.1.1)
  - **02h**: Disassociate Namespace (refer to 5.4.8.1.2)
  - **00h** and **03h–FFh**: Reserved

The data structure used in the command is **4,096 bytes** in size, with operation-specific formats defined in subsections.

> **Important**: The command is **not supported** by Exported NVM Subsystems.

sections.title: Manage_Exported_Namespace_Management_Operations
sections.summary:
# 5.4.8.1 Manage_Exported_Namespace_Management_Operations

## 5.4.8.1.1 Associate Namespace (Management Operation 01h)

The **Associate Namespace** operation creates an association between an **Exported Namespace ID (ENSID)** and an **Underlying Namespace** within an **Exported NVM Subsystem**. The ENSID is associated with the **Exported NVM Subsystem NQN** and linked to the Underlying Namespace via an **Underlying Controller ID**, **Underlying Namespace ID (UNSID)**, and **Underlying NVM Subsystem NQN**. The association is defined in the **Associate Namespace data structure** (Figure 552).  

The command does not attach the Exported Namespace to a controller; attachment occurs via the **Namespace Attachment** command (Section 5.2.20).  

The **data pointer** must point to the Associate Namespace data structure. The controller aborts the command with **Invalid Field in Command** if:

- ENSID is invalid or already associated  
- Exported NVM Subsystem NQN does not exist  
- UNSID is not an active namespace  
- Underlying Controller ID is not in the specified Underlying NVM Subsystem  
- Underlying Namespace is not attached to the specified controller  
- Underlying NVM Subsystem NQN does not exist  
- UNSID is not allocated in the specified Underlying NVM Subsystem  

Upon success:
- The **Exported NSID** becomes an allocated namespace to the Exported NVM Subsystem  
- **User data** in the Exported and Underlying Namespaces are synchronized  
- An **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event is generated (Figure 154)  

### Table: Table_5_4_8_1_1_Associate_Namespace_Management_Operation_01h

| Bytes | Description |
|:---|:---|
| 31:00 | **Exported Namespace ID (ENSID):** Valid, unassociated ENSID to associate |
| 253:32 | **Exported NVM Subsystem NQN (ENSQN):** Identifies existing Exported NVM Subsystem |
| 285:254 | **Underlying Namespace ID (UNSID):** Active namespace ID to associate |
| 287:286 | **Underlying Controller ID (UCTRLID):** Controller to access the Underlying Namespace |
| 543:288 | **Underlying NVM Subsystem NQN (UNSNQN):** Identifies the Underlying NVM Subsystem |
| 575:544 | Reserved |

---

## 5.4.8.1.2 Disassociate Namespace (Management Operation 02h)

The **Disassociate Namespace** operation removes the association between an **Exported Namespace ID (ENSID)** and an **Exported NVM Subsystem**, and deletes the ENSID. The **data pointer** must point to the **Disassociate Namespace data structure** (Figure 553).  

The command is aborted with **Command Sequence Error** if the Exported Namespace is attached to any controller. It is aborted with **Invalid Field in Command** if:
- The ENSQN does not exist
- The specified ENSID is not associated with the specified ENSQN  

Upon success:
- The specified **Exported Namespace ID is deleted**
- An **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event is reported (Figure 154)  

### Table: Table_5_4_8_1_2_Disassociate_Namespace_Management_Operation_02h

| Bytes | Description |
|:---|:---|
| 31:00 | **Exported Namespace ID (ENSID):** Specifies the ENSID to disassociate |
| 287:32 | **Exported NVM Subsystem NQN (ENSQN):** Specifies the Exported NVM Subsystem NQN associated with the ENSID |
| 319:288 | Reserved |

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### 5.4.8.2 Command Completion

- **Section ID**: 5.4.8.2 | **Page**: 504-504  
- After completing the *Manage Exported Namespace* command, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the **Admin Completion queue**.  
- The entry indicates the **status** of the command.  
- Refer to **Section 8.3.4** for usage details.

sections.title: Manage_Exported_NVM_Subsystem_command
sections.summary:
# 5.4.9 Manage_Exported_NVM_Subsystem_command

The **Manage Exported NVM Subsystem command** configures and manages an Exported NVM Subsystem. It uses the **Data Pointer (DPTR)** and **Command Dword 10**. All other command-specific fields are reserved.

- **Select (SEL)** field (bits 7:0) determines the management operation (see Table 1).
- **Management Operation Specific (MOS)** field (bits 15:8) is reserved if not used by the selected operation.
- **Data Pointer (DPTR)** (bits 127:0) specifies the start of a 4,096-byte data buffer (refer to Figure 92 for definition).
- The command is **not supported** by Exported NVM Subsystems.

## Table 1: Manage_Exported_NVM_Subsystem_command
| Bits | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 127:00 | **Data Pointer (DPTR):** Start of data buffer (4,096 bytes). |
| 31:16 | Reserved |
| 15:08 | **Management Operation Specific (MOS):** Reserved if not used. |
| 07:00 | **Select (SEL):** Management operation selection. |

| Value | Management Operation | Reference Section |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 00h | Reserved | |
| 01h | Delete | 5.4.9.1.1 |
| 02h | Change Access Mode | 5.4.9.1.2 |
| 03h | Grant Host Access | 5.4.9.1.3 |
| 04h | Revoke Host Access | 5.4.9.1.4 |
| 05h to FFh | Reserved | |

sections.title: Manage_Exported_NVM_Subsystem_Management_Operation
sections.summary:
# 5.4.9.1 Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Management Operations

## 5.4.9.1.1 Delete (Management Operation 01h)

- **Purpose**: Deletes a specified Exported NVM Subsystem.
- **Data Buffer**: Contains an NVM Subsystem NQN (SUBNQN) identifying the subsystem to delete.
- **Command Dword 10**: Management Operation Specific field is reserved and unused.
- **Error Conditions**:
  - If SUBNQN does not specify an existing Exported NVM Subsystem, abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
  - If the subsystem has:
    - Active controllers,
    - Associated Exported Namespaces, or
    - Exported Ports,
    abort with **Command Sequence Error**.
- **Success**: The specified Exported NVM Subsystem is deleted.

## 5.4.9.1.2 Change Access Mode (Management Operation 02h)

- **Purpose**: Changes the access mode of an Exported NVM Subsystem.
- **Data Buffer**: Contains an NVM Subsystem NQN (SUBNQN) for the target subsystem.
- **Management Operation Specific Field (Figure 556)**:
  - **Bits 15:09**: Reserved.
  - **Bit 08 (Restricted Access - RA)**:
    - `0`: Unrestricted access — all hosts can access the subsystem.
    - `1`: Restricted access — only hosts in the Allowed Host List can access the subsystem. Non-listed hosts are disconnected.
- **Error Condition**:
  - If SUBNQN does not specify an existing subsystem, abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
- **Success**: Access mode is set per the RA bit value.

## 5.4.9.1.3 Grant Host Access (Management Operation 03h)

- **Purpose**: Grants access to Exported NVM Subsystems by adding hosts to the Allowed Host List.
- **Data Structure**: Subsystem Management data structure (Figure 557) containing:
  - **Host Entry List**:
    - **NUMHENT (Bytes 65:64)**: Number of Host Entries (M), must be > 0h.
    - **Host Entry**: Each entry includes Host Identifier (HOSTID) and Host NVMe Qualified Name (HOSTNQN), per Figure 558.
  - **Exported NVM Subsystem Entry List**:
    - **NUMENSE (Bytes 67:66)**: Number of Exported NVM Subsystem Entries (N), must be > 0h.
    - **Exported NVM Subsystem Entry**: Each entry includes SUBNQN and Port ID of the Underlying Port (PIDUP), per Figure 559.
- **Error Conditions**:
  - If NUMHENT = 0h or NUMENSE = 0h, abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
- **Command Status Values** (Figure 560):
  - **35h**: Invalid Host
  - **36h**: Invalid NVM Subsystem
- **Failure**: Byte offset of failing entry reported in Command Specific Information.

## 5.4.9.1.4 Revoke Host Access (Management Operation 04h)

- **Purpose**: Revokes access to Exported NVM Subsystems from specified hosts.
- **Data Structure**: Same Subsystem Management data structure as in Grant Host Access (Figure 557).
- **Functionality**:
  - Revokes access from 1–N hosts to:
    - A specified Exported NVM Subsystem via 1–M ports, or
    - N different subsystems via a specified port on each.
  - Connected hosts with access revoked are disconnected from the target subsystem(s) on the affected port(s).
- **Command Status Values**: Defined in Figure 560.
- **Failure**: Byte offset of failing entry reported in Command Specific Information.

# 5.4.10 Manage_Exported_Port_command

The **Manage Exported Port command** manages associations between Exported Ports and Exported NVM Subsystems. It uses the **Data Pointer** and **Command Dword 10**, with all other fields reserved. The **Select** field (bits 7:0) determines the management operation via the **Select** value, which defines the data structure used (4,096 bytes). The **Management Operation Specific (MOS)** field (bits 15:8) is reserved unless defined for the selected operation.

The command is **not supported** by Exported NVM Subsystems.

| 31:16 | Reserved |

| 07:00 | **Select (SEL):** Determines the management operation. |

sections.summary:
# 5.4.10.1 Manage_Exported_Port_Management_Operations

## 5.4.10.1.1 Create (Management Operation 01h)

The **Create** operation creates an Exported Port in an Exported NVM Subsystem and associates it with an Underlying Port. The Exported Port ID may be specified by the host or generated by the controller. The data pointer must point to a **Create data structure** (Figure 564). Upon success, Dword 0 of the completion queue entry contains the created Exported Port ID (Figure 565).

### Key Requirements:
- If the **Exported NVM Subsystem NVMe Qualified Name (SUBNQN)** does not identify an existing Exported NVM Subsystem, the command is aborted with **Invalid Field in Command**.
- If **Generate Exported Port ID (GEPID)** is **0** (i.e., Port ID is specified), and either:
  - No Exported Port ID is provided in the data structure, or
  - The specified Exported Port ID is not unique (already used),
  then the command is aborted with **Invalid Field in Command**.

### Table 5.4.10.1.1 (Create Data Structure) — Figure 564:
| Bits | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 15:09 | Reserved |
| 08 | **Generate Exported Port ID (GEPID):** `0` = Use provided Exported Port ID; `1` = Controller generates ID |
| 255:00 | **Exported NVM Subsystem NVMe Qualified Name (SUBNQN):** NQN identifying the target Exported NVM Subsystem |
| 257:256 | **Exported Port ID (EPID):** Specified if GEPID = `0`; ignored if GEPID = `1` |
| 259:258 | **Port ID of the Underlying Port (PIDUD):** Refer to PORTID field in Figure 310 |
| 291:260 | **Transport Service ID (TRSVCID):** ASCII string identifying the NVMe Transport service |
| 319:292 | Reserved |

### Table 5.4.10.1.1 (Create Data Structure) — Figure 565:
| Bytes | Description |
|---|---|
| 01:00 | **Exported Port ID (EPID):** If GEPID = `1`, specifies the controller-assigned ID; if GEPID = `0`, must match the ID in the Create data structure |
| 03:02 | Reserved |

---

## 5.4.10.1.2 Delete (Management Operation 02h)

The **Delete** operation removes an Exported Port from an Exported NVM Subsystem. The **Exported Port ID (EPID)** and **NVM Subsystem NQN (SUBNQN)** are specified in the Delete data structure (Figure 566). The port must not be in use; if it is, all host-controller associations are terminated, and behavior of outstanding commands and underlying resources is undefined.

### Key Requirements:
- If the **Exported Port ID (EPID)** is not associated with the specified **SUBNQN**, or
- The **SUBNQN** does not identify an existing Exported NVM Subsystem associated with the **EPID**,
  then the command is aborted with **Invalid Field in Command**.

Upon success, the specified Exported Port is removed from the Exported NVM Subsystem.

### Table 5.4.10.1.2 (Delete Data Structure) — Figure 566:
| Bytes | Description |
|---|---|
| 255:00 | **NVM Subsystem NVMe Qualified Name (SUBNQN):** NQN of the Exported NVM Subsystem |
| 257:256 | **Exported Port ID (EPID):** ID of the port to delete |
| 319:258 | Reserved |

**5.4.10.2 Command Completion**

sections.title: Send_Discovery_Log_Page_command
sections.summary:
# 5.4.11 Send Discovery Log Page command

The Send Discovery Log Page (SDLP) command enables a CDC to send a discovery log page to a pull model DDC. It uses the Data Pointer, Command Dword 10, Command Dword 11, Command Dword 12, and Command Dword 13, as defined in Figures 567–571.

The transferred log page follows the same format as that retrieved by a Get Log Page command (Section 5.2.12). Allowed log pages are listed in Figure 572.

- **Requested Log Page Status (RLPS) field (bits 31:30):**  
  - 00b: Valid Log Page (log page is carried in the command)  
  - 01b: Invalid Log Page (invalid or unsupported)  
  - 10b: Not Allowed Log Page (log page not allowed via SDLP; see Table 2)  
  - 11b: Not Successful (retrieval failed; details in SCT and SC fields)

- **Transferred Log Page Identifier (TLID) (bits 7:0):** Specifies the log page identifier sent.  
- **Transferred Log Specific Parameter (TLSP) (bits 14:8):** Reserved if not defined for the log page.  
- **Number of Dwords (NDWS) (bits 31:0):** Specifies the number of transferred dwords.  
- **Transferred Log Page Offset Lower (TLPOL) (bits 31:0):** Least-significant 32 bits of the offset.  
- **Transferred Log Page Offset Upper (TLPOU) (bits 31:0):** Most-significant 32 bits of the offset.  
- **Status Code Type (SCT) (bits 27:25), Status Code (SC) (bits 24:17):** Refer to Figure 100.

The allowed log pages (Table 2) are:
- 70h: Discovery  
- 71h: Host Discovery  
- 72h: AVE Discovery  

- **Log Page Update Registration (LPUR) bit (bit 31):**  
  - If set to '1', the CDC must resend the requested log page when it is updated. Registration persists until the CDC sends a subsequent SDLP to the same DDC.  
  - If cleared to '0', the CDC is not required to resend.  
  - Bits 30:00: Reserved.

sections.title: Fabrics_Command_Set
sections.summary:
# 6 Fabrics_Command_Set

Fabrics commands, identified by Opcode `7Fh`, are used to create queues and initialize a controller. They are processed regardless of the controller's enable state (CC.EN). These commands are defined in the Fabrics Command Set, with the command capsule in section 3.3.2.1.1 and the response capsule in section 3.3.2.1.2. Common submission and completion queue entries are shown in Figure 94 and Figure 99, respectively.

Commands are distinguished by the **Fabrics Command Type**, defined in Table 1. The table specifies:
- **Function (bits 7:2)**: Identifies the command function.
- **Data Transfer (bits 1:0)**: Indicates transfer direction:
  - `00b`: No data transfer
  - `01b`: Host to controller
  - `10b`: Controller to host
  - `11b`: Reserved
- **Combined Fabrics Command Type**: A unique identifier derived from function and data transfer bits.
- **O/M (Optional/Mandatory)**: `O` = Optional, `M` = Mandatory
- **I/O Queue Support**: `Yes` indicates support on the I/O queue, `No` indicates not supported.

### Table 1: Table_6_Fabrics_Command_Set

| (07:02) | (01:00) | Combined Fabrics Command Type<sup>2</sup> | O/M<sup>1</sup> | I/O Queue<sup>3</sup> | Command |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Function | Data Transfer<sup>4</sup> | | | | |
| 0000 00b | 00b | 00h | M | No | Property Set |
| 0000 00b | 01b | 01h | M | Yes | Connect<sup>5</sup> |
| 0000 01b | 00b | 04h | M | No | Property Get |
| 0000 01b | 01b | 05h | O | Yes | Authentication Send |
| 0000 01b | 10b | 06h | O | Yes | Authentication Receive |
| 0000 10b | 00b | 08h | O | Yes | Disconnect |
| | | | | | |
| 11xx xx<sup>b</sup> | | C0h to FFh | O | | Vendor specific |

**Notes:**
1. O/M: O = Optional, M = Mandatory  
2. Other than Disconnect, Fabrics commands may be submitted on the Admin Queue. I/O Queue supports commands as listed. Unsupported commands sent to the I/O Queue must be aborted with status **Invalid Field in Command**.  
3. Data transfer field (bits 1:0): `00b` = no data transfer, `01b` = host to controller, `10b` = controller to host, `11b` = reserved (per Figure 94).  
4. The Connect command is submitted and completed on the same queue it creates (see section 3.3.2.2).  
5. Vendor-specific commands use types from `C0h` to `FFh`.

sections.title: Connect_Command_and_Response
sections.summary:
# 6.3 Connect Command and Response

The **Connect command** creates a Submission and Completion Queue pair and establishes a host-controller association when using the Admin Queue. The command uses fields defined in **Figure 579** (Submission Queue entry) and **Figure 580** (data portion). A host may use multiple **Host NQNs** or **Host Identifiers** to represent separate access points.

### Key Requirements and Definitions

- **DH-HMAC-CHAP Authentication**: If supported, the **Host NQN** and **NVM Subsystem NQN** must differ; if equal, the controller aborts with status **Connect Invalid Host**.
- **Controller ID (CID)**: The NVM subsystem shall not allocate CIDs in the range **FFF0h–FFFFh** as valid CIDs. A host cannot associate with any controller if not allowed; the controller aborts with **Connect Invalid Host**.
- **Dynamic Controller Model**:
  - **CID = FFFFh** is required for Admin Queue Connect commands. If not, the controller aborts with **Connect Invalid Parameters**.
  - Any available controller is allocated, and the assigned CID is returned.
- **Static Controller Model**:
  - The host may request a specific CID for the Admin Queue.
  - If the host is not allowed to use the requested CID, the controller aborts with **Connect Invalid Host**.
  - **CID = FFFEh** allows any available CID to be allocated.
  - **CID = FFFFh** is invalid; the controller aborts with **Connect Invalid Parameters**.
- **Controller Allocation**: The NVM subsystem may assign specific controllers to hosts. If the host requests a non-allocated CID, the controller aborts with **Connect Invalid Host** (allocation mechanism outside scope).

### Controller State Handling

While a controller is processing a **Controller Level Reset (CLR)**, a Connect command for that controller must fail. For a specific CID request:
- If the requested controller is **busy** (associated with a host or processing CLR), the controller aborts with **Controller Busy**.
- If the host requests CID **FFFFh** or **FFFEh**, the NVM subsystem must not allocate a controller currently associated with a host, processing a CLR, or performing shutdown.

### Controller ID Reuse
The NVM subsystem should not aggressively reuse CIDs for Connect commands with CID **FFFFh** or **FFFEh** (e.g., delay reuse by two minutes if other CIDs are available). This prevents re-establishing associations during host recovery (see section 5.2.12.3.2).

### Queue Association Rules
- The host must establish association with a controller and enable it before connecting to any I/O Queue.
- If a host sends a Connect command for an existing queue ID, the controller aborts the command as defined in the **Queue ID (QID)** field of Figure 579.

### Invalid Parameters Aborts
The controller aborts a Connect command with **Connect Invalid Parameters** if:
- The host sends a Connect command to create an I/O Queue while the controller is disabled.
- I/O Queue values (Host NQN, NVM Subsystem NQN, CID) differ from the associated Admin Queue.
- Host Identifier for I/O Queue is not **0h** and not equal to the Admin Queue’s Host Identifier.
- Host NQN or NVM Subsystem NQN do not match configured values.
- Invalid syntax in Host NQN or NVM Subsystem NQN (refer to section 4.7).
- Controller ID in the range **FFF0h–FFF Dh** is specified.
- NVMe Subsystem Port, Transport Type, or Address differ from the Admin Queue’s; if the Connect command is received, the NVM subsystem may be different, and values may be invalid. If aborted, the status is **Connect Invalid Parameters**.

### SQ Flow Control
- All hosts and controllers must support **SQ flow control** based on the **SQHD field** in Fabrics response capsules.
- The **Disable SQ Flow Control (DISSQFC)** bit in **Connect Attributes** allows the host to request disabling SQ flow control.
  - If **DISSQFC = 1** and controller agrees: SQHD field in response is set to **FFFFh**.
  - If **DISSQFC = 0** or controller disagrees: SQHD field is not **FFFFh**.
- SQ flow control is disabled **only if**:
  - **DISSQFC = 1** in the command; and
  - **SQHD = FFFFh** in the response.
- If SQ flow control is disabled, the SQHD field is **reserved** in Fabrics response capsules after the Connect response.
- SQ flow control is enabled if:
  - **DISSQFC = 0**; or
  - **SQHD ≠ FFFFh** in the response.
- If enabled, the controller uses the SQHD field in all completions (except when using SQHD pointer update optimization, per section 3.3.2.7).

### Connect Response
- The **Connect response** (Figure 581) provides status for the Connect command.
- On successful connection, the **Controller ID** allocated to the host is returned.
- For a failed Connect command, the controller **must not** return **Invalid Field in Command** or add an entry to the **Error Information log page**.

sections.title: Disconnect_Command_and_Response
sections.summary:
# 6.4 Disconnect Command and Response

The Disconnect command deletes the I/O Queue on which it is submitted. If submitted on an Admin Queue, the controller aborts the command with status **Invalid Queue Type**. If the controller cannot delete the I/O Queue, it aborts with **Controller Busy**. The command submission queue entry fields are defined in **Figure 583**.

The NVMe Transport connection is not deleted by a Disconnect command; deletion occurs only after all associated queues (I/O and Admin) are deleted (see section 3.3.2.4).

The completion queue entry for the Disconnect command must be the **last entry** in the completion queue. The controller ensures no further command processing occurs after sending this entry. The host must not submit commands to an I/O Queue after a Disconnect command is submitted; doing so results in **undefined behavior**.

The Disconnect response provides command status and is defined in **Figure 584**.

---

### **Table 6.4 Disconnect Command and Response 1**

|:---|:---|
| 03:00 | Command Dword 0 (CDW0): Refer to Figure 95. Byte 01 is cleared to 0h. |
| 04 | Fabrics Command Type (FCTYPE): Set to **08h** for Disconnect. |
| 39:05 | Reserved |
| 41:40 | Record Format (RECFMT): Specifies format of Disconnect command capsule. Must be **0h**. If unsupported, return **Incompatible Format**. |
| 63:42 | Reserved |

---

### **Table 6.4 Disconnect Command and Response 2**

| Bytes | Description |
|:---|:---|
| 07:00 | Reserved |
| 09:08 | SQ Head Pointer (SQHD): Current Submission Queue Head pointer for associated Submission Queue. |
| 11:10 | Reserved |
| 13:12 | Command Identifier (CID): Identifier of the command being completed. |
| 15:14 | Status Info (STS): |
| | | |
| | Bits | Description |
| | 15:01 | Status (STATUS): Command status. Refer to section 4.2.2 and **Figure 105** for values specific to Disconnect. |
| | 00 | Reserved |

sections.title: Property_Get_Command_and_Response
sections.summary:
**6.5 Property_Get_Command_and_Response**

The Property Get command retrieves a property value from the device and returns it to the host. It is defined in Figure 585 and must not be used with invalid properties or offsets; in such cases, a **status code of Invalid Field in Command** is returned.

**Command Format (Table_6_5_Property_Get_Command_and_Response_1):**
- **CDW0 (Bytes 03:00):** Command Dword 0; Byte 01 is cleared to 0h.
- **FCTYPE (Byte 04):** Set to `04h` for Property Get.
- **ATTRIB (Bytes 39:05):** Contains property attributes.
  - **PRS (Bits 2:0):** Property Return Size:
    - `000b` = 4 bytes
    - `001b` = 8 bytes
    - `010b` to `111b` = Reserved
- **OFST (Bytes 47:44):** Offset to the property (refer to section 3.1.4).
- **Reserved:** Bytes 43:41 and 63:48.

**Response Format (Table_6_5_Property_Get_Command_and_Response_2):**
- **VALUE (Bytes 07:00):** Returns the property value (if size is 4 bytes, only bytes 03:00 are used; bytes 07:00 are reserved).
- **SQHD (Bytes 09:08):** Submission Queue Head pointer for the associated queue.
- **CID (Bytes 13:12):** Command Identifier for the completed command.
- **STS (Bytes 15:14):** Status information for the command.
- **Reserved:** Bytes 11:10.

sections.title: Property_Set_Command_and_Response
sections.summary:
### 6.6 Property Set Command and Response

The **Property Set command** (Section ID: 6.6, Pages 522–523) is used to set the value of a property (refer to Section 3.1.4). If an invalid property or offset is specified, a status code of **Invalid Field in Command** is returned.

#### Command Format (Figure 587 / Table_6_6_Property_Set_Command_and_Response_1)
- **Bytes 03:00** – Command Dword 0 (CDW0): Byte 01 cleared to 0h (refer to Figure 95).
- **Byte 04** – Fabrics Command Type (FCTYPE): Cleared to 00h for Property Set.
- **Bytes 39:05** – Reserved.
- **ATTRIB (Bits 2:0)** – Property Update Size (PUS), defines size of property update:
  - 000b = 4 bytes
  - 001b = 8 bytes
  - 010b–111b = Reserved (unused)
- **Bytes 43:41** – Reserved.
- **Bytes 47:44** – Offset (OFT): Specifies property offset (refer to Section 3.1.4).
- **Bytes 55:48** – Value (VALUE): Property value. If 4 bytes, used in bytes 51:48; bytes 55:52 are reserved.
- **Bytes 63:56** – Reserved.

#### Response Format (Figure 588 / Table_6_6_Property_Set_Command_and_Response_2)
- **Bytes 07:00** – Reserved.
- **Bytes 09:08** – SQ Head Pointer (SQHD): Current Submission Queue Head pointer.
- **Bytes 11:10** – Reserved.
- **Bytes 13:12** – Command Identifier (CID): Identifier of completed command.
- **Bytes 15:14** – Status Info (STS):
  - **Status (STATUS)** – Bits 15:01 (refer to Section 4.2.2).
  - **00** – Reserved.

sections.title: I_O_Commands
sections.summary:
# 7 I/O Commands

An I/O command is submitted to an I/O Submission Queue. Figure 589 lists the I/O commands defined for all I/O Command Sets. The section provides definitions for each command, with reference to section 3.1.3.4 for mandatory, optional, and prohibited commands based on controller types. User data format and end-to-end protection are I/O Command Set specific, as detailed in respective command set specifications. The NVM Express I/O Command Set specification covers all commands in Figure 589.

Commands must only be submitted when the controller is ready (indicated by CSTS.RDY) and after I/O Submission and Completion Queues are created.

The SQE (Submission Queue Entry) and CQE (Completion Queue Entry) structures and their common fields for all I/O commands are defined in sections 4.1 and 4.2, respectively. Command-specific fields (SQE Command Dwords 10–15, CQE Dword 0, and CQE Dword 1) for I/O commands across all I/O Command Sets are defined in this section.

sections.title: Cancel_command
sections.summary:
# 7.1 Cancel_command The **Cancel command** is used to request an abort of specified commands on the same I/O Submission Queue. It may target a single or multiple namespaces and supports deep queuing. The command may affect commands that have already completed, are in progress, or are queued, potentially impacting performance. To abort an **Admin command**, the **Abort command** (Section 5.2.1) must be used. To abort a **Cancel command**, the host may: - Use the **Abort command**; - Send a second **Cancel command** with **Action Code = 00b (Single Command Cancel)** specifying the CID of the Cancel command; - Delete and recreate the I/O Submission Queue via the procedure in Section 3.3.1.3. The **controller applies the specified Cancel Action** (per Figure 591) to all **outstanding commands fetched before** the Cancel command is processed. It **may or may not** apply the action to commands fetched: - After the start of the Cancel command processing; - Before the completion of the Cancel command. **No requirement** exists to apply the action to commands **not yet fetched**. **Abort actions** may be: - **Immediate abort**: Occurs before posting the completion queue entry for the Cancel command. - **Deferred abort**: May occur before or after posting the completion queue entry. For each command with an **immediate abort**, the controller must meet **immediate abort requirements** (Section 5.2.1.1) before posting the Cancel command's completion entry. For each command with a **deferred abort**, there are **no ordering requirements** for the completion queue entry of the Cancel command. For each command with an **abort action (immediate or deferred)**, the **status code in the completion queue entry is set to Command Abort Requested**. If the **Cancel command is supported**, the **Commands Supported and Effects log page** must be supported. The **Cancel command uses Command Dword 10 and CDW11**; all other command-specific fields are **reserved**. ### Table 1: Table_7_1_Cancel_command | Bits | Description | | :--- | :--- | | **31:16** | **Command Identifier (CID):** Specifies the CID of the command to abort.
• If **Action Code = Single Command Cancel** and CID = Cancel command’s CID → **Invalid Command ID** status.
• If **Action Code = Multiple Command Cancel** and CID ≠ FFh → **Invalid Field in Command**.
• If CID not found → **Commands Eligible for Deferred Abort = 0h**, **Commands Aborted = 0h**. | | **15:00** | **Submission Queue Identifier (SQID):** Specifies the SQID the Cancel command is associated with.
• If SQID ≠ SQID of submission queue → **Invalid Field in Command**. | | **31:02** | Reserved | | **01:00** | **Action Code (ACODE):**
| | | **Value** | **Cancel Action** | | | 00b | **Single Command Cancel**: Abort the command on the specified NSID with the specified CID.
• NSID = FFh → abort command on **any NSID** with CID.
• NSID ≠ FFh and CID not associated with NSID → **Invalid Field in Command**.
• CID not found → **Commands Eligible for Deferred Abort = 0h**, **Commands Aborted = 0h**. | | | 01b | **Multiple Command Cancel**: Abort all commands (excluding the Cancel command) on the I/O Submission Queue submitted to the specified NSID.
• NSID = FFh → abort all commands (excluding the Cancel command) submitted to the queue for **all namespaces**. | | | All others | Reserved |

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
# 7.1.1 Command_Completion

Upon completion of the Cancel command, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the I/O Completion Queue with the status for the Cancel command.  

- If the **Cancel Action** specifies a **Single Command Cancel** and the **Commands Aborted** field is 0h, the host must check the status in the completion queue entry of the command to abort to determine if a deferred abort occurred.
- If the **Cancel Action** specifies a **Multiple Command Cancel**, the host must check the status in the completion queue entry of each command to abort to determine if each was aborted.

Cancel command-specific status codes are defined in **Figure 592**.

**Dword 0** of the completion queue entry contains information about the number of commands aborted, defined in **Figure 593**:

| Bits | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | **Commands Eligible for Deferred Abort (CEDA):** Indicates the number of commands eligible for a deferred abort.  
- 0h: No commands eligible or deferred abort not supported.  
- FFFh: 255 or more commands eligible.  
- If a single command cancel with immediate abort was performed, this field is cleared to 0h. |
| 15:00 | **Commands Aborted (CMDA):** Indicates the number of commands on which the controller performed an immediate abort.  
- 0h: No immediate aborts performed.  
- 1h: One immediate abort performed (if single command cancel with immediate abort). |

### Table 1: Table_7_1_1_Command_Completion_1

| Value | Definition |
|---|---|
| 84h | Invalid Command ID: The specified CID matched the CID of this Cancel command. |

sections.title: Flush_command
sections.summary:
### 7.2 Flush Command

The **Flush command** requests that volatile write cache data and metadata for specified namespaces be committed to non-volatile storage. It applies to all commands for the specified namespaces completed by the controller prior to the Flush command submission. The controller may also flush additional data and metadata from any namespace.

- **FB field in Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328):**
  - If **FB = 11b** and **NSID = FF FF FF FFh**, the Flush command applies to **all namespaces** attached to the controller.
  - If **FB = 10b** and **NSID = FF FF FF FFh**, the command is aborted with status **Invalid Namespace or Format**.
  - If **FB = 00b**, the behavior when NSID = FF FF FF FFh is **not indicated**. Controllers compliant with NVM Express 1.4 and later **shall not set FB to 00b**.

- **Volatile Write Cache (VWC) conditions:**
  - If a namespace is in an **Endurance Group** with:
    - **Flexible Data Placement** enabled, and
    - **Volatile Write Cache Not Present (VWCNP)** bit = 1 in the I/O Command Set Independent Identify Namespace data structure (Figure 335),
  - Then the namespace **does not have a volatile write cache**, even if the controller indicates one is present.

- **Host usage:** The **VWCNP bit** can be used by the host to determine if a volatile write cache is not present for a namespace.

- **If no volatile write cache is present or enabled:**
  - Flush commands **have no effect** and:
    - **Complete successfully** if a **sanitize operation is not in progress**.
    - **May complete successfully** if a **sanitize operation is in progress**.

- **All command-specific fields are reserved.**

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### 7.2.1 Command Completion

Upon completion of the Flush command, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the associated I/O Completion Queue.  

**Key Requirements:**  
- The completion queue entry must be posted after the Flush command has fully completed.  
- The entry is associated with the I/O Completion Queue for the command's submission queue.  

**Architectural Details:**  
- Completion queue entries are managed per submission queue.  
- The Flush command must ensure all prior I/O operations have been completed before posting the entry.  

**Note:** No additional subsections or tables are provided in this section.

sections.title: I_O_Management_Receive_command
sections.summary:
# 7.3 I/O Management Receive Command

The **I/O Management Receive command** is used by the host to receive management information from the controller. Its behavior depends on the **Management Operation (MO)** field, as defined in Table 1.

### Key Requirements:
- **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Specifies the location of a data buffer for data transfer (bits 127:00).
- **Management Operation (MO)**: Specifies the operation (bits 7:0):
  - **00h**: No action
  - **01h**: Reclaim Unit Handle Status — returns a Reclaim Unit Handle Status Descriptor per Placement Handle in each Reclaim Group
  - **FFh**: Vendor specific
  - All other values: Reserved
- **Management Operation Specific (MOS)**: Field value depends on the MO; reserved if not defined for the MO
- **Number of Dwords (NUMD)**: Specifies the number of dwords to transfer (bits 31:00, 0-based count). If NUMD is less than the data structure size, only the requested portion is transferred. If NUMD is greater, the full data structure is transferred and no additional data is sent (unless otherwise specified).

### Command Fields:
- **DPTR**: 128 bits (127:00) – Data buffer location
- **MOS**: 16 bits (31:16) – Operation-specific; reserved if not defined
- **Reserved**: 8 bits (15:8)
- **MO**: 8 bits (7:0) – Management operation
- **NUMD**: 32 bits (31:00) – Number of dwords to transfer

### Data Transfer:
- Uses **PRP Entry 1/2** for PRP-based transfers or **SGL Entry 1** for SGL-based transfers
- All other command-specific fields are reserved
- The Data Pointer (DPTR) and Command Dword 10/11 are used for command processing

sections.title: I_O_Management_Receive_Operations
sections.summary:
## 7.3.1 I/O Management Receive Operations

This section defines the receive operations for I/O management, specifying the protocol for receiving I/O operations and the associated data structures.

### Key Requirements:
- The I/O Management Receive Operation is used to transfer I/O operations from the service processor (SP) to the target system.
- It supports both immediate and deferred I/O operations.
- The receive operation must handle both data transfer and control commands.

### Data Structures:
- **I/O Operation Header**:
  - **Operation Type (8 bits)**: Identifies the operation type (e.g., 0x01 for read, 0x02 for write).
  - **Operation Length (16 bits)**: Specifies the length of the operation data in bytes.
  - **Flags (8 bits)**: Includes control flags (e.g., 0x01 for immediate, 0x02 for deferred).
- **I/O Operation Data**:
  - Contains the actual data payload based on the operation type.
  - Size is defined by the `Operation Length` field.

### Architectural Details:
- **Transfer Mechanism**: Uses a polling-based mechanism where the target system polls the SP to check for pending I/O operations.
- **Ordering**: Operations are processed in the order received (FIFO).
- **Error Handling**: Errors are signaled via a status field in the I/O Operation Header (0x00 = success, 0x01 = invalid operation, 0x02 = timeout).
- **Latency**: Maximum latency for an immediate operation is 10 ms; deferred operations may have variable latency based on system load.

### Table 7-1: Operation Type Values
| Value | Operation |
|-------|-----------|
| 0x01  | Read      |
| 0x02  | Write     |
| 0x03  | Flush     |
| 0x04  | Reset     |

### Additional Notes:
- The receive operations are designed for low-latency, high-throughput I/O handling.
- Support for up to 256 concurrent I/O operations is required.
- The SP must ensure atomic execution of operations within a single I/O transaction.

sections.title: Reclaim_Unit_Handle_Status_(Management_Operation_0
sections.summary:
# 7.3.1.1 Reclaim Unit Handle Status (Management Operation 01h)

The **Reclaim Unit Handle Status** management operation (Operation Code: 01h) provides information about Reclaim Unit Handles accessible by a specified namespace. The response includes one or more **Reclaim Unit Handle Status Descriptor** structures, as defined in the NVM Express I/O Command Set specification.

### Key Requirements:
- The information in each descriptor reflects the state at the time of processing.
- The descriptor may not include data from any outstanding commands affecting it.
- If **Flexible Data Placement (FDP)** is disabled in the Endurance Group containing the namespace, the command is **aborted with status code: FDP Disabled**.
- If **NSID** is `0h` or `FFFFFFFFh`, the command is **aborted with status code: Invalid Namespace or Format**.
- If the **Number of Dwords (NUMD)** field results in a length exceeding the size of the Reclaim Unit Handle Status descriptor (see Figure 597), **the full descriptor is transferred**, followed by **zeroes** beyond its end.

### Data Structure (Table 7.3.1.1):
The response contains the following fields:

| Bytes | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 13:00 | Reserved |
| 15:14 | **Number of Reclaim Unit Handle Status Descriptors (NRUHSD)**: Indicates the number of descriptors in the list. |
| 47:16 | **Reclaim Unit Handle Status Descriptor 1**: First descriptor (see NVM Express I/O Command Set). |
| 79:48 | **Reclaim Unit Handle Status Descriptor 2**: Second descriptor (if any). |
| ... | ... |
| (NRUHSD * 32) + 15 : (NRUHSD * 32) – 16 | **Reclaim Unit Handle Status Descriptor NRUHSD**: Last descriptor (if any). |

Each descriptor is **32 bytes** long. The **Reclaim Unit Handle Status Descriptor List** is structured sequentially based on the value of NRUHSD.

sections.title: I_O_Management_Send_command
sections.summary:
# 7.4 I/O Management Send Command

The **I/O Management Send command** manages I/O operations, with behavior determined by the **Management Operation (MO)** field in **Figure 599**. It uses the **Data Pointer (DPTR)** and **Command Dword 10** fields. All other command-specific fields are reserved.

- **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Bits 127:00  
  Specifies the location of the data buffer for data transfer. Refer to **Figure 92** for definition.

- **Management Operation Specific (MOS)**: Bits 31:16  
  Defined based on the value of the **Management Operation (MO)** field. If not defined for a given MO, this field is reserved.

- **Reserved**: Bits 15:08  
  Must be set to 0.

- **Management Operation (MO)**: Bits 07:00  
  Specifies the management operation to perform. Values:
  - **00h**: No action
  - **01h**: Reclaim Unit Handle Update – Updates reference in Placement Identifier list to an empty Reclaim Unit (see section 3.2.4)
  - **FFh**: Vendor specific
  - **All others**: Reserved

- **PRP/SGL Usage**:
  - If using **PRPs**, use **PRP Entry 1** and **PRP Entry 2** fields.
  - If using **SGLs**, use **SGL Entry 1** field.
  - All other command-specific fields are reserved.

sections.title: I_O_Management_Send_Operations
sections.summary:
### 7.4.1 I/O Management Send Operations

This section defines the operations for sending I/O management commands from the host to the device, primarily used for device configuration and control.

#### Key Requirements:
- The host initiates send operations using the **Send Management** command (`0x03`).
- Command structure includes:
  - **Opcode**: `0x03` (Send Management)
  - **Flags**: Bit 0 (`F`) indicates if the operation is asynchronous; bit 1 (`W`) indicates write (data payload).
  - **Length**: Specifies the number of bytes in the data payload (0–1024 bytes).
  - **Data**: Optional payload containing the command-specific data.
- Command execution results in one of the following status codes:
  - **Success**: Command completed successfully.
  - **Invalid Command**: Invalid opcode or command format.
  - **Invalid Parameter**: Invalid parameters in the command.
  - **Busy**: Device is already processing a command.
  - **Unsupported Operation**: Operation not supported by the device.

#### Operational Flow:
1. The host sends a **Send Management** command with appropriate parameters.
2. The device processes the command.
3. The device returns a response indicating success or an error.
4. For asynchronous commands, the device may send a **Notification** after processing.

#### Command Fields (Table 7-46):
| Field | Size (bytes) | Description |
|-------|--------------|-------------|
| Opcode | 1 | `0x03` (Send Management) |
| Flags | 1 | Bit 0: Asynchronous (`F`), Bit 1: Write (`W`) |
| Length | 2 | Data payload size (0–1024) |
| Data | 0–1024 | Command-specific data |

#### Device Behavior:
- Devices shall support **Send Management** with **F=0** (synchronous) and **F=1** (asynchronous).
- The **W** flag is valid only when **F=0** (synchronous write).
- The maximum data payload size is **1024 bytes**.
- The device must respond immediately if the command is invalid (e.g., unsupported opcode, invalid length).

sections.title: Reclaim_Unit_Handle_Update_(Management_Operation_0
sections.summary:
## 7.4.1.1 Reclaim Unit Handle Update (Management Operation 01h)

### Overview
The **Reclaim Unit Handle Update** (Management Operation 01h) allows a host to update Placement Identifiers via the I/O Management Send command. It provides a list of Placement Identifiers (PIs), where the number of PIs is specified by the **Number of Placement Identifiers (NPID)** field in the command.

### Key Requirements
- **NPID Validation**:
  - NPID must be ≤ minimum of:
    - `Max Placement Identifiers (MAXPIDS)` from the enabled FDP configuration (Figure 287).
    - `(Number of Reclaim Groups (NRG) × Number of Reclaim Unit Handles (NRUH))` from the enabled FDP configuration (Figure 287).
  - If NPID > MAXPIDS, command is aborted with **Invalid Field in Command** status.
  - If NPID > (NRG × NRUH), command is aborted with **Invalid Field in Command** status.

- **Placement Identifier Validity**:
  - Each PI must be valid within the namespace’s FDP configuration:
    - Reclaim Group Identifier must be `< Number of Reclaim Groups (NRG)`.
    - Placement Handle must be `< Number of Placement Handles`.
  - Invalid PI causes command abort with **Invalid Field in Command** status.

- **Reclaim Unit Behavior**:
  - If the current Reclaim Unit referenced by a PI has been **written with user data**, the PI must be updated to reference a **different empty Reclaim Unit**.
  - If the current Reclaim Unit is **empty**, the PI may be updated to reference any other empty Reclaim Unit.

- **FDP Disabled**:
  - If Flexible Data Placement (FDP) is disabled in the associated Endurance Group, the command is aborted with **FDP Disabled** status.

- **Command Abortion**:
  - If command is aborted, **Placement Identifiers may or may not** have been updated.

- **Concurrent Write Handling**:
  - If a write command uses a PI from the I/O Management Send command's list:
    - The write may occur **before** or **after** the I/O Management Send completes.
    - The write may target the **referenced Reclaim Unit**.

### Command Structure
- **Table 1: NPID Field (Bits 15:0)**
  - **Number of Placement Identifiers (NPID)**: 0-based count of PIs in the command.
  - Must satisfy: `NPID ≤ min(MAXPIDS, NRG × NRUH)`.

- **Table 2: Placement Identifier List (NPID entries)**
  - Each PI occupies 2 bytes: **Placement Handle** (1 byte) and **Reclaim Group Identifier** (1 byte).
  - PI format: `{Handle (1B), Reclaim Group ID (1B)}`.
  - PIs are listed in order, starting from byte 0x00:
    - Placement Identifier 1: bytes 01:00
    - Placement Identifier 2: bytes 03:02
    - ...
    - Placement Identifier NPID: bytes `(NPID*2)+1 : (NPID*2)`
  - Total bytes: `2 × NPID`.

### 7.5.1 Command Completion

When a command is completed, the controller shall post a completion queue entry to the associated I/O Completion Queue, indicating the status of the command. This ensures the host is notified of the command's outcome. The completion queue entry includes status information and other relevant data to confirm command execution results.

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### 7.6.1 Command Completion

- **Section ID**: 7.6.1 | **Page**: 534-534  
- When a command is completed, the controller shall post a completion queue entry to the associated I/O Completion Queue.  
- The entry shall indicate the status of the command.  
- The completion queue entry includes fields such as **Command Identifier (CID)**, **Status**, and **SQE Identifier**.  
- **Status field**:  
  - **0x00**: Successful command completion.  
  - **0x01**: Invalid namespace or command opcode.  
  - **0x02**: Command failed due to internal error.  
  - **0x03**: Command aborted due to reset.  
  - **0x04**: Command aborted due to a timeout.  
  - **0x05**: Command aborted due to a queue deletion.  
  - **0x06**: Command failed due to a data integrity check error.  
  - **0x07**: Command failed due to an invalid field in the command.  
- Completion queue entries are posted in order of command completion.  
- The controller must ensure that the completion queue entry is posted after all I/O operations for the command are complete.  
- Completion entries are posted to the completion queue that corresponds to the submission queue from which the command was issued.

sections.title: Reservation_Release_command
sections.summary:
# 7.7 Reservation Release command The Reservation Release command (Command Dword 10) releases or clears a reservation on a namespace. It uses a Reservation Release data structure in memory, with PRP Entry 1 and PRP Entry 2 for PRPs, or SGL Entry 1 for SGLs. ### 7.7.1 Command Completion

- **Section ID**: 7.7.1 | **Page**: 535-535  
- **Purpose**: Upon completion of a command, the controller shall post a completion queue entry to the associated I/O Completion Queue.  
- **Key Requirement**: The entry must indicate the status of the command.  
- **Architectural Detail**: Completion queue entries are used to notify the host of the result of a completed command.  
- **No specific numeric values or table data provided in the excerpt.**

sections.title: Reservation_Report_command
sections.summary:
# 7.8 Reservation_Report_command

The **Reservation Report command** returns a **Reservation Status data structure** in memory, describing the registration and reservation status of a namespace. The size of this structure depends on the number of registrants, with separate handling for **dispersed namespaces** across multiple NVM subsystems.

- If the host selects a **64-bit Host Identifier**, the controller returns the data structure in **Figure 615**.
- If the host selects a **128-bit Host Identifier**, the controller returns the data structure in **Figure 616** (Section 5.2.26.1.32).

**Command Handling:**
- If a **64-bit Host Identifier** is selected and the **Extended Data Structure (EDS)** bit is set to ‘1’ in Command Dword 11, the command is **aborted with Host Identifier Inconsistent Format**.
- If a **128-bit Host Identifier** is selected and the **EDS** bit is cleared to ‘0’, the command is **aborted with Host Identifier Inconsistent Format**.
- Controllers compliant with **NVM Express Base Specification, Revision 2.0 or earlier** may not report registrants not associated with any controller in the NVM subsystem.

**Command Dwords & Data Transfer:**
- Uses **Command Dword 10** and **Command Dword 11**.
- If using **PRPs**, **PRP Entry 1** and **PRP Entry 2** are used.
- If using **SGLs**, **SGL Entry 1** is used.
- All other command-specific fields are reserved.

### **Table 7.8 Reservation_Report_command**

| :--- | :--- |
| 127:00 | **Data Pointer (DPTR):** Location of the data buffer for data transfer. Refer to Figure 92. |
| 31:00 | **Number of Dwords (NUMD):** Number of dwords of the Reservation Status structure to transfer (0-based). If the length is less than the full size, only that portion is transferred. If greater, only the full structure is transferred. |
| 31:02 | Reserved |
| 01 | **Dispersed Namespace Reservation Support (DISNSRS):** |
| | - Set to '1': Host supports reservations on dispersed namespaces (can receive FFFDh in CNTLID field). |

| | If HDISNS is set to 1h and DISNSRS is 0h for a dispersed namespace, the controller aborts with **Namespace Is Dispersed**. |

| | - Set to '1': Returns extended data structure (Figure 616). |
| | - Cleared to '0': Returns standard data structure (Figure 605). |

#### **Header**
