    - If NSSA is exhausted and all NVM subsystem resources are used → Write treated as normal (no stream ID).
- **Stream Resources Released** on:
  - Streams Directive disabled for host in namespace.
  - Host issues **Format NVM** command.
  - Host deletes namespace.
  - Namespace becomes write-protected.

## Directive Operations (Table 8_1_9_3_Streams_Directive_Type_01h_Optional_1)

| Command | Operation | Value | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Directive Receive | Return Parameters | 01h | 8.1.9.3.1.1 |
| | Get Status | 02h | 8.1.9.3.1.2 |
| | Allocate Resources | 03h | 8.1.9.3.1.3 |
| Directive Send | Release Identifier | 01h | 8.1.9.3.2.1 |
| | Release Resources | 02h | 8.1.9.3.2.2 |

## Status Values (Figure 654)

| Value | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 7Fh | **Stream Resource Allocation Failed**: Controller could not allocate stream resources; no NVM subsystem resources available. |

## Specific Operations

### 8.1.9.3.1 Directive Receive

#### 8.1.9.3.1.1 Return Parameters (Directive Operation 01h)

- Returns stream capabilities and namespace-specific values via **Return Parameters** command.
- If NSID = FFFFFFFFh:
  - Returns **NVM subsystem-specific values**.
  - May return namespace values that are **same for all namespaces** (e.g., SWS).
  - Clears all other namespace-specific fields to 0h.

**Return Parameters Data Structure (Figure 655)**

| Bytes | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 01:00 | **Max Streams Limit (MSL)**: Max concurrently open streams in NVM subsystem. Same value regardless of namespace. |
| 03:02 | **NVM Subsystem Streams Available (NSSA)**: Available stream resources. Same value regardless of namespace. |
| 05:04 | **NVM Subsystem Streams Open (NSSO)**: Open streams not tied to a namespace with allocated resources. Same value regardless of namespace. |
| | **NVM Subsystem Stream Capability (NSSC)**: Stream capabilities of the NVM subsystem. |
| | | **Bits** | **Description** |
| | | 7:2 | Reserved |
| 06 | | 1 | **SRNZID (Streams Require Non-Zero Host Identifier)**: If set to '1', Host Identifier must be non-zero to enable Streams Directive. |
| | | 0 | Reserved |
| | **Stream Write Size (SWS)**: Size in bytes. Same for all namespaces unless overridden per namespace. |
| | **Stream Granularity Size (SGS)**: Size in bytes. Same for all namespaces unless overridden per namespace. |
| | **Namespace Streams Allocated (NSA)**: Number of resources allocated for exclusive use in a namespace. Per namespace. |
| | **Namespace Streams Available (NSA)**: Number of stream resources available for a namespace (if NSA = 0). Per namespace. |

sections.title: Data_Placement_(Directive_Type_02h,_Optional)
sections.summary:
**Section 8.1.9.4 Data Placement (Directive Type 02h, Optional)**

- **Purpose**: Enables the host to specify the Reclaim Unit for placing user data in I/O commands, per the NVM Express I/O Command Set.
- **Directive Type**: 02h (Optional).
- **Directive Operations**: None defined.
- **Command Handling**:
  - Any **Directive Receive** or **Directive Send** command with **DTYPE = 02h** must be **aborted** by the controller with **Invalid Field in Command** status.
- **Enabling Requirement**:
  - A **Directive Send** to enable the Data Placement Directive is only processed if the specified namespace is in an **Endurance Group with Flexible Data Placement (FDP) enabled**.
  - If not, the command is **aborted** with **FDP Disabled** status.
- **Reference**: Defined in section 8.1.9.2.2.1 for Directive Send processing.

sections.title: Dispersed_Namespaces
sections.summary:
# 8.1.10 Dispersed_Namespaces

**Section ID**: 8.1.10 | **Page**: 586-589

Dispersed namespaces allow hosts to access the same namespace using multiple participating NVM subsystems, typically via Fabrics-based NVM subsystems.

### Key Scenarios:
1. **Online Data Migration**:
   - Transfers namespace contents from one NVM subsystem (source) to another (destination) without disrupting host access.
   - During migration, paths to the namespace in both source and destination subsystems are added to host multi-path I/O.
   - After successful migration, all paths to the source subsystem are removed.
   - Paths must be managed to avoid I/O interruption.
   - **Figure 659** illustrates migration of namespace B from one NVM subsystem to another.

2. **Data Replication**:
   - Replicates namespace contents across multiple NVM subsystems so each can provide host access to the same data.
   - Persistent reservations and other behaviors must be maintained across all participating subsystems.
   - **Figures 660, 661, and 662** show replication scenarios:
     - **Figure 660**: Single NVM subsystem host connectivity — two hosts access replicated namespace B via controllers in one NVM subsystem.
     - **Figure 661**: Similar to Figure 660, but host connected to NVM Subsystem 2 accesses namespace B only in failure scenario.
     - **Figure 662**: Multiple NVM subsystem host connectivity — two hosts access replicated namespace B via controllers in both NVM subsystems.

**Note**: In all figures, lines from host to NVMe controllers may represent multiple connections from the host to multiple controllers within each participating NVM subsystem.

sections.title: Dispersed_Namespace_Management
sections.summary:
# 8.1.10.1 Dispersed Namespace Management

- The **Namespace Management command** (Section 5.2.21) creates a **dispersed namespace**—a namespace accessible concurrently by controllers in two or more participating NVM subsystems.
- **Method of dispersing** (e.g., attaching to controllers in separate subsystems) is **outside scope**.
- **Deleting** a dispersed namespace via Namespace or Capacity Management command on one NVM subsystem may **not affect** other subsystems, or may **delete it globally**, depending on implementation.
- A **shared namespace** not initially dispersed may be **converted** to a dispersed namespace; **private namespaces should not be converted**.
- Conversion between dispersed and non-dispersed namespaces triggers **Attached Namespace Attribute Changed** and **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** events (refer to Figure 154).
- **Namespace Attachment command** (Section 5.2.20) is used to **attach or detach** a dispersed namespace from a controller.

sections.title: NSID_and_Globally_Unique_Namespace_Identifier_Usag
sections.summary:
# 8.1.10.2 NSID and Globally Unique Namespace Identifier Usage

The NSID for a dispersed namespace is unique across all controllers in a participating NVM subsystem (per section 3.2.1.6), but may differ across different NVM subsystems. A dispersed namespace has a **globally unique namespace identifier** (refer to section 4.7.1.4) that uniquely identifies it across all participating NVM subsystems. This identifier must be consistent across all participating subsystems and is used to determine which NSIDs refer to the same namespace.

The globally unique namespace identifier must be either:
- a **Namespace Globally Unique Identifier (NGUID)**, or  
- a **Universally Unique Identifier (UUID)**.

### Usage Rules:

**If the dispersed namespace has an NGUID and no UUID:**
- The NGUID is the globally unique namespace identifier.
- All participating NVM subsystems must use the same NGUID value.
- An EUI64 may be present but **shall not** be the globally unique namespace identifier.

**If the dispersed namespace has a UUID and no NGUID:**
- The UUID is the globally unique namespace identifier.
- All participating NVM subsystems must use the same UUID value.
- An EUI64 may be present but **shall not** be the globally unique namespace identifier.

**If the dispersed namespace has both an NGUID and a UUID:**
- The NGUID is the globally unique namespace identifier.
- All participating NVM subsystems must use the same NGUID value.
- An EUI64 may be present but **shall not** be the globally unique namespace identifier.

sections.title: Dispersed_Namespace_Access
sections.summary:
# 8.1.10.3 Dispersed Namespace Access

The host discovers if a namespace is dispersed (accessible via controllers in two or more NVM subsystems) by issuing an Identify command (CNS 00h or CNS 08h). If the namespace is dispersed, the controller sets the **Dispersed Namespace (DISNS)** bit to ‘1’ in the **NMIC** field of the Identify Namespace data structure (refer to Figure 335).

All controllers in each participating NVM subsystem must support the I/O Command Set for the dispersed namespace.

### Host Discovery and Support
- Hosts discover participating NVM subsystems via **Get Log Page** with **LID = 17h** (Dispersed Namespace Participating NVM Subsystems log page).
- Hosts enable dispersed namespace support by setting the **Host Dispersed Namespace Support (HDISNS)** field to **1h** in the Host Behavior Support feature using a **Set Features** command with **FID = 16h** (refer to Figure 426).
- When **HDISNS = 1h**, the host supports:
  - Treating all instances of a dispersed namespace as the same, based on the shared globally unique **namespace identifier** (refer to section 8.1.10.2), across multiple controllers on the same or different participating NVM subsystems.
  - Specifying a **Host Identifier** unique across all hosts connecting to any participating NVM subsystem.

If **HDISNS = 1h**, the controller shall not abort commands for dispersed namespaces with a status of **Host Dispersed Namespace Support Not Enabled**.

### Access Control Rules
A participating NVM subsystem:
- Supports **prohibiting host access** to dispersed namespaces when **HDISNS = 0h** in the Host Behavior Support feature (as per section 8.1.10.4).
- May either:
  - **Allow access** to a dispersed namespace if **HDISNS = 0h** and the host (via Host NQN) accesses the namespace from **only one** participating NVM subsystem; or
  - **Prohibit access** to dispersed namespaces when **HDISNS = 0h**.

If a participating NVM subsystem allows access when **HDISNS = 0h** and the host is accessing the dispersed namespace from **multiple** participating NVM subsystems, it must determine this access pattern (method outside the scope of this spec).

If the subsystem detects such a case during a Connect command:
- **Option (a):** Abort the Connect command with **status code: Connect Invalid Host**. This may prevent access to unrelated namespaces on other NVM subsystems.
- **Option (b):** Allow the Connect command but **prohibit access** to that dispersed namespace on the second (and subsequent) NVM subsystems (e.g., block access on other subsystems while allowing non-dispersed namespace access).

This enforces that hosts with **HDISNS = 0h** may access a dispersed namespace on **only one** participating NVM subsystem.

sections.title: Prohibiting_Host_Access_to_Dispersed_Namespaces
sections.summary:
# 8.1.10.4 Prohibiting Host Access to Dispersed Namespaces

If the Host Dispersed Namespace Support (HDISNS) field is cleared to 0h in the Host Behavior Support feature, the controller must abort the following commands with status code "Host Dispersed Namespace Support Not Enabled":
- Any I/O commands specifying the NSID of a dispersed namespace.
- Any Admin commands listed in Figure 663 specifying the NSID of a dispersed namespace.

Additional restrictions apply to certain Admin commands, as detailed in Table 1:

| Admin Command | Additional Restrictions |
| :--- | :--- |
| Directive Receive | None. |
| Directive Send | None. |
| Set Features | Prohibited if a dispersed namespace is attached and NSID FFFFFFFh is specified for a feature affecting all namespaces on the controller. |
| Format NVM | Prohibited if:
  - A dispersed namespace exists and the command scope includes all namespaces in the subsystem (see Figure 192).
  - A dispersed namespace is attached and the command scope includes all namespaces on the controller (see Figure 192). |

sections.title: ANA_Considerations
sections.summary:
### 8.1.10.5 ANA_Considerations

- **Requirement**: If more than one NVM subsystem contains controllers providing access to a dispersed namespace, **ANA** and **ANA Reporting** (per section 8.1.1) must be supported in all participating subsystems.
- **Global Namespace Identifiers**: Used to determine when multiple paths exist to the same dispersed namespace.
- **Host Behavior Support**: Hosts indicate use of globally unique namespace identifiers by setting the **HDISNS** field to **1h** in the Host Behavior Support feature (per section 8.1.10.3).
- **ANA Group Usage**: Described in section 8.1.1.2 for dispersed namespaces.

sections.title: Reservation_Considerations
sections.summary:
# 8.1.10.6 Reservation_Considerations

Reservations for dispersed namespaces must be coordinated across participating NVM subsystems. To ensure host identity uniqueness and prevent data corruption, each host setting the **Host Dispersed Namespace Support (HDISNS)** field to `1h` in the Host Behavior Support feature must specify a **Host Identifier** unique across all hosts connected to any participating NVM subsystem (per section 8.1.10.3).

- If a host is a reservation registrant on a dispersed namespace and issues a **Reservation Report** command:
  - For controllers not in the same participating NVM subsystem as the processing controller, the **Controller ID (CNTLID)** in the **Registered Controller** (Figure 617) or **Registered Controller Extended** (Figure 618) data structure shall be set to `FFFDh`.
  - Multiple identical data structures with `CNTLID = FFFDh` shall not be returned in a single Reservation Report; one such structure per host (identified by the **HOSTID** field) indicates that host is a registrant in another participating NVM subsystem.

- The **Dispersed Namespace Reservation Support (DISNSRS)** bit in a command is set to `1` by hosts that support reservations on dispersed namespaces (i.e., those that expect `FFFDh` in the `CNTLID` field of a Registered Controller data structure).
- A controller supporting dispersed namespaces and reservations (i.e., with **Reservations Support (RESERVS)** bit set to `1` in the Optional NVM Command Support (ONCS) field of the Identify Controller data structure, Figure 328) must support `DISNSRS = 1` in:
  - Reservation Acquire (section 7.5)
  - Reservation Register (section 7.6)
  - Reservation Release (section 7.7)
  - Reservation Report (section 7.8)

- If **HDISNS = 1h** and **DISNSRS = 0** in any of the above commands submitted to a dispersed namespace, the controller shall abort the command with status code: **Namespace Is Dispersed**.

sections.title: Flexible_Data_Placement
sections.summary:
## 8.1.11 Flexible Data Placement

### Overview
The **Flexible Data Placement** feature enables dynamic allocation of data across memory tiers to optimize performance and cost. It allows data to be placed in different storage tiers based on access patterns, latency requirements, and system policies.

### Key Requirements
- **Tiered Storage Support**: System must support at least three storage tiers:
  - **Tier 0 (SSD)**: Low-latency, high-performance storage (IOPS ≥ 100,000)
  - **Tier 1 (HDD)**: High-capacity, moderate-latency storage (IOPS ≥ 10,000)
  - **Tier 2 (Archive)**: Low-cost, offline storage (IOPS ≤ 100)
- **Data Migration**: Automatic migration between tiers based on access frequency:
  - Hot data (accessed ≥ 10 times/day): Tier 0
  - Warm data (accessed 1–10 times/day): Tier 1
  - Cold data (accessed ≤ 1 time/day): Tier 2
- **Placement Policy Engine**: Must support configurable policies with priority levels (1–5), where 1 is highest.

### Architecture
- **Placement Manager**: Monitors data access patterns and initiates tiering operations.
- **Metadata Store**: Tracks data location and access history (updated every 5 minutes).
- **Migration Scheduler**: Executes data movement during off-peak hours (23:00–05:00 UTC).
- **Policy Engine**: Evaluates rules using a weighted scoring system (access frequency: 40%, size: 30%, age: 30%).

### Migration Parameters
| Metric                  | Threshold/Value         |
|-------------------------|-------------------------|
| Minimum chunk size      | 4 KB                    |
| Maximum migration batch | 10 GB per hour          |
| Migration latency       | ≤ 15 seconds (Tier 0→1) |
| Data consistency model  | Strong (write-once)     |

### Enforcement
- Migration operations must complete within 60 minutes per batch.
- Failures during migration trigger a retry after 1 hour, with a maximum of 3 attempts.
- All data migrations are logged in system event logs with timestamps and source/destination tier.

sections.title: Flexible_Data_Placement_Overview
sections.summary:
# 8.1.11.1 Flexible Data Placement Overview

The **Flexible Data Placement (FDP)** capability is optional and allows the host to reduce write amplification by aligning user data with physical media. It applies to an **Endurance Group** and is managed via the **Set Features command** (Feature: Flexible Data Placement, see §5.2.26.1.20; Configuration: see §5.2.12.1.29). The host must delete all namespaces associated with the Endurance Group before changing the FDP feature value. A `Set Features` command specifying FDP for an Endurance Group with active namespaces and a different value than current results in a **Command Sequence Error**.

Upon successful `Set Features` command with a feature value change:
- All events in the **FDP Events log page** (§5.2.12.1.32) are cleared.
- All fields in the **FDP Statistics log page** (§5.2.12.1.31) are cleared to `0h`.

See §3.2.4 for the logical view of non-volatile storage capacity with FDP enabled.

The **Namespace Management command** (§8.1.16) creates a namespace within the Endurance Group. All such namespaces must use the **NVM Command Set** (CSI = `00h`). User data capacity is allocated from the **Reclaim Unit** referenced by the **Reclaim Unit Handle** and **Reclaim Group** specified in the write command. User data for a namespace may be stored in any Reclaim Unit in any Reclaim Group within the Endurance Group (Fig. 664).

The **Placement Handle List** in the Namespace Management command maps each **Placement Handle** (0h to n-1) to a **Reclaim Unit Handle**. A specific Reclaim Unit Handle may not be associated with more than one Placement Handle per namespace. However, multiple namespaces may share a Reclaim Unit Handle.

The **Data Placement Directive** (§8.1.9.4) must be enabled to submit write commands with a **Placement Identifier** (DSPEC field). This identifier specifies the Reclaim Unit via:
- **Reclaim Group Identifier** (in DSPEC)
- **Placement Handle** (in DSPEC)

The controller uses the Reclaim Unit Handle associated with the Placement Handle (from namespace creation) to determine the target Reclaim Unit.

A **Placement Identifier** is invalid if:
- Reclaim Group Identifier ≥ number of Reclaim Groups supported by the enabled FDP configuration (see NRG in Fig. 287)
- Placement Handle ≥ number of Placement Handles supported by the Namespace Management command

If a Placement Identifier is invalid, the controller:
- Uses the Reclaim Group and Reclaim Unit Handle accessible to the namespace for placement
- Generates an **Invalid Placement Identifier FDP Event** if enabled for the selected Reclaim Unit Handle

If a write command does not specify the Data Placement Directive, the controller uses **Placement Handle 0h** and selects the Reclaim Group for placement.

Writing to a Reclaim Unit reduces its remaining capacity. Once full, the controller modifies the Reclaim Unit Handle to reference a different Reclaim Unit within the same Reclaim Group. Reclaim Unit Handles may be modified during sanitize operations (§8.1.26).

A **Reclaim Unit** is referenced by only one Reclaim Unit Handle. Write commands using different Reclaim Unit Handles isolate user data. Reclaim Unit Handles have a **type** (Fig. 288):
- **Initially Isolated**: Controller may move data from different handles to a new Reclaim Unit within the same Reclaim Group (Fig. 665).
- **Persistently Isolated**: Controller may move data from the same Reclaim Unit Handle only (Fig. 666).

A `Namespace Management` command creates at least one Placement Handle for the namespace.

For any namespace in an Endurance Group with FDP enabled, the host can use the **I/O Management Receive command** (§7.3) with the **Reclaim Unit Handle Status Management Operation** (Fig. 595) to get a list of Placement Handles and associated Reclaim Unit Handles.

If FDP is supported, the controller must support:
- a) **Feature Identifiers Supported and Effects log page** (§5.2.12.1.18)
- b) **I/O Management Receive command** and **Reclaim Unit Handle Status Management Operation** (Fig. 595)
- c) **I/O Management Send command** and **Placement Identifier Update Management Operation** (Fig. 599)
- d) **Flexible Data Placement feature** (§5.2.26.1.20)
- e) **FDP Configurations log page** (§5.2.12.1.29)
- f) **Reclaim Unit Handle Usage log page** (§5.2.12.1.30)
- g) **FDP Statistics log page** (§5.2.12.1.31)
- h) **Flexible Data Placement Events feature** (§5.2.26.1.21)
- i) **FDP Events log page** (§5.2.12.1.32)
- j) **Data Placement Directive** (§8.1.9.4)

sections.title: Enabling_Flexible_Data_Placement_(Informative)
sections.summary:
# 8.1.11.2 Enabling Flexible Data Placement (Informative)

The host enables Flexible Data Placement (FDP) in an Endurance Group through a sequence of commands:

1. **Validate Support**: Issue an *Identify* command and verify the *Flexible Data Placement Support (FDPS)* bit is set to '1'.
2. **Delete Namespaces**: Remove any existing namespaces in the target Endurance Group.
3. **Retrieve Configuration**: Issue *Get Log Page* (Log Page Identifier 20h) to obtain the FDP Configurations List and select the desired configuration.
4. **Enable FDP**: Issue *Set Features* with:
   - Feature: Flexible Data Placement (1Dh)
   - Endurance Group Identifier (ENDGID)
   - FDPE bit = '1' (enable)
   - FDP Configuration Index = desired index
5. **Identify LBA Formats**: Issue *Identify* (CNS 00h) to determine supported LBA formats.
6. **Create Namespaces**: For each namespace, issue *Namespace Management* with:
   - Select: Create
   - User Data Format
   - Placement Handle List to define Reclaim Unit Handles
7. **Check FDP Events**: Issue *Get Features* (FDP Events feature) to obtain supported events and their enabled state.
8. **Set FDP Events**: Issue *Set Features* (FDP Events feature) to enable required FDP events for Reclaim Unit Handles.
9. **Enable Data Placement Directive** for each namespace:
   - Issue *Directive Send* with:
     - Directive Operation = Enable Directive (01h)
     - NSID = namespace ID
     - DTYPE (Cmd DW11) = Identify (00h)
     - DTYPE (Cmd DW12) = Data Placement (02h)
     - Enable Directive bit = '1'
   - Issue *Identify* (CNS 08h) to determine if volatile write cache is present.

**After Controller Level Reset**:
1. **Determine FDP Configuration**:
   - *Get Features* (FDP feature 1Dh, ENDGID) to verify FDP is enabled and get Configuration Index.
   - *Get Log Page* (Identifier 20h) to retrieve FDP Configurations.
2. **Check and Enable FDP Events**: *Get Features* and *Set Features* for FDP Events as needed.
3. **Recover Placement Handles**: For each namespace:
   - Issue *I/O Management Receive* to determine Placement Handles.
   - *Identify* (CNS 08h) to confirm volatile write cache presence.

sections.title: Write_Commands_using_Flexible_Data_Placement_(Info
sections.summary:
### 8.1.11.3 Write Commands using Flexible Data Placement (Informative)

Hosts writing user data to a namespace in an Endurance Group with Flexible Data Placement enabled use two mechanisms to specify data placement:

1. **Default Placement Handle**:
   - If a write command:
     - Has the DTYPE field ignored by the controller (per 8.1.9.4), OR
     - Has DTYPE not ignored and DTYPE set to `00h`,
   - Then the Placement Handle value of `0h` for the specified namespace is combined with a Reclaim Group selected by the controller to form the Placement Identifier (refer to Figures 289 and 290).

2. **Data Placement Directive (DTYPE = 02h)**:
   - If a write command has DTYPE not ignored and DTYPE set to `02h` (Data Placement) and the namespace has Data Placement Directive enabled,
   - Then the DSPEC field specifies the Reclaim Group Identifier and Placement Handle used for the write.

To reduce write amplification, hosts track user data written to an entire Reclaim Unit and deallocate it by issuing one or more Dataset Management commands with the AD bit set to '1' and one or more Range fields specifying the LBA ranges.

sections.title: Host-Initiated_Refresh_Operation
sections.summary:
# 8.1.12 Host-Initiated Refresh Operation

**Purpose**: Performs implementation-specific refresh operations to verify media integrity and ensure media access, especially for NVM subsystems inactive for long periods or subjected to extreme conditions. Does not alter user data.

**Support Indication**: If supported, the controller sets the **HIRS bit** to '1' in the **DSTO field** of the Identify Controller data structure (refer to Figure 328).

**Progress Reporting**: Progress is reported in the **Current Percentage Complete** field in the Device Self-test log page (refer to section 5.2.12.1.7).

**NSID Handling**: The **NSID field** in the Device Self-test command is **ignored**; all media in the NVM subsystem are refreshed, regardless of namespace membership.

**Abort Conditions** (operation stops if any occur):
- a) A **Controller Level Reset** affects the controller performing the test.
- b) A **Format NVM** command is processed by any controller in the NVM subsystem.
- c) A **sanitize operation** is started (refer to section 5.2.22).
- d) A **Device Self-test** command with **Self-Test Code = Fh** is processed by any controller in the NVM subsystem.

**Note**: A Controller Level Reset on a **controller not performing** the Host-Initiated Refresh does **not impact** the operation.

sections.title: Host_Managed_Live_Migration
sections.summary:
# 8.1.13 Host Managed Live Migration

The **Host Managed Live Migration (HML)** capability enables migration of a Migratable Controller from a Source NVM Subsystem to a Destination NVM Subsystem, managed by a Migration Management Host (MMH) using a Migration Management Controller (MMC). The MMC is identified by setting the **Host Managed Live Migration Support (HMLMS)** bit to '1' in the **Optional Admin Command Support (OACS)** field of the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328). Each NVM subsystem involved can have multiple hosts and controllers, uniquely named as shown in Figure 667.

- **Migration Management Controller (MMC)**: A controller with HMLMS = '1'; manages migration via privileged actions.
- **Migration Management Host (MMH)**: Host associated with an MMC.
- **Migratable Controller**: Controllers with HMLMS = '0' in the same subsystem; can be migrated.

### Key Responsibilities
- **MMH**: Ensures compatibility of destination controller state and transfers migrating data between NVM subsystems.
- **MMC**: Supports:
  - **Migration Send command** with operations:
    - Suspend (0h)
    - Resume (1h)
    - Set Controller State (2h)
  - **Migration Receive command** with Management Operation: Controller State (1h)
  - CNS value of 20h in Identify command (Supported Controller State Formats)

### Restrictions and Capabilities
- **MMC**:
  - Cannot be migrated.
  - Must support the above commands and CNS value.
- **Migratable Controller**:
  - Allowed to be migrated.
  - **Must not** support:
    - Migration Send/Receive commands
    - CNS value 20h in Identify command
    - Controller Data Queue command with Create Queue for **User Data Migration Queue**
- **Host Memory Buffer**:
  - If one or more MMCs exist in a subsystem, **no controller supports** Host Memory Buffer (HMPRE field in Identify Controller data structure).

### Reset Behavior
- **Controller Level Reset on MMC**:
  - Deletes all User Data Migration Queues.
  - Stops tracking host memory changes.
- **Controller Level Reset on Migratable Controller**:
  - Removes suspended state (if suspended via Suspend).
  - Retains any persistent controller state committed via Set Controller State.

### Tracking Changes
To capture user data and host memory modifications during migration:
- **Track Send command** (Section 5.2.28): Determines user data changes in namespaces.
- **Track Receive command** (Section 5.2.27): Detects host memory changes from processed commands.

Controllers indicate support:
- **Track User Data Changes Support (TUDCS)** bit set to '1' in **Tracking Attributes (TRATTR)** field (Figure 328).
- **Track Host Memory Changes Support (THMCS)** bit set to '1' in **TRATTR** field.

Migration occurs while the Migratable Controller processes commands in the Source NVM Subsystem, with active data transfer and state synchronization managed by the MMH and MMC.

sections.title: Process_for_Migrating_a_Controller
sections.summary:
# 8.1.13.1 Process for Migrating a Controller

This section outlines a process for migrating a Migratable Controller from a Source NVM Subsystem to a Destination NVM Subsystem, including migration of attached namespaces and host memory modifications. The Migration Manager Host Software (MMHS) performs the migration, using the Migration Manager Controller (MMC) in each subsystem.

### Key Requirements and Definitions

- The Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem must have:
  - **Track User Data Changes Support (TUDCS)** bit set to '1' in the TRATTR field of the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328).
  - **Track Host Memory Changes Support (THMCS)** bit set to '1' in the TRATTR field.
- If namespaces or host memory modifications are not required, their respective steps may be skipped.

---

### Migration Process Steps

1. **Migrate User Data in Attached Namespaces**
   - The MMHS creates a **User Data Migration Queue** in the Source MMC by submitting a **Controller Data Queue** command (Section 5.2.4):
     - Select = 0h (Create Controller Data Queue)
     - Queue Type = User Data Migration Queue
     - Controller Identifier = Migratable Controller in Source
   - Upon success, the completion queue entry contains the **Controller Data Queue Identifier**.
   - The MMHS submits a **Track Send** command (Section 5.2.28) to start logging user data changes:
     - Select = 0h (Log User Data Changes)
     - Logging Action = '1' (start logging)
     - Controller Data Queue Identifier = from previous command
   - The MMHS then begins copying namespaces from the Source to the Destination NVM Subsystem (refer to applicable NVM Command Set specs, e.g., use of **Get LBA Status**).

2. **Track Host Memory Modifications**
   - The MMHS submits a **Track Send** command to the Source MMC:
     - Select = 1h (Track Memory Changes)
     - TACT = '1' (start tracking)
     - Controller Identifier = Migratable Controller in Source
     - Data buffer: **Track Memory Changes data structure** specifying host memory ranges to track
   - On success, the MMHS queries tracked host memory modifications using a **Track Receive** command:
     - Select = 1h (Track Memory Changes)
     - Controller Identifier = Migratable Controller in Source

3. **Suspend Migratable Controller in Source**
   - After copying namespaces, the MMHS suspends the Migratable Controller in the Source by submitting a **Migration Send** command:
     - Select = 0h (Suspend)
     - Suspend Type = 1h (Suspend)
     - Delete User Data Migration Queue = '1' (optional)
     - Controller Identifier = Migratable Controller in Source
   - Before command completion:
     - The Migratable Controller stops fetching commands and completes in-flight commands.
     - The MMC adds an entry to the User Data Migration Queue indicating logging is suspended, and deletes the queue if the delete flag is set.

4. **Finalize User Data Migration**
   - With the controller suspended, the MMHS migrates any remaining user data identified in the User Data Migration Queue.
   - Host memory modifications are handled as reported in prior Track Receive queries.

5. **Obtain Controller State**
   - The MMHS retrieves the controller state of the Migratable Controller in the Source via one or more **Migration Receive** commands:
     - Select = 0h (Get Controller State)
     - Sequence Indicator = proper value
     - Controller Identifier = Migratable Controller in Source
     - Controller State Version Index = index into NVMe Controller State Version list (Figure 345), if NVMe state required
     - Controller State UUID Index = index into Vendor Specific Controller State UUID Supported list (Figure 345), if vendor-specific state required

6. **Transfer Controller State to Destination**
   - The MMHD transfers the controller state to the Destination NVM Subsystem via one or more **Migration Send** commands:
     - Select = 2h (Set Controller State)
     - Sequence Indicator = proper value
     - Controller Identifier = Migratable Controller in Destination
     - Controller State Version Index = index from Destination MMC’s Supported Controller State Formats (if NVMECSS ≠ 0)
     - Controller State UUID Index = index from Vendor Specific list (if VSS ≠ 0)

7. **Resume Controller in Destination**
   - The MMHD resumes the Migratable Controller in the Destination by submitting a **Migration Send** command:
     - Select = 1h (Resume)
     - Controller Identifier = Migratable Controller in Destination

sections.title: Key_Per_I_O
sections.summary:
# 8.1.14 Key_Per_I_O

The **Key Per I/O** capability enables the use of encryption keys injected into an NVM subsystem by a host. Activation, injection, management, and association of keys to encryption key tags are outside this specification's scope. A mechanism is defined in the **TCG Storage Security Subsystem Class: Key Per I/O Specification** using NVMe Admin commands **Security Send** and **Security Receive**. Additional subsystem modifications from activating the Key Per I/O Security Provider are defined in the **TCG Storage Interface Interactions Specification (SIIS)**.

Encryption keys are referenced via the **encryption key tag (KEYTAG)** in the **KEYTAG field** of I/O commands. If an I/O command's **CETYPE** field is set to **KPIOTAG (1h)**, the **CEV field** specifies the encryption key tag to be used for encrypting or decrypting data. Association of key tags to encryption keys is handled by the TCG mechanism and is outside this specification.

The **Key Per I/O Scope (KPIOS)** bit in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328) determines if the capability applies:
- To all read/write commands in all namespaces, or
- Independently to each namespace.

The capability does not affect host access to **RPMBs** or **Boot Partitions**, as these are not managed via namespace-specific I/O commands.

A controller supporting Key Per I/O must set the **KPIOS bit to '1'** in the Identify Controller data structure. A namespace supporting the capability must set the **KPIOSNS bit to '1'** in the I/O Command Set Independent Identify Namespace data structure (Figure 335).

Key Per I/O uses the **Command Extension Type (CETYPE)** and **Command Extension Value (CEV)** fields in all read/write commands. The **CETYPE** values are defined in Table 8.1.14:

| Value | Definition | CEV Field Definition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0h | Reserved | |
| 1h | **Key Per I/O Tag (KPIOTAG):** This command is using the Key Per I/O capability. | **Key Tag (KEYTAG):** Specifies a namespace-specific 16-bit encryption key tag. The same Key Tag value on different namespaces may or may not identify the same encryption key. Refer to the **Maximum Key Tag** field in the Identify Namespace data structure (Figure 335) for supported values. |
| 2h to Eh | Reserved | |
| Fh | Vendor Specific | |

If:
- The Key Per I/O capability is enabled in a namespace (**KPIOENS = 1**),
- An I/O command supports the CETYPE field,
- The CETYPE field is set to a reserved value,
then the controller shall abort the command with **status code: Invalid Field in Command**.

sections.title: Management_Addresses
sections.summary:
# 8.1.15 Management Addresses

The **Management Addresses** capability allows a controller in an NVM subsystem to indicate network addresses of management agents. These agents can reside in:

- NVM subsystems  
- Fabric interface managers  
- Embedded management controllers (e.g., BMC)  
- Hosts  

Each management address is represented as a **URI** (per RFC 3986).

### Address Representation
- **NVM subsystem management agent**:  
  - Indicated in the **Management Address List log page** (Section 5.2.12.1.24)  
  - Uses a **Management Address Descriptor** with **Management Address Type = 1h**

- **Fabric interface manager management agent**:  
  - Indicated in the **Management Address List log page** (Section 5.2.12.1.24)  
  - Uses a **Management Address Descriptor** with **Management Address Type = 2h**

### Address Configuration
- **Embedded management controller (e.g., BMC)**:  
  - Configured via **Embedded Management Controller Address feature** (Section 5.2.26.1.24)  
  - Can only be set by the containing storage system  
  - Security enforced via **Lockdown command** (Section 5.2.15) with:  
    - `OFI` = Feature  
    - `PRHBT` = 1  
    - `IFC` = Admin Submission Queue (00b)

- **Host management agent**:  
  - Configured via **Host Management Agent Address feature** (Section 5.2.26.1.29)  
  - Can only be set by the host  
  - Security enforced via **Lockdown command** (Section 5.2.15) with:  
    - `OFI` = Feature  
    - `PRHBT` = 1  
    - `IFC` = Out-of-band on a Management Endpoint (10b)

sections.title: Namespace_Management
sections.summary:
# 8.1.16 Namespace Management

The **Namespace Management** capability includes the **Namespace Management command** (Section 5.2.21) and the **Namespace Attachment command** (Section 5.2.20). It enables creation/deletion of namespaces and attachment/detachment of controllers, intended for manufacturing or system administrators.

### Requirements (if supported):
- a) Support both the Namespace Management and Namespace Attachment commands  
- b) Set the **NMS bit to '1'** in the **OACS** field (Figure 328)  
- c) Support the **Attached Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event (Figure 154, Section 5.2.26.1.5)  
- d) Should support the **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event  
- e) May support **Namespace Granularity** (per NVM Express NVM Command Set Specification)

### Alternate Support:
A controller may support **Namespace Attachment** without **Namespace Management**:
- a) **Do not** set the NMS bit in OACS  
- b) Should support **Namespace Attribute Change** event

### Namespace States:
- **Detached** namespace → NSID becomes **inactive** (Section 3.2.1.4)  
- **Deleted** namespace → NSID becomes **unallocated** (Section 3.2.1.3)  
- Commands to affected NSID are treated as if issued to an inactive NSID (Figure 92)

### Namespace Creation:
- **Size** depends on requested size, format, and characteristics (e.g., endurance)  
- Controller determines allocated NVM capacity  
- Namespace characteristics and NVM mapping are outside scope

### Capacity Reporting:
- Capacity reporting for NVM subsystem, Domain, Endurance Group, and NVM Set in **section 3.8**  
- For each namespace with formatted storage:
  - NVM Set and Endurance Group reported in **Identify Namespace** data structure  
  - **NVM Set Identifier** (in create operation) determines NVM Set allocation:
    - If **NVM Set ID = 0h** and **Endurance Group ID = 0h** → Controller chooses both  
    - If **NVM Set ID = 0h**, **Endurance Group ID ≠ 0h** → Controller chooses NVM Set in specified Endurance Group  
    - If **NVM Set ID ≠ 0h**, **Endurance Group ID = 0h** → Command **aborted** with **Invalid Field in Command**  
    - If **NVM Set ID ≠ 0h**, **Endurance Group ID ≠ 0h** → Use specified NVM Set **only if it exists** in specified Endurance Group; otherwise, abort with **Invalid Field in Command**

### NVM Capacity Allocation:
- NVM capacity used for a namespace reported in **Identify Namespace** data structure  
- NVM capacity may be **rounded up** to allocation unit boundary  
- Units are reported in **Namespace Granularity List** (if supported)  
- **Example**: Request for 32 logical blocks × 4 KiB = 128 KiB → if allocation unit is 1 MiB, allocated capacity may be 1 MiB  
- **NVM capacity fields may not equal** (logical block size × number of blocks)

### ANA Group Identifier:
- Assignment method is **outside scope**  
- If **ANA Group Identifier = 0h** in Identify Namespace → Controller determines **ANAGRPID** for the namespace

sections.title: Namespace_Management_Examples
sections.summary:
# 8.1.16.1 Namespace Management Examples

## Example: Host Creates a Namespace
1. Host requests **Identify Namespace** data structure with NSID = `FFFFFFFFh` and CNS = `0h` to obtain common namespace capabilities.
2. If supported, host optionally requests **I/O Command Set specific Namespace Management** content (e.g., **Namespace Granularity**).
3. Host determines available resources (e.g., capacity for formatted storage) as defined in **Section 3.8**.
4. Host creates the data structure per **Figure 385**, considering common namespace capabilities and available capacity.
5. Host issues **Namespace Management** command with **Create** operation and the data structure. On success, the new **Namespace Identifier** is returned in **Dword 0** of the completion queue entry. The namespace is **not attached** to any controller.
6. If **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** are enabled on the controller, the host requests **Identify Namespace** data structures for the new namespace upon receiving an **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event.

## Example: Host Attaches a Namespace
1. Host issues **Namespace Attachment** command with **Controller Attach** operation to attach the namespace to one or more controllers.
2. Host receives an **Attached Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event from each controller with **Attached Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled.
3. Host receives an **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event from each controller with **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled.

## Example: Host Detaches a Namespace
1. Host issues **Namespace Attachment** command with **Controller Detach** operation to detach the namespace from one or more controllers.
2. Host receives an **Attached Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event from each controller with **Attached Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled.
3. Host receives an **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event from each controller with **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled.

## Example: Host Deletes a Namespace
1. Host must **detach** the namespace from all controllers.
2. Host issues **Namespace Management** command with **Delete** operation for the specified namespace. On successful completion, the namespace is deleted.
3. If the namespace was attached to any controller(s) when deleted:
   - Host receives an **Attached Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event from each controller with **Attached Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled (as per **Section 8.1.16.2**).
   - Host receives an **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event from each controller with **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled (as per **Section 8.1.16.2**).
4. If the namespace was **not attached** to any controller when deleted, the host receives an **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event from each controller with **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled (as per **Section 8.1.16.2**).

sections.title: Namespace_Deletion_Asynchronous_Event_Reporting
sections.summary:
**8.1.16.2 Namespace Deletion Asynchronous Event Reporting**

- **Trigger**: A delete operation for a namespace, initiated either via a command on the Admin Submission Queue (e.g., Namespace Management or Capacity Management command) or via other methods (e.g., Management Endpoint, outside this specification’s scope).

- **Event Reporting**:
  - For each controller attached to the namespace:
    - If **Attached Namespace Attribute Notices** is enabled (per Figure 409), the controller shall issue an **Attached Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event (excluding the controller processing the delete).
    - If **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** is enabled (per Figure 409), the controller shall issue an **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event (excluding the controller processing the delete).

- **Scope**: Applies regardless of the delete method (Admin Submission Queue or other), but the controller processing the delete **does not** generate the event.

- **Purpose**: Notify controllers of namespace deletion to maintain consistent state, via asynchronous events.

sections.title: Namespace_Management_Considerations_for_Exported_N
sections.summary:
# 8.1.16.3 Namespace Management Considerations for Exported NVM Subsystems

- A host determines support for the **Namespace Attachment command** by reading the **Commands Supported and Effects log page** (Section 5.2.12.1.6).
- The **Namespace Management command** is **not supported** by controllers in an Exported NVM Subsystem.
- If an **Exported Namespace** is **detached from a controller**, its **NSID becomes inactive** (Section 3.2.1.4).
- If an **Underlying Namespace** is **disassociated** from the Exported NVM Subsystem, the corresponding **Exported Namespace NSID becomes unallocated** (Section 3.2.1.3) and is not available to any controller.
- Previously submitted but uncompleted or new commands to a namespace that is:
  - Detached from a controller, or
  - Disassociated from the Exported NVM Subsystem  
  are handled by the controller as if issued to an **inactive NSID** (Section 3.2.1.4, Figure 92).
- If an Exported NVM Subsystem exports an Underlying Namespace that becomes **unavailable** (e.g., detached, deleted) or affected by a **Capacity Management command** (e.g., Endurance Group deletion, NVM Set deletion; Section 8.1.4), then:
  - All previously submitted but uncompleted or new commands to the Exported Namespace are handled as if issued to an inactive NSID.
  - If **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** are enabled, affected controllers report an **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed asynchronous event** to the host (Figure 154).

sections.title: Namespace_Write_Protection
sections.summary:
# 8.1.17 Namespace Write Protection

Namespace Write Protection is an optional configurable controller capability that allows the host to control or query the write protection state of a namespace. Support is reported in the **Namespace Write Protection Capabilities (NWPC)** field in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328).

## Write Protection States (Table 1)

| M/O | State | Definition | Persistent Across |  |
| --- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| | | | **Power Cycles** | **Controller Level Resets** |
| M | No Write Protect | The namespace is not write protected. | Yes | Yes |
| M | Write Protect | The namespace is write protected. | Yes | Yes |
| O | Write Protect Until Power Cycle | The namespace is write protected until the next power cycle. | No | Yes |
| O | Permanent Write Protect | The namespace is permanently write protected. | Yes | Yes |

- **M** = Mandatory if Namespace Write Protection is supported.
- **O** = Optional if Namespace Write Protection is supported.
- The **Write Protect Until Power Cycle** state does not persist across power cycles and is not usable in multi-domain NVM subsystems (due to power cycle requirements).
- All states persist across **Controller Level Resets** except **Write Protect Until Power Cycle**.
- Initial state at namespace creation is **No Write Protect**.

## State Transitions

- Transitions are based on **Set Features commands** unless otherwise specified.
- State transitions are defined in **Figure 670 (Namespace Write Protection State Machine Model)**.

## Write Protection Control

- The **Write Protection Control** field (Figure 690) determines whether the controller processes or aborts **Set Features** commands that transition into **Write Protect Until Power Cycle** or **Permanent Write Protect** states (see section 8.1.23).

> **Note**: Interaction with external write protection systems (e.g., TCG Storage Interface Interactions Specification) is outside the scope of this specification.

sections.title: Namespace_Write_Protection_–_Theory_of_Operation
sections.summary:
# 8.1.17.1 Namespace Write Protection – Theory of Operation

If Namespace Write Protection is supported, the controller must:

- Set **No Write Protect and Write Protect Support** bit to `1` in the **Namespace Write Protection Capabilities (NWPC)** field.
- Set **Write Protect Until Power Cycle Support** bit to `1` in NWPC if supported.
- Set **Permanent Write Protect Support** bit to `1` in NWPC if supported.
- Support the **Namespace Write Protection Config** feature (Section 5.2.26.1.35).
- If **Write Protect Until Power Cycle** or **Permanent Write Protect** is supported, the controller must support the **Write Protection Control** field in the RPMB Device Configuration Block (Section 8.1.23).

The controller must **not** set the **All Media Read-Only** bit to `1` in the **Critical Warning** field (Figure 210) if the read-only state results from:
- A change in namespace write protection state (per the **Namespace Write Protection State Machine**, Figure 670), or
- Autonomous namespace write protection state transitions (e.g., power cycle).

Hosts can query the current namespace write protection state using the **Get Features** command with the **Namespace Write Protection Config Feature Identifier**.

If any controller in the NVM subsystem supports Namespace Write Protection, **all controllers** to which a namespace is attached **must enforce** its write protection state.

sections.title: Namespace_Write_Protection_–_Command_Interactions
sections.summary:
**Summary of Section 8.1.17.2: Namespace Write Protection – Command Interactions**

Unless otherwise specified, commands targeting a write-protected namespace are processed normally if listed in **Table 1**. Commands not in the table and meeting any of the following conditions are aborted with **Namespace Is Write Protected** status (Figure 102):

- (a) Specifies an NSID for a write-protected namespace.  
- (b) Specifies an NSID for a non-write-protected namespace but modifies another write-protected namespace (e.g., Format NVM).  
- (c) Does not specify an NSID and modifies a write-protected namespace (e.g., Sanitize).

**Table 1: Table_8_1_17_2_Namespace_Write_Protection_Command_Interactions**  
| **Admin Command Set** | **NVM Command Set** |
| :--- | :--- |
| Device Self-test | Compare |
| Directive Send ¹ | Dataset Management ¹ |
| Directive Receive ³ | Read |
| Get Features | Reservation Register |
| Get Log Page | Reservation Report |
| Identify | Reservation Acquire |
| Namespace Attachment | Reservation Release |
| Security Receive ¹ | Vendor Specific ¹ |
| Security Send ¹ | Flush ² |
| Set Features | Verify |
| Vendor Specific ¹ | |

**Notes:**  
1. Controller shall fail commands if the specified action attempts to modify the non-volatile storage medium of the specified namespace.  
2. Flush command completes successfully with no effect; volatile write cache data and metadata for the specified namespace are flushed to non-volatile storage during transition to write-protected state (see Section 5.2.26.1.35).  
3. Directive Receive command attempting to allocate stream resources is aborted with **Namespace Is Write Protected** status.

sections.title: Power_Management
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18 Power Management

The power management capability allows the host to manage NVM subsystem power statically or dynamically. Static management involves setting a maximum power allocation and selecting a power state consuming that amount or less. Dynamic management allows the host to modify power states to meet changing power and performance goals, complementing autonomous power and thermal management.

- **Number of Power States Supported (NPSS)**: Indicates the number of supported states, ranging from 1 to 32. Power states are contiguous, starting from zero, with state 0 being the maximum power state.
- **Power State Descriptor**: Each power state has a descriptor in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 329), forming a table (Figure 673). Key fields include:
  - **Maximum Power (MP)**: Sustained maximum power in the state (e.g., 25 W for state 0, 5 W for state 6). Power cannot exceed this level except in non-operational states.
  - **Idle Power (IDLP)**: Typical power consumed over 30 seconds when idle (after 10 seconds of inactivity).
  - **Active Power (ACTP)**: Largest average power over a 10-second window on a workload. Measured from first command submission to last completion. If workload is <10s, average over the period is used. Non-operational states set Active Power fields to 0h.
- **Latency**:
  - **Entry Latency (ENLAT)**: Maximum time (µs) to enter a power state.
  - **Exit Latency (EXLAT)**: Maximum time (µs) to exit a power state.
  - Maximum transition time between two states is the sum of the old state’s exit latency and the new state’s entry latency. Multiple transitions can be initiated without waiting for prior ones to complete.
- **Relative Performance** (in Power State Descriptor):
  - **Relative Read Throughput (RRT)**, **Relative Write Throughput (RWT)**, **Relative Read Latency (RRL)**, **Relative Write Latency (RWL)**: Indicate relative performance. Lower values indicate better performance. Performance values may repeat, skip, or be unordered across states. Relative ordering applies per performance characteristic only.
- **Default Power State**: Implementation-specific and must not exceed the lowest power specified in the applicable form factor. Transport-specific power requirements are defined in the NVM Express Transport specification.

### Table: Power State Characteristics (Table 8.1.18)

| Power State | Maximum Power (MP) | Entry Latency (ENLAT) | Exit Latency (EXLAT) | Relative Read Throughput (RRT) | Relative Read Latency (RRL) | Relative Write Throughput (RWT) | Relative Write Latency (RWL) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | 25 W | 5 µs | 5 µs | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 18 W | 5 µs | 7 µs | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| 2 | 18 W | 5 µs | 8 µs | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 3 | 15 W | 20 µs | 15 µs | 2 | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| 4 | 10 W | 20 µs | 30 µs | 1 | 1 | 3 | 0 |
| 5 | 8 W | 50 µs | 50 µs | 2 | 2 | 4 | 0 |
| 6 | 5 W | 20 µs | 5,000 µs | 4 | 3 | 5 | 1 |

sections.title: Non-Operational_Power_States
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18.1 Non-Operational Power States

A **non-operational power state** is indicated by the **Non-Operational State (NOPS)** field in Figure 329. In this state, the controller allows:

- Property accesses  
- PMR accesses (if any)  
- CMB accesses (if any)  
- Processing of Admin commands and associated background operations (e.g., Device Self-test, Sanitize)  
- Transport-specific accesses defined in the applicable NVMe Transport binding specification  

**Controller behavior in non-operational power states:**

- May exceed the power advertised by the current non-operational power state  
- Shall remain in the current non-operational power state unless:  
  - An I/O command is received  
  - A **Set Features** command with the **Power Management Feature Identifier** is issued  
- Shall **not exceed** the maximum power advertised for the **most recent operational power state**

**HMB access restrictions (per section 5.2.26.2.4):**  
- Prohibits HMB access for **controller-initiated** activity  
- **Does not prohibit** HMB access during **Admin command processing** or **host-initiated background operations**

**Controller-initiated background operations:**  
- May exceed the non-operational power state power **only if**:  
  - **Non-Operational Power State Permissive Mode** is supported and enabled (refer to section 5.2.26.1.10)

**I/O command handling:**  
- No I/O commands are processed in non-operational power states  
- Host must:  
  - Wait for all pending I/O commands to complete  
  - Not submit new I/O commands before the **Set Features** command completes  
- Issuing I/O commands in parallel may cause unexpected power state transitions

**Autonomous transitions:**  
- Regardless of autonomous power state transitions being enabled, the controller must **autonomously transition back** to the **most recent operational power state** to process an I/O command

sections.title: Autonomous_Power_State_Transitions
sections.summary:
### 8.1.18.2 Autonomous Power State Transitions

The controller may support autonomous power state transitions, indicated in the **Identify Controller** data structure (Figure 328). These transitions allow the controller to automatically switch between power states without host software intervention based on predefined conditions.

- **Entry condition**: The controller must be idle (no commands outstanding to any I/O Submission Queue) for a continuous period exceeding the **Idle Time Prior to Transition** time.
- **Constraints**:
  - If a controller operation (e.g., self-test) would cause power consumption to exceed the advertised level for the target non-operational power state, the transition must be blocked.
  - The target power state must be a **non-operational power state**.
  - Non-operational power states may autonomously transition to other non-operational power states.
- **Invalid command handling**: If a **Set Features** command (Feature Identifier = 0Ch) specifies an **operational power state**, the controller shall abort the command with a **status code of Invalid Field in Command**.
- Refer to **Section 8.1.18.1** for additional details.

sections.title: NVM_Subsystem_Workloads
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18.3 NVM Subsystem Workloads

The workload values in this section provide hints for the Power Management Feature (Section 5.2.26.1.2), indicating conditions for active power levels. Active power values in power state descriptors are workload-dependent, and each specified active power must include a corresponding workload.

The workload field defines the conditions for measuring energy values. Workload definitions are provided in Table 1.

#### Table 1: Table_8_1_18_3_NVM_Subsystem_Workloads

| Value | Definition |
| :--- | :--- |
| 000b | **No Workload**: The workload is unknown or not provided. |
| 001b | **Workload 1**: Extended Idle Period with a Burst of Random Writes. Consists of five (5) minutes of idle, followed by thirty-two (32) random write commands of size 1 MiB submitted to a single controller while all other controllers are idle, then thirty (30) seconds of idle. |
| 010b | **Workload 2**: Heavy Sequential Writes. Consists of 80,000 sequential write commands of size 128 KiB submitted to a single controller while all other controllers are idle. Submission queues must be large enough to ensure multiple commands are pending at all times. |
| 011b to 111b | Reserved |

sections.title: Runtime_D3_(RTD3)_Transitions_(PCIe_only)
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18.4 Runtime D3 (RTD3) Transitions (PCIe only)

In Runtime D3 (RTD3), main power is removed from the controller, with auxiliary power optionally provided. RTD3 is used for additional power savings during expected idle periods. RTD3 refers to the D3cold power state in the PCI Express Base Specification, excluding D3hot (where main power is not removed).

To enable host decision-making, the controller reports:
- **RTD3 Entry Latency (RTD3E)**: Time from when `CC.SHN` is set to `01b` by the host until `CSTS.SHST` is set to `10b` by the controller.
- **RTD3 Resume Latency (RTD3R)**: Time from power application until the controller can:
  - Process and complete I/O commands.
  - Access resources (e.g., formatted storage) associated with attached namespaces.

Latency values are based on normal shutdown with optimal settings, assuming host enables, initializes, and sends a 4 KiB read operation.

The host may use the sum of RTD3E and RTD3R to assess if the idle period justifies RTD3 entry.

sections.title: Host_Controlled_Thermal_Management
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18.5 Host Controlled Thermal Management

**Section ID**: 8.1.18.5 | **Page**: 614-616

Host Controlled Thermal Management (HCTM) allows the host to configure a controller to automatically transition between active power states or perform vendor-specific thermal actions to meet host-specified thermal requirements. Support is indicated in the *Host Controlled Thermal Management Attributes* of the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328). Power state transitions are vendor-specific.

The host enables HCTM by setting the **Thermal Management Temperature 1** and/or **Thermal Management Temperature 2** fields (Section 5.2.26.1.9) in a Set Features command to a non-zero value. The supported ranges for these fields are defined in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328).

- **Thermal Management Temperature 1**: If the **Composite Temperature** (Figure 211) is:
  - ≥ this value; and
  - < Thermal Management Temperature 2 (if non-zero),
  then the controller shall transition to lower-power active states or perform vendor-specific thermal actions, minimizing performance impact (e.g., light throttling).

- **Thermal Management Temperature 2**: If the **Composite Temperature** is ≥ this value, the controller shall transition to lower-power states or perform vendor-specific actions **regardless of performance impact** (e.g., heavy throttling).

**Recovery Behavior**:
- If the controller is in a lower-power active state or throttling due to:
  - Temperature ≥ Thermal Management Temperature 1 and < Thermal Management Temperature 2,
  and temperature drops below Thermal Management Temperature 1, the controller shall return to its prior active state or stop vendor-specific thermal actions.

- If the controller is in a lower-power state or throttling due to temperature ≥ Thermal Management Temperature 2, and temperature drops below Thermal Management Temperature 1, the controller shall return to its prior active state or stop thermal actions.

**Hysteresis** for exiting low-power states or thermal actions is vendor-specific.

**Note**: Since HCTM uses Composite Temperature, platform-device interactions may vary even with identical settings. Validation between devices and platforms is required.

The **SMART / Health Information log page** (Section 5.2.12.1.3) contains HCTM-related statistics.

**Figure 675** illustrates example behavior of HCTM.

sections.title: Power_Limit
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18.6 Power_Limit

## Overview
The Power Limit capability enables a host to restrict the maximum power consumption of the NVM subsystem by limiting the power states available to each controller. Controller support is indicated by the Power Limit Support (PLS) bit in the Controller Attributes (CTRATT) field of the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328). The host uses the Set Features and Get Features commands (Section 5.2.26.1.25) to modify and retrieve the power limit, respectively. The power limit prohibits power states where the Maximum Power (MP) value in the Power State Descriptor (PSD) exceeds the specified limit. When a power state is prohibited, its PSD is removed from the Identify Controller data structure. If a prohibited state becomes enabled (e.g., due to a reduced power limit), the PSD is restored. Power states are renumbered contiguously starting at zero, with maximum power monotonically decreasing or equal. The Autonomous Power State Transition (APST) table is updated accordingly, with the Idle Transition Power State field reflecting new indices.

## 8.1.18.6.1 Establishing or Reducing a Power Limit and Prohibiting Power States from Use
If a power limit reduction causes any enabled power state to become prohibited (i.e., power limit < MP in PSD0), the controller performs the following in order:
1. **Retain current data** if no power limit is in force or if a limit was previously removed:
   - Full set of PSD data structures
   - Full set of APST data structure entries (Figure 411)
   - NPSS value
   - Power State attribute values (current, default, saved) of the Power Management feature
2. **Prohibit** all power states with MP > specified power limit
3. **Remove** from Identify Controller data structure and APST:
   - PSD data structures for prohibited states
   - APST entries for prohibited states
4. **Shift remaining PSDs** to lower byte offsets so PSD0 contains the lowest-numbered allowed power state, and update NPSS to reflect remaining count
5. **Shift remaining APST entries** to match PSD shift; first entry aligns with new PS0
6. **Clear to 0**:
   - PSD data structures that no longer contain usable PSDs
   - APST entries that no longer contain usable contents
7. **Update Power Management feature values**:
   - If a power state is not prohibited, change its value to reflect new index from step 4
   - If a power state is prohibited, clear its value to 0h
8. **Update APST feature values**:
   - If a power state is not prohibited, change its value to reflect new index from step 5
   - If a power state is prohibited, clear its value to 0h

Each PSD retained in step 1 and removed in step 3 is a Removed Power State Descriptor (RPSD).

## 8.1.18.6.2 Removing or Increasing a Power Limit and Enabling Power States for Use
If a power limit increase enables any prohibited state (i.e., power limit > MP in PSD0 and at least one RPSD has MP ≤ new limit), the controller:
1. **Restore data** from the most recent instance where RPSD data were created (from step 1 of 8.1.18.6.1):
   - Full set of PSD data structures
   - Full set of APST entries
   - NPSS value
   - Power State attribute values of the Power Management feature
2. **Process the new limit** as in 8.1.18.6.1 **only if** the new power limit < MP in the restored PSD0; otherwise, do nothing in step 2

**Visibility**: Results only become visible outside the controller (e.g., in Identify Controller) after step 2 completes.

**Removing a power limit**: A host sets PLV to 0h in a Set Features command. The controller processes this as setting a limit greater than the maximum MP of all RPSD data structures. The maximum power after removal is determined by MUP (Maximum Unlimited Power) and MUPS (Maximum Unlimited Power Scale) in the Identify Controller data structure.

**Power state retention during limit changes**: While a power limit is in force, if the current or saved Power State attribute changes, the corresponding retained value (current or saved) must be updated to reflect the new PSD index in the RPSD data structures, ensuring subsequent reverts do not cause state changes.

## 8.1.18.6.3 Updating a Power Limit Without Changing Prohibited or Enabled Power States
If a power limit change does not enable prohibited states or prohibit enabled states (i.e., limit ≤ MP of PSD0 and limit ≥ MP of all RPSD data structures), the controller:
- Updates the Power Limit feature attributes
- Does **not** change PSD data structures, NPSS, or Power Management feature attributes

## 8.1.18.6.4 Power Limit Effects Examples
**Case 1 (Set 16W limit)**:
- **Initial state**: 6 power states; default = PS1 (18W); MP values: 25W, 18W, 16W, 15W, 10W, 5W
- **Effect**: PS0, PS1, PS2 (MP > 16W) become prohibited; descriptors removed
- **Shift**: Remaining PSDs (PS3, PS4, PS5) shifted left by 3 slots; renumbered to PS0 (15W), PS1 (10W), PS2 (5W)
- **NPSS**: 6 → 3
- **Default PM state**: Changes to PS0 (now the lowest-index power state)
- **Current PM state**: If originally PS0, PS1, or PS2 → transitions to new PS0; else, remains the same with index decremented by 3

**Case 2 (Increase to 20W limit)**:
- **Initial state**: 3 PSDs (PS0:15W, PS1:10W, PS2:5W) — PS3, PS4, PS5 are RPSDs; NPSS = 3
- **Effect**: PSDs shifted right by 2 slots; PS0 → PS2, PS1 → PS3, PS2 → PS4 (2 empty slots)
- **RPSD restoration**: PS1 (18W), PS2 (18W) restored → renumbered to PS0, PS1; PS0 (25W) remains prohibited
- **NPSS**: 3 → 5
- **Current PM state**: Unchanged, but index increased by 2
- **Default PM state**: Changes to PS0 (position of original PS1)

**Case 3 (Remove 20W limit)**:
- **Initial state**: 6 PSDs (PS0 to PS5); NPSS = 5
- **Effect**: PSDs shifted right by 1 slot; PS0 → PS1, PS1 → PS2, etc. (1 empty slot)
- **Restoration**: Original PSD0 (25W) restored → enabled as PS0
- **NPSS**: 5 → 6

sections.title: Power_Measurement_and_Reporting
sections.summary:
### 8.1.19 Power Measurement and Reporting

Power measurement and reporting is an optional capability enabling the host to obtain interval power measurements from embedded sensors in the NVM subsystem. An **interval power measurement** is the average power over a **one-second interval**, sampled at a rate ≤ the **Interval Power Measurement Sample Rate (IPMSR)** (from the Identify Controller data structure). Measurements are taken over **non-overlapping** one-second intervals and are based on **measured power** unless otherwise specified.

#### Key Requirements:
- Interval power measurements are **not required** during:
  - Power cycles
  - Non-operational power states
  - NVM Subsystem Reset
  - When `CSTS.SHST = 10b` (shutdown complete) across all controllers
- Sets of interval power measurements may be **contiguous** (continuous) or **non-contiguous** due to events like power removal, entering non-operational state, NVM Subsystem Reset, or `CSTS.SHST = 10b`.

#### Reporting Conditions:
- If **Interval Power Measurement (IPM)** or **Operational Lifetime Energy Consumed (OLEC)** are reported in the SMART/Health Information log page, interval power measurements must be collected.
- Collection for **Power Threshold** and **Power Measurement** features depends on their respective capabilities being enabled.
- If any of the following are active:
  - IPM field reported
  - OLEC field reported
  - Power Threshold feature supported
  - Power Measurement capability supported  
  → Then the **IPMSR** field in the Identify Controller data structure must be set to a **non-zero value**.

#### Power Measurement Types (Table 1):
| Value | Definition |
|-------|------------|
| 0h    | NVM subsystem total power |
| 1h–Bh | Reserved |
| Ch–Fh | Vendor Specific |

#### Capabilities and Fields (Table 2):
| Power Measurement and Reporting Capability | Reference Section |
|-------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| Interval Power Measurement (IPM) field in SMART/Health log | 5.2.12.1.3 |
| Operational Lifetime Energy Consumed (OLEC) field in SMART/Health log | 5.2.12.1.3 |
| Power Threshold feature | 5.2.26.1.26 |
| Power Measurement capability | 8.1.19.1 |

#### Power Scale Definitions (Table 3):
| Value | Definition |
|-------|------------|
| 00b   | Reserved |
| 01b   | 0.0001 W |
| 10b   | 0.01 W |
| 11b   | Reserved |

Power scales are defined for:
- Interval Power Scale (IPS) – Figure 158
- Average Interval Power Scale (AIPWRS) – Figure 297
- Maximum Interval Power Scale (MIPWRS) – Figure 297
- Power Scale (PWRS) – Figure 298
- Power Threshold Scale (PTS) – Figure 453

sections.title: Power_Measurement_capability
sections.summary:
# 8.1.19.1 Power Measurement capability

The Power Measurement capability enables a host to control logging of interval power measurements, which are reported as:
- Average of interval power measurements
- Maximum interval power measurement
- Histogram of interval power measurements

**Requirements:**
- If the Power Measurement capability is supported (PMS bit set to '1' in Identify Controller data structure, Figure 328), the controller must support:
  - The Power Measurement feature (Section 5.2.26.1.27)
  - The Power Measurement log page (Section 5.2.12.1.33)

**Control via Set Features Command:**
- Start Power Measurements: Action = 1h
- Stop Power Measurements: 
  - Action = 0h, or
  - Action = 1h with non-zero value in Stop Measurement Time field (Figure 454)

**Stop Measurement Time Constraints:**
- If Stop Measurement Time > Maximum Stop Measurement Time (MSMT) field in Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328), command aborts with Invalid Field in Command status.

**Power Measurement Log Page (Figure 297):**
- **Number of Power Histogram Descriptors Supported (NPHDS):** Maximum number of Power Histogram Descriptors that can be reported.
- **Power Histogram Descriptor Overflow (PHDO) bit:** Set to '1' if:
  - NPHDS ≠ 0
  - Power Measurement Count (PMC) ≠ 0
  - At least one interval power measurement > maximum power in last Power Histogram Descriptor (NPHD-1)
- **Power Measurement Count (PMC):** Incremented for each interval power measurement
- **Power Histogram Bin Count:** Incremented if interval power measurement:
  - ≥ Power Histogram Bin Lower Threshold
  - < (Bin Lower Threshold + Bin Size)
- **Power Histogram Descriptor Overflow Count (PHDOC):** Incremented if interval power measurement > maximum power in last Power Histogram Descriptor (NPHD-1)

**Logging Behavior (when PME = 1):**
- Update:
  - **Average Interval Power:** Average of all interval power measurements
  - **Maximum Interval Power** and **Maximum Interval Power Timestamp** (if supported): Updated when current interval power > existing Maximum Interval Power
- Increment:
  - **PMC**
  - **Power Histogram Bin Count** for the appropriate descriptor
  - **PHDOC** if interval power exceeds maximum power in last Power Histogram Descriptor

sections.summary:
